datasets.name: ego_social
citations: J. McAuley and J. Leskovec. "Learning to Discover Social Circles in Ego Networks." NIPS (2012). arxiv:1210.8182

datasets.name: elec
datasets.description:
Votes in the elections of administrators of the English Wikipedia, collected by J. Leskovec, D. Huttenlocher and J. Kleinberg. In order for a Wikipedia user to become an administrator, a Request for Adminship (RfA) is issued, and the community decides on the promotion by a public discussion or a vote. The data were extracted from the complete dump of the Wikipedia page edit history of 3 January 2008, and comprise 2,794 elections held between 2004 and 2008, of which 1,248 resulted in a promotion. Users may be candidates in more than one election.

Nodes are Wikipedia users that cast a vote, were candidates, or nominated a candidate, and a directed edge $(i,j)$ indicates that user $i$ voted in an election of candidate $j$. Each vote is an edge, so the network can contain parallel edges when a user voted in several elections of the same candidate. Some users voted in their own elections (72 self-loops). The 25 users that only appear as nominators have no edges. Some vote times are invalid (in the years 2061 to 2105), and are kept as they are in the source data. The time zone of the times is not documented; they are interpreted as UTC.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `user_id`: the user ID in the source data.
- (Node) `name`: the user name (lowercased in the source data; in a few names a non-ASCII character is truncated in the source and replaced by U+FFFD).
- (Edge) `vote`: the vote, $+1$ (support), $0$ (neutral) or $-1$ (oppose).
- (Edge) `time`: the time of the vote, in Unix time.
- (Edge) `election`: the number of the election (in the order of the source file, from 0).
- (Edge) `promoted`: whether the election resulted in the promotion of the candidate.
- (Edge) `closed`: the time the election was closed, in Unix time.
- (Edge) `nominator`: the node index of the user that nominated the candidate, or $-1$ if unknown (2,117 elections).
citations: J. Leskovec, D. Huttenlocher, J. Kleinberg, "Signed networks in social media." Proceedings of the SIGCHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI '10), 1361-1370 (2010)

J. Leskovec, D. Huttenlocher, J. Kleinberg, "Predicting positive and negative links in online social networks." Proceedings of the 19th International Conference on World Wide Web (WWW '10), 641-650 (2010)

J. Leskovec, D. Huttenlocher, J. Kleinberg, "Governance in social media: A case study of the Wikipedia promotion process." Proceedings of the International AAAI Conference on Web and Social Media (ICWSM) 4(1), 98-105 (2010)

datasets.name: elite
datasets.description:
A small bipartite network of the affiliations of 20 members of the Chicago corporate elite with 24 organizations in 1962: the boards of 15 corporations, of four cultural and educational institutions (the Art Institute of Chicago, the Museum of Science and Industry, Northwestern University and the University of Chicago) and five social clubs. The data are from Table 1 of Barnes and Burkett (2010), as transcribed in Cory Brunson's bitriad R package (data set `chicago1960s`).

Nodes are persons (identified by surname) and organizations, and an edge connects a person to an organization with which the person is affiliated (as a board member or club member).

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the surname of the person or the name of the organization.
- (Node) `is_organization`: whether the node is an organization.
citations: R. Barnes, T. Burkett, "Structural redundancy and multiplicity in corporate networks." Connections 30(2), 4-20 (2010)

datasets.name: email_company
datasets.description:
A network of the internal email communication among the employees of a mid-sized manufacturing company, over the first nine months of 2010 (from 1 January to 30 September; the first email is of 2 January), with the company's reporting hierarchy, collected by Radosław Michalski and colleagues. Each node is an email account of the company (167 in total), and a directed edge from account A to account B is an email sent by A with B among its recipients, so that an email to several recipients appears as several edges (recipients in To, CC and BCC are not distinguished), and pairs of accounts are connected by several edges (a multigraph). Some emails were sent by an account to itself (51 self-loops). The data give the time of each email in local time, to the second; the time zone is not given, and the times are taken here as local times of Poland (Europe/Warsaw, with daylight saving time), the country of the authors' university (the company's location is not stated). The content of the emails is not included in the data.

The reporting hierarchy gives, for each employee, the employee they report to (their supervisor), without job titles or positions; node 86 is the chief executive officer, who reports to themself. Seven accounts are technical email accounts, not used by employees, and six are accounts of former employees, for which the hierarchy has no supervisor.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `id`: the identifier of the account in the data (1 to 167).
- (Node) `reports_to`: the identifier of the account of the employee's supervisor (-1 for technical accounts and accounts of former employees).
- (Node) `is_technical`: whether the account is a technical email account not used by employees.
- (Node) `is_former_employee`: whether the account is that of a former employee.
- (Edge) `time`: the time of the email (Unix time, from the local time taken as Europe/Warsaw time).
citations: R. Michalski, S. Palus, P. Kazienko, "Matching organizational structure and social network extracted from email communication." Business Information Systems, Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing 87, 197-206 (2011)
M. Nurek, R. Michalski, "Combining Machine Learning and Social Network Analysis to Reveal the Organizational Structures." Applied Sciences 10(5), 1699 (2020)
R. Michalski, "Manufacturing company email metadata and corporate hierarchy." Harvard Dataverse, dataset (2020)

datasets.name: email_enron
datasets.description: An email communication network from the Enron corporation, covering around half a million emails, as compiled by J. Leskovec and collaborators from the Enron email corpus. The corpus consists of the emails of about 150 Enron employees, mostly senior management, which were made public by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission during its investigation of the company's collapse, and were cleaned and released for research by B. Klimt and Y. Yang (CMU). Nodes are email addresses, and an undirected edge connects two addresses if at least one email was sent from one to the other (in either direction). Addresses outside Enron are also present, but only their communication with Enron addresses is observed. Nodes are identified only by numeric identifiers, and the network has no node or edge properties.
citations: B. Klimt and Y. Yang, "The Enron Corpus: A New Dataset for Email Classification Research." Proc. Eur. Conf. Machine Learning (ECML), 217-226 (2004).

datasets.name: email_enron_core
datasets.description:
A bipartite network of Enron employees and the emails they exchanged, constructed by Benson et al. from the Enron email corpus distributed by William Cohen at Carnegie Mellon University. The corpus contains the mailboxes of about 150 Enron employees, mostly senior management, which were made public by the US Federal Energy Regulatory Commission during its investigation of the company. Only the email addresses of a core set of 148 employees are included, and only emails sent by one of them to at least one other of them; recipients outside this set are not represented. Each email node is connected to its sender and to its recipients from the core set (the source data do not distinguish the sender from the recipients). The emails span November 1998 to June 2002. This is the version of the data without restriction on the number of participants (at most 37 per email). 431 emails have a single participant, i.e. an employee who emailed themselves. Five of the 148 addresses do not take part in any email and are not included.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `is_email`: whether the node is an email (otherwise an employee).
- (Node) `name` (employees): the email address of the employee.
- (Node) `time` (emails): the time the email was sent, in Unix time (seconds since 1970-01-01), converted from the millisecond timestamps of the source (the source does not document how the time zones of the original email headers were handled).
citations: A. R. Benson, R. Abebe, M. T. Schaub, A. Jadbabaie, J. Kleinberg, "Simplicial closure and higher-order link prediction." Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 115(48), E11221-E11230 (2018)
B. Klimt, Y. Yang, "The Enron Corpus: A New Dataset for Email Classification Research." Machine Learning: ECML 2004, Lecture Notes in Computer Science 3201, 217-226 (2004)

datasets.name: email_enron_law
datasets.description:
A directed network of email communication built by the Laboratory for Web Algorithmics (LAW) from the Enron email corpus, the partially anonymized collection of email messages of (mostly senior management) employees of the Enron corporation that was made public by the U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission during its investigation of the company. Nodes are correspondents (email addresses, including addresses outside Enron, whose links are only observed through their exchanges with the mailboxes in the corpus), and a directed edge from x to y indicates that y was the recipient of at least one message sent by x. The network has 69,244 nodes and 276,143 edges, including 1,535 self-loops (messages sent to oneself). Nodes are anonymous (no addresses are given), and edges are unweighted.

This version differs in its construction from other networks derived from the same corpus (e.g. the SNAP `email-Enron` network, which is undirected and has 36,692 nodes).
citations: P. Boldi and S. Vigna, "The WebGraph framework I: compression techniques." Proceedings of the 13th International Conference on World Wide Web (WWW 2004), 595-602 (2004).

P. Boldi, M. Rosa, M. Santini, and S. Vigna, "Layered label propagation: a multiresolution coordinate-free ordering for compressing social networks." Proceedings of the 20th International Conference on World Wide Web (WWW 2011), 587-596 (2011).

datasets.name: email_eu
datasets.description: An email network from a large European research institution, compiled by J. Leskovec, J. Kleinberg and C. Faloutsos from anonymized information on all incoming and outgoing email of the institution over a period of 18 months, from October 2003 to May 2005. Nodes are email addresses, and a directed edge $i \to j$ means that address $i$ sent at least one email to address $j$. Since the data contain only emails sent or received by the institution, communication between addresses outside the institution is not observed. Some addresses sent emails to themselves, resulting in self-loops. Nodes are identified only by anonymous numeric identifiers, and the network has no node or edge properties.
citations: Leskovec, J. Kleinberg and C. Faloutsos. "Graph Evolution: Densification and Shrinking Diameters." ACM Transactions on Knowledge Discovery from Data 1(1), article 2 (2007).

datasets.name: email_eu_core
datasets.description:
A bipartite network of the members of a large European research institution and the emails they exchanged, constructed by Benson et al. from the timestamped email records underlying the SNAP `email-Eu-core` network (Leskovec, Kleinberg and Faloutsos; Yin et al.). The records are anonymized (sender, recipient, time) entries, at 1-second resolution, of the emails sent between members of the institution from September 2003 to December 2005 (803 days); messages to or from people outside the institution are not included. Benson et al. reconstructed each email as a group made of a sender and all the recipients that the sender emailed at exactly the same time. In this network each email is a node connected to its sender and recipients (the source data do not distinguish the sender from the recipients). This is the version of the data without restriction on the number of participants (at most 40 per email). 25,755 emails have a single participant, i.e. a member who emailed themselves. Each member belongs to one of 42 departments of the institution, as given by the SNAP department labels.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `is_email`: whether the node is an email (otherwise a member of the institution).
- (Node) `department` (members): the department of the member (anonymized index, from 0 to 41).
- (Node) `snap_id` (members): the node identifier in the SNAP `email-Eu-core` network (0-based; equal to the source's 1-based identifier minus one).
- (Node) `time` (emails): the time the email was sent, in Unix time (seconds since 1970-01-01 UTC).
citations: A. R. Benson, R. Abebe, M. T. Schaub, A. Jadbabaie, J. Kleinberg, "Simplicial closure and higher-order link prediction." Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 115(48), E11221-E11230 (2018)

H. Yin, A. R. Benson, J. Leskovec, D. F. Gleich, "Local Higher-Order Graph Clustering." Proceedings of the 23rd ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining, 555-564 (2017)
J. Leskovec, J. Kleinberg, C. Faloutsos, "Graph evolution: Densification and shrinking diameters." ACM Transactions on Knowledge Discovery from Data 1(1), 2 (2007)

datasets.name: email_eu_core_temporal
datasets.description:
Directed temporal networks of the emails exchanged between members of a large European research institution over 803 days, from the anonymized email records underlying the SNAP `email-Eu-core` network, distributed by SNAP as `email-Eu-core-temporal` (Paranjape, Benson and Leskovec). Messages to or from people outside the institution are not included. Nodes are members of the institution, and an edge $(u, v, t)$ means that member $u$ sent an email to member $v$ at time $t$; an email with several recipients gives one edge per recipient. Repeated emails between the same members are separate edges (a multigraph).

There are five networks:

- `all`: the emails among all 986 members (the largest weakly connected component of the `email-Eu-core` network);
- `dept1`, `dept2`, `dept3`, `dept4`: the emails among the members of four departments of the institution.

The node identifiers differ between the networks, and from those of the `email-Eu-core` network and of the entry `email_eu_core` (the same records, as a bipartite network of emails and members, with the departments of all members), so that the members cannot be matched across them.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `member_id`: the anonymized identifier of the member in the source data.
- (Edge) `time`: the time the email was sent, in seconds since the beginning of the data (the absolute dates are not given).
citations: A. Paranjape, A. R. Benson, and J. Leskovec, "Motifs in Temporal Networks." Proceedings of the Tenth ACM International Conference on Web Search and Data Mining (WSDM), 601-610 (2017).

datasets.name: emp_microbiome
datasets.description:
Bipartite networks of environmental samples and the microbes (bacteria and archaea) found in them, from release 1 of the Earth Microbiome Project (EMP), a collaborative effort that collected and sequenced (16S rRNA gene amplicons, V4 region) about 27,000 samples from 97 studies of all kinds of environments: soils, sediments, fresh and salt water, plants, animal bodies and guts, built environments, etc., with a common protocol, and classified them with the EMP ontology of habitats (EMPO).

Nodes are samples and microbial taxa (sequence variants or OTUs), and an edge connects a sample to each taxon observed in it, with the number of reads of the taxon in the sample as weight. There is one network for each of the published observation tables of the release, which differ in how the reads were grouped into taxa:

- `deblur_90bp`, `deblur_100bp`, `deblur_150bp`: exact sequence variants (sub-OTUs) obtained with Deblur from the reads trimmed to 90, 100 and 150 base pairs (the 150 bp table contains fewer samples, those with longer reads).
- `cr_gg_13_8`, `cr_silva_123`: OTUs of closed-reference picking (97% identity) against the Greengenes 13.8 and SILVA 123 references.
- `or_gg_13_8`: OTUs of open-reference picking against Greengenes 13.8 (without the OTUs found in a single sample).

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `is_sample`: whether the node is a sample (otherwise it is a taxon).
- (Node) `name`: the identifier of the sample (in lower case in `or_gg_13_8`, as given in its table), or of the taxon (the sequence itself for the Deblur tables, the OTU identifier otherwise).
- (Node) `taxonomy`: the taxonomy of the taxon (from kingdom to species, separated by `; `; empty for samples).
- (Node) The sample metadata, all the columns of the mapping file of the release (empty, NaN or false for taxa; strings unless said otherwise):
  - (Node) `barcode_sequence`, `linker_primer_sequence`, `description`, `host_subject_id`: the barcode and primer sequences, the description of the sample and the identifier of its host individual, as given by the study.
  - (Node) `study_id`, `title`, `principal_investigator`, `doi`, `ebi_accession`: the EMP study of the sample, its title, principal investigator, the DOI of its publication, and its accession in the European Nucleotide Archive.
  - (Node) `target_gene`, `target_subfragment`, `pcr_primers`, `illumina_technology`, `extraction_center`, `run_center`, `run_date`, `read_length_bp` (number): the sequencing of the sample.
  - (Node) `sequences_split_libraries`, `observations_closed_ref_greengenes`, `observations_closed_ref_silva`, `observations_open_ref_greengenes`, `observations_deblur_90bp`, `observations_deblur_100bp`, `observations_deblur_150bp` (numbers): the numbers of sequences of the sample after demultiplexing, and in each observation table.
  - (Node) `emp_release1`, `qc_filtered`, `subset_10k`, `subset_5k`, `subset_2k` (booleans): whether the sample is in release 1, whether it passed the quality filters of the EMP, and whether it belongs to the even subsets of 10,000, 5,000 and 2,000 samples used in the paper.
  - (Node) `sample_taxid`, `sample_scientific_name`: the NCBI taxon and name of the kind of sample (e.g. `soil metagenome`).
  - (Node) `host_taxid`, `host_common_name_provided`, `host_common_name`, `host_scientific_name`, `host_superkingdom`, `host_kingdom`, `host_phylum`, `host_class`, `host_order`, `host_family`, `host_genus`, `host_species`: the host of the sample and its taxonomy.
  - (Node) `collection_timestamp`: the date of collection of the sample (as given).
  - (Node) `country`, `latitude_deg`, `longitude_deg`, `depth_m`, `altitude_m`, `elevation_m` (numbers, except the country): the location of the sample (NaN if unknown).
  - (Node) `env_biome`, `env_feature`, `env_material`, `envo_biome_0` ... `envo_biome_5`: the environment of the sample (ENVO terms), and the levels of the hierarchy of its biome.
  - (Node) `empo_0`, `empo_1`, `empo_2`, `empo_3`: the habitat of the sample in the levels of the EMP ontology (e.g. `EMP sample` / `Free-living` / `Saline` / `Water (saline)`).
  - (Node) `adiv_observed_otus`, `adiv_chao1`, `adiv_shannon`, `adiv_faith_pd` (numbers): the alpha diversity of the sample (observed OTUs, Chao1, Shannon, Faith's phylogenetic diversity), as computed by the EMP.
  - (Node) `temperature_deg_c`, `ph`, `salinity_psu`, `oxygen_mg_per_l`, `phosphate_umol_per_l`, `ammonium_umol_per_l`, `nitrate_umol_per_l`, `sulfate_umol_per_l` (numbers): physicochemical measurements of the sample (NaN if not given).
- (Edge) `count`: the number of reads of the taxon in the sample.
citations: L. R. Thompson, J. G. Sanders, D. McDonald, A. Amir, J. Ladau, K. J. Locey, R. J. Prill, A. Tripathi, S. M. Gibbons, G. Ackermann, et al., "A communal catalogue reveals Earth's multiscale microbial diversity." Nature 551, 457-463 (2017)

datasets.name: endow_sites
datasets.description:
Social networks of rural communities studied in the ENDOW project ("Evolutionary and Dynamic Origins of Wealth"), a cross-cultural project that collected comparable data on kinship, cooperation, social support and wealth in more than 20 communities around the world (funded by the US National Science Foundation, award 1743019). The project's own repositories contain only simulated ("faux") data; the networks here are those that the authors of the studies that use ENDOW data (listed on the project's publications page) released openly, one network per community:

- `mosuo_labai` and `mosuo_yongning`: two communities of Mosuo agriculturalists in Yunnan, China, the patrilineal Labai and the matrilineal Yongning (Mattison et al. 2021). Nodes are individuals, and edges are the nominations of the respondents (one per household) for the questions of the survey (the layers): who they borrow money from and lend it to, borrow farm equipment from and lend it to, who helps with the harvest, home repairs, slaughtering, childcare and the preparation of community meals, who pays school fees, with whom the women and the men of the household spend time after dinner, kin relations (`Relations`), influential people outside the community, government and NGO contacts, and who they ride with. Some questions were answered by the respondent on behalf of other household members (e.g. the men's and women's evening company); the edges are as recorded, from the respondent. Two identifiers are corrected as in the authors' code (`YN9076` to `YN2000`, and `YN2016` to `YN2017`).
- `pemba_mitini` and `pemba_mitini_sharing`: the village of Mitini, on the island of Pemba, Zanzibar (Redhead et al. 2023). In `pemba_mitini`, the nodes are the households (`pesu...`), and the layers `work_women` and `work_men` (with whom the women and the men commonly work) and `friends_women` and `friends_men` (with whom they spend free time) go from the nominating household to the nominated one. In `pemba_mitini_sharing`, the nodes are the "sharing units" of the food sharing data (`pessu...`; some of them merge two households, e.g. `pessu101108` for households 101 and 108), with the layers `food_help_received` (which households commonly help you with food) and `food_given` (to which households do you often give food), from the nominating unit to the nominated one, and `relatedness`, the mean genetic relatedness between the units (undirected, given as weighted edges in one direction); the household attributes are given for the units that are single households. The two networks are kept apart because their nodes differ.
- `matlab_bangladesh`: the households of a village in Matlab, Bangladesh (Hwang et al. 2026). Layers: `financial` (cash), `material` and `labor` support, as recorded (the authors note that the direction of the `labor` edges is the reverse of the flow of the help), and `kinship` between households.
- `shodagor`: Shodagor women (a community of semi-nomadic traders and fishers in Bangladesh) and their partners in childcare and work, as recorded (Starkweather et al. 2022), with `relatedness` (weighted) edges.
- `colombia`: friendship nominations in rural Colombia (Afrocolombian, Emberá and Mestizo individuals), from the data published with the STRAND package by C. T. Ross (`Colombia_Data`, a sample of 149 individuals of the study of Redhead, Dalla Ragione and Ross 2023), with `relatedness` (weighted) edges.

Several other studies on the publications page were checked: their network data are not openly available (only on request, e.g. the South Indian Tamil data of E. A. Power, the fishing communities of Barnes et al. 2020; or not released), or the studies do not concern networks. Physical distances between households, given as matrices, are not included.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the identifier of the individual or household in the data.
- (Edge) `layer`: the question or relation of the edge (see above).
- (Edge) `weight`: the relatedness for `relatedness` edges, and 1 for the others.
- (Node) Other properties, depending on the community, as given in the data:
  - (Node) `household`, `relationship_to_head`, `birth_year`, `age`, `gender`, `marital_status`, `years_of_education`, `occupation`, `group`, `status`, `wealth`, `ability_to_work`, `location` (Mosuo): as given in the data.
  - (Node) `wives` (Pemba): number of wives of the household in 2018.
  - (Node) `wealth` (Pemba): direct material wealth.
  - (Node) `log_wealth` (Pemba): as given in the data.
  - (Node) `status` (Pemba): a member holds a position.
  - (Node) `khazi` (Pemba): a member belongs to the labor cooperative.
  - (Node) `household_size`, `head_age`, `status`, `salaried`, `land`, `wealth_usd` (Matlab): as given in the data.
  - (Node) `household` (Shodagor): as given in the data.
  - (Node) `ethnicity`, `sex`, `age`, `bmi`, `pa` (Colombia): as given in the data.
citations: S. M. Mattison, N. G. MacLaren, R. Liu, A. Z. Reynolds, G. D. Baca, P. M. Mattison, M. Zhang, C.-Y. Sum, M. K. Shenk, T. Blumenfield, C. von Rueden and K. Wander, "Gender Differences in Social Networks Based on Prevailing Kinship Norms in the Mosuo of China." Social Sciences 10(7), 253 (2021)
D. Redhead, E. Maliti, J. B. Andrews and M. Borgerhoff Mulder, "The interdependence of relational and material wealth inequality in Pemba, Zanzibar." Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B 378, 20220288 (2023)

datasets.name: enron_emails_cmu
datasets.description:
A bipartite network of email addresses and the emails in the Enron email corpus, as distributed by William Cohen at Carnegie Mellon University (version of May 7, 2015). The corpus contains about 0.5 million messages from the mailboxes of about 150 Enron employees, mostly senior management, organized into folders. The messages were made public by the US Federal Energy Regulatory Commission during its investigation of the company, and were prepared by the CALO project, with integrity problems corrected at SRI; attachments are not included, and some messages were deleted at the request of affected employees. Invalid recipient addresses were converted to the form user@enron.com where possible, and to no_address@enron.com when no recipient was specified. Since the same email is often stored in several folders and mailboxes, the messages were deduplicated: messages with identical date, sender, recipients, subject and body are considered the same email. Each email is connected to its sender and to all the addresses in its To, Cc and Bcc header fields, which include addresses outside Enron. Almost all emails are dated between 1999 and 2002; 483 have dates before 1998 or after 2002 (292 of them in 1980), which are mostly invalid. Messages without any sender or recipient address are not included.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `is_email`: whether the node is an email (otherwise an email address).
- (Node) `name` (addresses): the email address (in lower case).
- (Node) `time` (emails): the date of the email from its Date header field, in Unix time (seconds since 1970-01-01 UTC; -1 if missing or invalid).
- (Edge) `field`: the header field in which the address appears: `from` (the sender), `to`, `cc` or `bcc`. If an address appears in more than one field of the same email, only the first of these is used, in this order. In this corpus every address in a Bcc field is also in the Cc field of the same message, so no edge has the value `bcc`.
citations: B. Klimt, Y. Yang, "The Enron Corpus: A New Dataset for Email Classification Research." Machine Learning: ECML 2004, Lecture Notes in Computer Science 3201, 217-226 (2004)

datasets.name: enron_priebe
datasets.description:
Directed temporal network of emails among 184 email addresses of the Enron email corpus, as prepared by C. E. Priebe, J. M. Conroy, D. J. Marchette and Y. Park for their study of anomaly detection with scan statistics, in the version distributed by the R package networkDynamicData. The Enron corpus contains about 0.5 million messages from the mailboxes of about 150 Enron employees (mostly senior management, but also energy traders, executive assistants, etc.), which were made public by the US Federal Energy Regulatory Commission during its investigation of the company, and later distributed by William Cohen at Carnegie Mellon University. Priebe et al. obtained 184 unique addresses from the "From" line of the emails in the "Sent" folders, after manually removing addresses clearly not associated with the 150 users. Nodes are these addresses, and each directed edge is an email from the source to the target, with its time; an email to several recipients corresponds to several edges with the same time, and repeated edges between the same pair of addresses correspond to different emails. There are 3,129 distinct ordered pairs of addresses (including 119 self-loops, i.e. emails sent to oneself), and 38,184 email edges. Some of the timestamps are clearly invalid: 53 email edges have the placeholder time 315522000 (1979-12-31), and Priebe et al. restrict their analyses to the 189 weeks from 1998 to 2002; the observation period declared in the data is from 1998-11-13 to 2002-06-21. No email contents are included.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `email_id`: the address of the employee without the "@enron.com" part.
- (Node) `name`: the name of the person associated with the address.
- (Node) `role`: the role of the person (e.g. "Employee", "Vice President", "Director", "Trader").
- (Node) `dept`: the department or subsidiary of the person. The names, roles and departments are missing (empty) or redacted for some or many nodes.
- (Edge) `time`: the time of the email, in Unix time (seconds since 1970-01-01).
- (Edge) `to`, `cc`, `bcc`: binary flags of the email as given by the source data, without documentation (the large majority of the edges have only `cc` set, and nearly all the others have both `to` and `bcc` set, so that the flags may not be encoded as their names suggest).
- (Edge) `count`: an integer given for each email by the source data, also without documentation (possibly the number of copies of the email record in the corpus).
citations: C. E. Priebe, J. M. Conroy, D. J. Marchette, Y. Park, "Scan Statistics on Enron Graphs." Computational and Mathematical Organization Theory 11(3), 229-247 (2005)
S. Bender-deMoll et al., "networkDynamicData: Dynamic (Longitudinal) Network Datasets." R package (2016)

datasets.name: epinions
datasets.description:
The "extended Epinions dataset", which the staff of the consumer review site Epinions.com gave to Paolo Massa, and which he distributed on the TrustLet wiki: the helpfulness ratings that the users gave to the reviews and essays (articles) written by other users, and the trust and distrust statements among the users, including the distrust statements, which the site did not show publicly. Users and articles are identified by anonymized numeric ids. The files are obtained from a copy of the dataset on Kaggle (the TrustLet site no longer exists).

- `ratings`: a bipartite network of the users and the articles they rated. Nodes are the users who rated some article, and the rated articles (users and articles have separate id spaces), and an edge connects a user to an article they rated. The rated objects are articles, not products: each rating states how helpful a user found an article of another user, on a scale of 1 ("not helpful") to 5 ("most helpful"). The data contain also 6 as rating value (in about 0.7% of the ratings), which the original documentation does not mention (the Kaggle copy says to treat it as 5); the values are kept as they are. The creation dates of the ratings range from 10 January 2001 to May 2002, but about 90% of the ratings bear the date of 10 January 2001, which is apparently the earliest date recorded (Epinions was founded in 1999), so that the dates of the earlier ratings are not known. The file of the ratings ends in the middle of its last line, without the category of that rating (and possibly cut short at the source: the copies of the file on TrustLet and on Kaggle are the same); that rating is kept, with the category -1. The authors and subjects of the articles are given for the articles in the file `mc.txt` of the dataset.
- `trust`: a directed signed network of the trust and distrust statements among the users (717,667 trusts and 123,705 distrusts), with their dates, from January 2001 to August 2003. Nodes are the users making or receiving some statement (in the same id space as the users of `ratings` and the authors of the articles), and a directed edge from user A to user B is a statement of A about B (573 users made a statement about themselves). These are the same data as the network `epinions` of the entry `signed_social_media` (from SNAP, with the same numbers of statements and of users, 131,828), here with the original user ids and the dates.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `is_user` (`ratings`): whether the node is a user (otherwise an article).
- (Node) `id` (`ratings`): the anonymized id of the user or article.
- (Node) `author_id` (`ratings`): the id of the user who wrote the article (-1 for users, and for the articles not listed in `mc.txt`).
- (Node) `subject_id` (`ratings`): the id of the subject the article is about (-1 for users, for the articles not listed in `mc.txt`, and for the 341 articles of `mc.txt` without a subject).
- (Edge) `rating` (`ratings`): the rating value (1 to 5, or the undocumented value 6).
- (Edge) `status` (`ratings`): the display status of the rating (1 if the user chose not to show their name next to the rating, 0 otherwise).
- (Edge) `time` (`ratings`): the date the article was first rated by the user (Unix time, at 00:00 UTC of that date).
- (Edge) `last_modified` (`ratings`): the date the rating was last modified (Unix time, at 00:00 UTC; -1 if not given).
- (Edge) `type` (`ratings`): the type of the rated object (1 or 2; the meaning of the values is not documented).
- (Edge) `vertical_id` (`ratings`): the id of the category ("vertical") of the article (-1 for about 7% of the ratings, which the documentation does not explain, and for the incomplete last rating).
- (Node) `id` (`trust`): the anonymized id of the user.
- (Edge) `sign` (`trust`): +1 for trust and -1 for distrust.
- (Edge) `time` (`trust`): the date of the statement (Unix time, at 00:00 UTC of that date).
citations: P. Massa, P. Avesani, "Controversial users demand local trust metrics: An experimental study on Epinions.com community." Proceedings of the 20th National Conference on Artificial Intelligence (AAAI-05), 121-126 (2005)

M. R. Hamedani, I. Ali, J. Hong, S.-W. Kim, "TrustRec: An effective approach to exploit implicit trust and distrust relationships along with explicit ones for accurate recommendations." Computer Science and Information Systems 18(1), 93-114 (2021)

datasets.name: epinions_massa
datasets.description:
The "downloaded Epinions dataset" of Paolo Massa, collected in a 5-week crawl of the consumer review site Epinions.com in November and December 2003, and distributed on the TrustLet wiki: the ratings that the users gave to products (items) when reviewing them, and the trust statements among the users (their "web of trust"). Users and items are identified by anonymized numeric ids, from 1 to 49,289 for the users (the documentation gives 49,290 users, but no id above 49,289 appears in the files) and from 1 to 139,738 for the items. The distrust statements (the "block list") are not included, since the site kept them private.

- `ratings`: a bipartite network of the users and the items, with 664,824 ratings (no pair of user and item is repeated). An edge connects a user to an item they rated, on a scale of 1 to 5. All the users of the dataset are included, also the 9,126 who rated no item (but appear in the trust statements), so that the user nodes are the same as in `trust`.
- `trust`: a directed network of the 487,183 trust statements among the users (the documentation gives 487,181), where an edge from user A to user B means that A trusts B. All the users are included, also those making or receiving no statement; 181 users trust themselves.

Other Epinions data in the repository: `epinions` is the larger dataset that the Epinions staff gave to Massa (2001-2003), with the helpfulness ratings of the reviews (not of the products), and the trust and distrust statements with their dates; `epinions_trust` is the trust network collected by Richardson, Agrawal and Domingos in 2003; and the network `epinions` of `signed_social_media` is the same trust and distrust network as in `epinions`, without the dates. The user ids differ between these datasets.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `is_user` (`ratings`): whether the node is a user (otherwise an item).
- (Node) `id` (`ratings`): the id of the user or item.
- (Edge) `rating` (`ratings`): the rating (1 to 5).
- (Node) `id` (`trust`): the id of the user.
citations: P. Massa, P. Avesani, "Trust-aware recommender systems." Proceedings of the 2007 ACM Conference on Recommender Systems (RecSys), 17-24 (2007)

datasets.name: epinions_trust
datasets.description: A who-trusts-whom network of the users of Epinions.com, a general consumer review website, collected by M. Richardson, R. Agrawal and P. Domingos. Members of the site could declare whether they "trust" other members; these trust relationships form the site's "Web of Trust", which was combined with review ratings to determine which reviews were shown to each user. Nodes are users, and a directed edge $i \to j$ means that user $i$ trusts user $j$. Users are identified only by anonymous numeric identifiers, stored in the node property `name`, and the network has no other node or edge properties.
citations: M. Richardson, R. Agrawal and P. Domingos. "Trust Management for the Semantic Web." ISWC, 351-368 (2003).

datasets.name: erc20_ethereum
datasets.description:
Networks of transfers of ERC20 tokens between addresses of the Ethereum blockchain, extracted from the blockchain and distributed by SNAP as part of the Chartalist collection of blockchain data sets (C. G. Akcora, M. Kantarcioglu, Y. R. Gel, F. Victor and collaborators). Nodes are Ethereum addresses (externally owned accounts, controlled by people or organizations, or smart contracts), and an edge $u \to v$ is a transfer of a quantity of a token from address $u$ to address $v$. Each transfer is a separate edge (a multigraph). The addresses are not anonymized, and can be looked up in block explorers. There are two data sets:

- `stablecoins`: the transfers of the five largest stablecoins by market capitalization, tokens meant to keep a fixed price of 1 USD (USDT, USDC, DAI, UST and PAX), and of Wrapped LUNA (WLUNA), around the crash of the Terra (LUNA) ecosystem in May 2022, when UST lost its peg. The network spans the blocks 14,500,001 to 15,872,937 (1 April to 1 November 2022), with 36.7 million transfers. The data come in three versions, each spanning a longer period than the previous one; since the two shorter versions are contiguous parts of the longest one (from 28 April 2022), only the longest is included. The addresses of the Alphacore of the network (a core decomposition) are labeled by their kind (e.g. decentralized exchanges such as Uniswap).
- Exchange tokens (`exchanges`): the transfers of 28 of the largest ERC20 tokens (TUSD, BAT, MANA, MGC, BNT, HEX, AMB, LINK, DAI, HT, AZ, LAMB, SAI, EGT, MXM, USDP, MKR, USDC, NPXS, STORJ, BNB, EBK, WETH, KICK, OMG, KNC, ZRX and ENJ) between 16 October 2018 and 4 May 2020, for the study of the classification of exchange addresses with the Alphacore decomposition. The addresses of 149 centralized and decentralized exchanges (296 addresses), from the labels of the block explorer Etherscan.io in May 2020, are labeled. The token of each transfer is given by its contract address; the data do not give which of the token names corresponds to which address.

The price series of the stablecoins and the list of events of the crash, which are provided with the stablecoin data, are not included. The transaction hashes of the transfers of the exchange tokens are also left out (the transfers are identified by their block and log index).

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `address`: the Ethereum address.
- (Node) `label`, `label_name` and `label_asset` (`stablecoins`): the label of the address in the Alphacore of the stablecoin network (e.g. "uniswap"), the name of the labeled entity (e.g. "Uniswap V3") and the asset (e.g. "DAI-FRAX"), if any.
- (Edge) `time` (`stablecoins`): the time of the block of the transfer, in Unix time.
- (Edge) `block` (`stablecoins`): the block number.
- (Edge) `tx_index` (`stablecoins`): the index of the transaction in the block.
- (Edge) `token` (`stablecoins`): the token transferred, as an index into the graph property `tokens` (0: USDT, 1: USDC, 2: DAI, 3: UST, 4: PAX, 5: WLUNA, by their contract addresses, see below).
- (Edge) `value` (`stablecoins`): the quantity transferred, in units of the token.
- (Node) `exchange_type` (`exchanges`): "cex" for centralized and "dex" for decentralized exchanges, if labeled.
- (Node) `exchange_name` (`exchanges`): the name of the exchange.
- (Edge) `block` (`exchanges`): the block number.
- (Edge) `log_index` (`exchanges`): the index of the transfer event in the block.
- (Edge) `token` (`exchanges`): the token transferred, as an index into the graph property `tokens`.
- (Edge) `value` (`exchanges`): the quantity transferred, in the smallest units of the token (as a floating-point number, which may round large integer values).
- (Graph) `tokens`: the contract addresses of the tokens.
citations: K. Shamsi, F. Victor, M. Kantarcioglu, Y. R. Gel, and C. G. Akcora, "Chartalist: Labeled Graph Datasets for UTXO and Account-based Blockchains." Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 35 (NeurIPS 2022), Datasets and Benchmarks Track (2022).

F. Victor, C. G. Akcora, Y. R. Gel, and M. Kantarcioglu, "Alphacore: Data Depth based Core Decomposition." Proceedings of the 27th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery & Data Mining, 1625-1633 (2021).

datasets.name: erdos_collaboration
datasets.description:
Networks of the mathematicians with Erdős number 1 or 2, i.e. the co-authors of Paul Erdős, and the co-authors of these, from the data of the Erdős Number Project of J. W. Grossman, as converted to Pajek networks by V. Batagelj and A. Mrvar, in four versions of the data: `erdos97`, `erdos98`, `erdos99` (from 1997, 1998 and 1999) and `erdos02` (from 2002). Each node is a mathematician, and an undirected edge connects two of them if they wrote a paper together. The data list the co-authors of the people with Erdős number 1 only, so that the edges join people with Erdős number 1, or people with Erdős numbers 1 and 2; there are no edges between people with Erdős number 2. Paul Erdős himself (and his edges to his co-authors) is included only in `erdos02`.

Batagelj and Mrvar also distribute the networks of the people with Erdős number 1 for 1997 to 1999 (e.g. `ERDOS971.NET`); they are not included as separate networks, since they are the subgraphs of the full networks induced by these people.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the name of the mathematician (in upper case, except in `erdos97` and for a few names of `erdos02`).
- (Node) `erdos_number`: the Erdős number of the mathematician (0 for Paul Erdős, 1 or 2 otherwise). For `erdos97` to `erdos99` they are given by the partitions distributed with the networks; for `erdos02` they follow from the network.
citations: V. Batagelj, A. Mrvar, "Some analyses of Erdős collaboration graph." Social Networks 22(2), 173-186 (2000)
J. W. Grossman, P. D. F. Ion, "On a portion of the well-known collaboration graph." Congressus Numerantium 108, 129-131 (1995)

datasets.name: escorts
datasets.description:
A bipartite network of sex buyers and escorts (sex sellers) in Brazil, compiled by L. E. C. Rocha, F. Liljeros and P. Holme from a Brazilian online community where sex buyers post reviews of their encounters with escorts. The data cover the forum's activity from its start in September 2002 to October 2008. Nodes are 10,106 buyers (all male) and 6,624 escorts (all female), and an undirected edge connects a buyer to an escort for each post in which the buyer reports a sexual encounter with her; repeated encounters result in parallel edges. Edges are timestamped by the date of the post.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `is_male`: whether the node is a buyer (male) or an escort (female).
- (Edge) `time`: the date of the post, in days since the beginning of the data.
- (Edge) `rating`: the grade given by the buyer to the escort (-1: bad, 0: neutral, +1: good).
- (Edge) `anal`, `oral` and `kiss`: answers reported in the post to the questions "anal sex with/without condom?", "oral sex with condom?" and "mouth kiss?", respectively (+1: yes, -1: no, 0: information not available).
citations: L. Rocha, F. Liljeros, & P. Holme. "Simulated epidemics in an empirical spatiotemporal network of 50,185 sexual contacts." PLoS Comput Biol, 7(3). (2011).

datasets.name: estonia_company_ownership
datasets.description:
Networks of the ownership and management of the legal entities of Estonia (companies, sole proprietors, non-profit associations, foundations, apartment associations, state and municipal agencies, ...), from the open data of the Estonian e-Business Register (e-äriregister), kept by the Centre of Registers and Information Systems (RIK). The data are those in force on the download date (31 October 2026): the register publishes only the current state, and its files are replaced daily (ended relations are not included).

There are four networks, in which a directed edge goes from a person (natural or legal) to the legal entity:

- `shareholders`: the shareholders of the private limited companies (osaühing), with their shares (`osanikud`).
- `officers`: the persons entered on the registry card of the legal entity (`kaardile kantud isikud`): the members of the management board, sole proprietors, general and limited partners, liquidators, procurators, contact persons, keepers of the share register, etc.
- `other_roles`: the persons related to the legal entity who are not entered on its registry card (`kandevälised isikud`): founders, members of the supervisory board, auditors, shareholders of public limited companies, members of bankruptcy committees, etc.
- `beneficial_owners`: the beneficial owners (natural persons who ultimately own or control the legal entity), with the way in which they exercise control (`kasusaajad`).

The legal entities are identified by their registry code, and described by the general data of the register (`lihtandmed`: legal form, status, address, VAT number). The persons that are Estonian legal entities are the same nodes as the legal entities themselves, so that the networks include chains of ownership and control between companies. The natural persons with an Estonian personal identification code are identified by a pseudonymous hash of it given by the register (the same in all files), so that they are identified across companies and networks. The natural persons without an Estonian code (foreigners) are only given by name and (mostly) date of birth: they are merged by name and date of birth together. The foreign legal entities are identified by their name, their foreign registry code and its country. Only the legal entities that take part in some edge are included. The memberships of building associations (given on the registry cards, without members) and the texts of the rules of representation are not included.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `kind`: `legal_entity` (an Estonian legal entity, in the register), `foreign_entity`, `natural_person`.
- (Node) `name`: the name of the legal entity, or of the person (first name and surname).
- (Node) `regcode` (Estonian legal entities): the registry code (empty for the others).
- (Node) `person_hash` (natural persons): the pseudonymous hash of the Estonian personal identification code (empty if none).
- (Node) `birth_date` (natural persons without Estonian code): the date of birth (`YYYY-MM-DD`, empty if not given).
- (Node) `foreign_code`, `foreign_code_country` (foreign legal entities): the foreign registry code and its country.
- (Node) `country`: the country of the address of the person (as first found; empty if not given).
- (Node) `legal_form`, `legal_form_subtype` (Estonian legal entities): the legal form (e.g. `Osaühing`, private limited company; `Korteriühistu`, apartment association) and its subtype.
- (Node) `status` (Estonian legal entities): the status (`Registrisse kantud`, entered in the register; `Likvideerimisel`, in liquidation; `Pankrotis`, in bankruptcy).
- (Node) `first_entry_date` (Estonian legal entities): the date of the first entry in the register (`YYYY-MM-DD`).
- (Node) `vat_number`, `address`, `postal_code`, `ehak_code` (Estonian legal entities): the VAT number, the normalized address, its postal code and the code of its administrative unit (EHAK).
- (Edge) `record_id` (all networks): the id of the entry in the register.
- (Edge) `start_date` (all networks): the date since which the relation holds (`YYYY-MM-DD`).
- (Edge) `share_percent` (`shareholders`): the percentage of the share capital, NaN if not given.
- (Edge) `share_amount` and `share_currency` (`shareholders`): the nominal value of the share.
- (Edge) `ownership` (`shareholders`): `Ainuomand` sole ownership, `Ühisomand` joint ownership, `Kaasomand` co-ownership.
- (Edge) `ownership_group` (`shareholders`): the id of the group of the joint owners of a share, -1 if none.
- (Edge) `role` and `role_code` (`officers` and `other_roles`): the role (e.g. `Juhatuse liige`/`JUHL`, member of the management board; `Asutaja`/`A`, founder; `Nõukogu liige`, member of the supervisory board).
- (Edge) `mandate_end` (`officers` and `other_roles`): the date of expiry of the mandate, if given.
- (Edge) `card_type` (`officers`): the kind of registry card: `R` commercial register, `MTÜ` non-profit associations, `SA` foundations, `KÜ` apartment associations, `G` state and municipal agencies, ...
- (Edge) `contribution` and `contribution_currency` (`officers`): the contribution of general partners, NaN if not given.
- (Edge) `share_amount`, `share_currency` and `ownership` (`other_roles`): as for `shareholders` (for founders and shareholders; NaN or empty otherwise).
- (Edge) `control` and `control_code` (`beneficial_owners`): the way the control is exercised, e.g. `otsene osalus`/`O` direct shareholding, `kaudne osalus` indirect shareholding, membership of the management board.
- (Edge) `discrepancy` (`beneficial_owners`): whether a notice of discrepancy about the data was filed.
citations: Centre of Registers and Information Systems (RIK), "e-Business Register open data." (2026)

datasets.name: eu_airlines
datasets.description:
A multiplex network of the routes operated by 37 airlines between European airports. Nodes are airports, and an undirected edge in layer $\ell$ connects two airports if airline $\ell$ operated a flight between them. The data were compiled by A. Cardillo and collaborators from the complete list of commercial flights operating under Instrument Flight Rules (IFR) between European airports on a single day (1 June 2011), obtained from EUROCONTROL (via the ComplexWorld Network / SESAR Work Package E). Only the 37 airlines whose number of destinations exceeds the average (32) were kept; they include major carriers (e.g. Lufthansa, Air France), low-cost carriers (e.g. Ryanair, Easyjet), and a few cargo and business-aviation operators (e.g. TNT Airways, Netjets). The edges are unweighted, and the same pair of airports may be connected in several layers.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `name` and `nodeLabel`: the ICAO code of the airport (two airports have placeholder codes `XXXX` and `YYYY`).
- (Node) `nodeLong` and `nodeLat`: longitude and latitude of the airport, in degrees (0 for the two airports with placeholder codes).
- (Edge) `layer` (edges): the airline (layer) operating the route, numbered 1 to 37; the graph property `layer_key` maps these numbers to airline names.
- (Edge) `weight` (edges): always 1.
citations: Alessio Cardillo, Jesús Gómez-Gardenes, Massimiliano Zanin, Miguel Romance, David Papo, Francisco del Pozo and Stefano Boccaletti. "Emergence of network features from multiplexity." Scientific Reports 3, Article number: 1344 doi:10.1038/srep01344

datasets.name: eu_copatenting
datasets.description:
A bipartite network of institutions and the patents they filed, built by D. Vasques Filho and D. R. J. O'Neale from about 2.8 million patents recorded by the European Patent Office (EPO), to study the co-patenting (R&D collaboration) network among institutions, which is its one-mode projection onto the institutions. Nodes are institutions (companies, universities, research institutes, and other patent applicants) and patents, and an edge connects an institution to a patent filed by it; patents filed jointly by several institutions thus connect them. The network has 313,767 institutions, 2,784,313 patents and 2,970,404 edges (there are no multiple edges). Most patents have a single applicant institution.

Vertex properties: `is_patent`, which marks the patents (the remaining nodes are institutions); `institution_id`, the numeric identifier of the institution in the data (-1 for patents); `country`, the two-letter country code of the institution (empty for patents); `patent_number`, the EPO publication number of the patent (empty for institutions); `year`, the year of the patent, between 1978 and 2015 (-1 for institutions).
citations: D. Vasques Filho and D. R. J. O'Neale, "The role of bipartite structure in R&D collaboration networks." Journal of Complex Networks 8(4), cnaa016 (2020).

datasets.name: eu_procurements
datasets.description:
Networks of public procurement contracts in 26 European countries (25 EU member states and Norway) from 2008 to 2016. The data were collected by J. Wachs, M. Fazekas and J. Kertész from Tenders Electronic Daily (TED), the official EU portal where all contracts above an estimated value of 5.2 million Euro (works) or 135 thousand Euro (services and supplies) must be published. Contracts from Luxembourg, Croatia and EU institutions were excluded. The identities of issuers and winners were deduplicated algorithmically per country, using string similarity and clustering with the Dedupe software. The entry contains two kinds of networks built from these data, and a third kind from the later data of OpenTender:

- `contracts`: a bipartite multigraph of all contracts, in which one set of nodes are issuers (buyers: public institutions such as ministries, hospitals or city halls), the other are winners (suppliers, generally private firms), and each edge is a single awarded contract, so that two nodes may be connected by many edges.
- 234 networks of the annual national procurement markets of each country and year, named by the two-letter country code and the year (e.g. `HU_2012`), published separately by the authors. Each is a bipartite graph between issuers and winners, in which an edge connects an issuer and a winner if at least one contract was awarded between them in that year. Their node identifiers are consistent across years within a country, but have been randomly generated and do not correspond to any official identifiers, nor to those of the `contracts` network.
- 36 networks of the procurement data of OpenTender (opentender.eu), the platform of the Government Transparency Institute (successor of the DIGIWHIST project, in which the data above were collected), which collects and cleans the contracting data of TED and of the national procurement portals (thus also contracts below the EU thresholds) of 35 jurisdictions, from 2004 to 2025 (most from 2006 to 2024), as republished in the Open Contracting Data Standard (OCDS) by the OCP Data Registry of the Open Contracting Partnership (retrieved by the registry in June 2026, January 2026 for Poland and April 2026 for the EU institutions). They are named `opentender_<code>`, by the two-letter code of the country as above (`opentender_AT`, ..., `opentender_UK`, and `opentender_CH`, `opentender_GE`, `opentender_IS`, `opentender_MK`, `opentender_RS` for Switzerland, Georgia, Iceland, North Macedonia and Serbia), `opentender_EU` for the procurement of the EU institutions, and `opentender_TED` for all the notices of TED. Each node is a buyer or a supplier, identified by the de-duplicated body id of OpenTender (the same in all processes of a network), and each directed edge is the award of a contract by a buyer to a supplier, one edge for each supplier of each award (a multigraph). The tenders without awards, the bids, lots, items and the indicators of OpenTender are not included.

The `contracts` network has the following properties, taken from the upstream data dictionary:

- (Node) `id_final`: deduplicated identifier of the issuer or winner, ending in `_i` for issuers and `_w` for winners.
- (Node) `is_issuer`: whether the node is an issuer (True) or a winner (False).
- (Node) `name`: raw name.
- (Node) `canonical_name`: most common name after deduplication.
- (Node) `country`, `address`, `postcode`, `town`: location of the issuer or winner (raw text).
- (Node) `type` and `sector`: type (e.g. "3. Regional or local authorities") and sector (e.g. "Health") of the issuer.
- (Edge) `tender_id`: contract identifier.
- (Edge) `year` and `date_dispatched`: year and date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the contract.
- (Edge) `est_value` and `contract_value`: raw estimated and final value of the contract (currency and VAT treatment unclear).
- (Edge) `contract_nuts` and `processed_nuts`: raw and (imperfectly) cleaned NUTS geographic code of where the contract is performed.
- (Edge) `contract_cpv` and `cpv2`: Common Procurement Vocabulary (CPV) code of the purchased goods or services, and its 2-digit prefix.
- (Edge) `contract_eu_funded`: 1 if the contract was supported by EU funding.
- (Edge) `contract_type`: works, services or supplies.
- (Edge) `procedure`: the award procedure (e.g. open, restricted).
- (Edge) `n_bids`: number of bids received.
- (Edge) `nocft`: 1 if no call for tenders was found.
- (Edge) `single_bidder`: 1 if there was no competition for the contract (single bid), an indicator of corruption risk; missing values were imputed with the country mean.

The country-year networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `label`: node identifier, ending in `_i` for issuers and `_w` for winners.
- (Node) `is_issuer`: whether the node is an issuer (True) or a winner (False).
- (Edge) `count`: the number of contracts between the issuer and the winner in the given year.
- (Edge) `pctSingleBid`: the fraction of these contracts that were awarded without competition, i.e. with a single bidder or to a sole supplier, an elementary indicator of corruption risk. Missing single-bidding information was imputed, as described in the paper.

The OpenTender networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `body_id`: the body id of OpenTender.
- (Node) `name`: the name of the buyer or supplier (the first one found).
- (Node) `organization_ids`: its other identifiers, as given (e.g. national registration numbers).
- (Node) `country`: the country of its address (two-letter code, as given; empty if none).
- (Node) `is_buyer`, `is_supplier`: whether it appears as a buyer or as a supplier.
- (Edge) `ocid`: the open contracting id of the contracting process.
- (Edge) `award_id`: the id of the award within the process.
- (Edge) `amount`, `currency`: the value of the award (NaN if not given).
- (Edge) `date`: the date of the award (or of the release, if not given), ISO 8601.
- (Edge) `method`: the procurement method (`open`, `selective`, `limited`, `direct`; empty if not given).
- (Edge) `method_details`: the procedure in the terms of OpenTender.
- (Edge) `category`: the main procurement category (`goods`, `works`, `services`; empty if not given).
- (Edge) `cpv`: the CPV codes of the items of the award (or of the tender, if the award has none).
- (Edge) `title`: the title of the tender.
citations: J. Wachs, M. Fazekas, and J. Kertész, "Corruption Risk in Contracting Markets: A Network Science Perspective." International Journal of Data Science and Analytics, pp 1–16 (2020)
Government Transparency Institute, "OpenTender." OCDS publications of the OCP Data Registry (2026)

datasets.name: euppollnet
datasets.description:
Plant-pollinator networks from EuPPollNet (European Plant-Pollinator Networks), a database that harmonizes the plant-pollinator interaction data of 54 studies carried out between 2004 and 2021 in 23 European countries, compiled by J. B. Lanuza, T. M. Knight and more than a hundred collaborators. The studies recorded the insects (bees, hoverflies and other flies, butterflies, beetles, ...) visiting the flowers of plants, by transects, focal observations of plants or random censuses; the taxonomy of plants and pollinators was harmonized against GBIF and expert-curated checklists. This is version 1.3.0 of the database (April 2025), which removed duplicated records of earlier versions, with 623,476 interaction records; the networks of the earlier versions are also included (see below).

Each network is one sampling event in space and time, as defined by the database: the records of one study, one site (the `Network_id` of the study) and one year, giving 1,864 networks. They are named `<study>_<site>_<year>`, e.g. `1_Bartomeus_BAT1CA_2005` (with accents removed and runs of characters other than letters, digits and "-" replaced by underscores; the original identifiers are kept as graph properties). The networks are bipartite and undirected: nodes are plant and pollinator taxa (by their accepted names), with the property `is_pollinator` marking the pollinators, and an edge connects a plant and a pollinator observed interacting, weighted by the number of records of the interaction (each record of the database is one observed interaction). The original names of the taxa in the studies, the dates of the individual records, and the flower counts that the database also provides are not included. A few records have taxon names in the Mac OS Roman encoding instead of UTF-8, which were converted. The coordinates are those of the network's site; for six networks with records at several coordinates, the graph properties give their mean.

The earlier versions of the database are included as networks named after the version (`v1.0_<network>`, `v1.1_<network>`), taken from the GitHub repository at the commits of the releases (their archives at Zenodo are not openly accessible), where they are only available as R data files (`Interaction_data.rds`, `Metadata.rds`). Version 1.0.0 (October 2024) has 1,162,913 records, almost twice as many as version 1.3.0, since many records were duplicated; its networks are the same 1,864 sampling events (8 sites of the study `53_Libran-Embid` were renamed later), and 1,850 of them differ from those of version 1.3.0 (most of them in their edges or weights only, with the same nodes), and are included as `v1.0_<network>` (the other 14 are identical). Version 1.1.0 (December 2024) changed the records of 9 networks, which are included as `v1.1_<network>` (its other networks are identical to those of version 1.0.0). The data files of version 1.2.0 (January 2025) are identical to those of version 1.1.0. The networks of the earlier versions are built in the same way and have the same properties.

The networks of the study `1_Bartomeus` (Bartomeus et al. 2008, Cap de Creus, Spain) are also in the entry `iwdb` (`pollination_bartomeus_<plot>`), and those of `14_Dupont` (Dupont et al. 2009, Denmark) appear to be in the entry `web_of_life` (`M_PL_047`, `M_PL_048`, Dupont and Olesen 2009).

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the accepted name of the taxon.
- (Node) `is_pollinator`: whether the node is a pollinator (otherwise a plant).
- (Node) `rank`: the taxonomic rank of the name ("SPECIES", "GENUS", "FAMILY", ...).
- (Node) `order`, `family`, `genus`: the taxonomy of the taxon (empty if not available).
- (Node) `unsure_id`: whether the identification of the taxon is uncertain in some record ("Yes" in the database).
- (Edge) `weight`: the number of records of the interaction.
- (Graph) `study_id`, `network_id` (the site within the study, as in the database) and `year`; `doi` (the publication of the study, if any, or "Unpublished"); `sampling_method`; `country`, `locality`, `bioregion`, `habitat` (the EuPPollNet habitat class) and `authors_habitat` (the habitat as described by the authors), with several values separated by "; " if the records of the network differ; `latitude`, `longitude`; and `first_date`, `last_date` (the dates of the first and last record, as YYYY-MM-DD).
citations: J. B. Lanuza, T. M. Knight, N. Montes-Perez, et al., "EuPPollNet: A European Database of Plant-Pollinator Networks." Global Ecology and Biogeography 34(2), e70000 (2025)

datasets.name: euroroad
datasets.description:
The network of the international E-road network, a numbering system for main roads in Europe (and some neighboring countries) defined by the United Nations Economic Commission for Europe. The network was compiled by L. Šubelj and M. Bajec from the description of the E-roads in Wikipedia. Nodes are the cities listed along the E-roads and an edge connects two cities that are consecutive on some E-road. Some pairs of cities are connected by more than one edge (50 pairs), which presumably correspond to road segments shared by several E-roads, although this is not documented upstream; the E-road numbers are not included. Three cities have no connections (Mariehamn, Kapellskär and Civitavecchia), presumably because they are joined to the network only by ferry routes. The network is undirected and unweighted.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the name of the city.
citations: L. Šubelj, M. Bajec, "Robust network community detection using balanced propagation." The European Physical Journal B 81(3), 353-362 (2011)

datasets.name: eva_ownership
datasets.description:
Ownership relations among companies in the telecommunications and media industries, from the EVA (Extraction, Visualization and Analysis of corporate inter-relationships) project of the Denali group at the University of California, Berkeley. The relations were extracted automatically, using probabilistic information retrieval and extraction techniques, from heterogeneous sources of online text, including the corporate annual reports (10-K) filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. A directed edge points from a company to a company it owns (a parent-subsidiary relation). Ownership relations are not available for all companies, so many companies have no edges. The data were converted into Pajek format by V. Batagelj (2004). The data were distributed in Pajek format on the Pajek datasets page of V. Batagelj and A. Mrvar, from which this version was obtained. The Pajek file declares 8497 vertices, but only 8325 identifiers are used (8322 with a company name, and 3 unnamed companies with edges); the unused identifiers are not included.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the name of the company ("?" for 100 companies whose name is unknown, and empty for the 3 unnamed ones).
citations: K. Norlen, G. Lucas, M. Gebbie, J. Chuang, "EVA: Extraction, Visualization and Analysis of the Telecommunications and Media Ownership Network." Proceedings of the International Telecommunications Society 14th Biennial Conference, Seoul (2002)

datasets.name: eventernote
datasets.description:
A bipartite network of Japanese idols, voice actors and other artists, and the events they took part in (concerts, release events, stage greetings, broadcasts, etc.), from Eventernote, a crowdsourced Japanese website that lists such events, as collected for XGI-data. Events span from July 1980 to April 2024; an event of several days is split into one event per day. An artist node is either an individual artist or a group of artists (e.g. an idol group); individuals and their groups are distinct nodes, and which artists belong to which groups is not given. The data list 5,381 artists without any event, which are isolated nodes.

XGI-data also distributes a bipartite network of the artists and the places of their events; it is not included as a separate network, since it follows from this one (the places are given as properties of the events).

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `is_event`: whether the node is an event (otherwise an artist).
- (Node) `eventernote_id`: the identifier of the artist or event on Eventernote (e.g. `https://www.eventernote.com/actors/<id>` or `https://www.eventernote.com/events/<id>`).
- (Node) `name` (artists): the name of the artist or group.
- (Node) `kana` (artists): the reading of the name in kana.
- (Node) `sex` (artists): `female`, `male`, or `other` (non-binary, not specified or not applicable, e.g. for groups).
- (Node) `name` (events): the name of the event.
- (Node) `date` (events): the date of the event (YYYY-MM-DD).
- (Node) `time` (events): the same date in Unix time (midnight UTC).
- (Node) `place_id` (events): the Eventernote identifier of the place of the event (`https://www.eventernote.com/places/<id>`; -1 if unknown).
- (Node) `place_name` (events): the name of the place.
- (Node) `prefecture` (events): the prefecture of the place, as its ISO 3166-2:JP code (1 for Hokkaido to 47 for Okinawa; 0 if the prefecture of a known place is not given, 90 for places outside Japan, and -1 for events without a known place).
citations: N. W. Landry, M. Lucas, I. Iacopini, G. Petri, A. Schwarze, A. Patania, L. Torres, "XGI: A Python package for higher-order interaction networks." Journal of Open Source Software 8(85), 5162 (2023)

datasets.name: faa_routes
datasets.description:
A network of air traffic control routes in the United States, constructed by the Ma'ayan Laboratory (Mount Sinai School of Medicine) from the Preferred Routes Database of the National Flight Data Center (NFDC) of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), which lists the routes recommended for flights between airports. Each preferred route is a string of route elements, and a directed edge joins each element to the next one in a route string. Nodes are these elements, identified by their codes: airports, navigational aids and fixes, airways (e.g. Victor airways such as V162 and jet routes such as J10) and named standard terminal arrival routes (suffix `_STAR`) and departure procedures (suffix `_DP`). The network was distributed in the laboratory's SIG flat file format, and was extracted from the database at an undocumented date before 2010; the FAA database is updated regularly, and its current version differs from this network.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the code of the route element (as used in the FAA database).
citations: United States Federal Aviation Administration, "Air traffic control system command center."

datasets.name: facebook100
datasets.description:
Facebook friendship networks within 100 American colleges and universities, from a single day in September 2005, when Facebook was still restricted to university communities. The data were provided to A. L. Traud, P. J. Mucha and M. A. Porter by Facebook, and released by them in 2011 (as `facebook100.zip`; five of the networks had been released before as "Facebook5"). Each network contains all the friendships between Facebook users of the same institution (links to other institutions are not included), without isolated nodes, and is not restricted to the largest connected component. Nodes are users (anonymous, labeled consecutively), and an undirected edge connects two users who are Facebook friends. Each network is named after its institution with the number by which the authors indexed it (e.g. `Caltech36`, `Harvard1`, `Penn94`; the spaces of `Johns Hopkins55` and `Notre Dame57` are replaced by underscores).

The data were obtained from a copy of the original files (identical to the copy of five of them in the LINKX benchmark repository) in the history of a public GitHub repository, pinned at a fixed commit, since the copy in the Internet Archive (item `oxford-2005-facebook-matrix`, facebook100.zip) is no longer publicly accessible.

The node attributes were anonymized by the authors: each attribute value is replaced by an integer code (except the year), and the meaning of the codes is not provided; the code 0 means missing data. The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `status`: the student/faculty status flag (an integer code; which code stands for which status, e.g. student or faculty, is not documented; the codes are 1 to 6, 0 if missing, and 10 for two nodes).
- (Node) `gender`: the gender (an integer code, 1 or 2; 0 if missing; which code stands for which gender is not documented).
- (Node) `major`: the major (an integer code).
- (Node) `second_major`: the second major or minor (an integer code).
- (Node) `dorm`: the dorm or house (an integer code).
- (Node) `year`: the class year (a calendar year, e.g. 2008; 0 if missing). A few implausible values are kept as in the data (e.g. 1887, 3000, and the year 2147483647 of a node of `Harvard1` and -80085 of a node of `UChicago30`).
- (Node) `high_school`: the high school (an integer code).
citations: A. L. Traud, P. J. Mucha, and M. A. Porter, "Social structure of Facebook networks." Physica A 391(16), 4165-4180 (2012).
A. L. Traud, E. D. Kelsic, P. J. Mucha, and M. A. Porter, "Comparing Community Structure to Characteristics in Online Collegiate Social Networks." SIAM Review 53(3), 526-543 (2011).

datasets.name: facebook_friends
datasets.description:
The anonymized Facebook friendship network of B. F. Maier, collected in fall 2014. Nodes are the Facebook profiles of his friends, and an undirected edge connects two profiles that are "friends" on Facebook. The ego node (Maier's own profile), which was connected to every other node, has been removed, so the network has several connected components (the largest has 329 nodes). The network was used as an example in a study of random-walk cover times.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `context_0`, `context_1`, `context_2`, `context_3`: up to four free-text labels given by the ego to describe the social context of the relationship with that person (e.g. "school", "uni", "choir", "family", "friend of friend"); unused labels are empty.
citations: B. F. Maier and D. Brockmann, "Cover time for random walks on arbitrary complex networks." Phys. Rev. E 96, 042307 (2017)

datasets.name: facebook_organizations
datasets.description:
Six networks of Facebook friendships among employees of six anonymized high-tech companies, collected in 2012 by M. Fire and R. Puzis. Nodes are Facebook users who stated in their public profile that they worked for the target company, and an undirected edge connects two such users who are Facebook friends; only friendships between employees of the same company are included. The data were obtained with a focused crawler that starts from seed profiles of known employees and preferentially explores profiles with many friends already identified as employees, matching company-related keywords in each public profile. User identities were anonymized by replacing Facebook IDs with consecutive integers, which are stored in the vertex property `name`.

The companies are grouped by size: small (`S1`, `S2`; 500 to 2,000 employees), medium (`M1`, `M2`; 4,000 to 20,000 employees) and large (`L1`, `L2`; more than 50,000 employees). Companies labeled 1 were crawled with the first version of the crawler, which stops when its queue is exhausted, and those labeled 2 with a second version with a stricter stopping condition. The companies described in the paper are a network hardware company (S1), a software company (S2), a telecommunication services company (M1), a software and outsourcing company (M2), and two large multinational technology corporations (L1, L2). Note that the sizes of the published `S1` (320 nodes, 2,369 edges) and `S2` (165 nodes, 726 edges) networks are swapped relative to those reported in the paper. The employee job positions analyzed in the paper are not included in the data.
citations: M. Fire, and R. Puzis, "Organization mining using online social networks." Networks and Spatial Economics 16(2), 545-578 (2016)

datasets.name: facebook_pages
datasets.description:
Networks of verified ("blue") Facebook pages, collected through the Facebook Graph API in November 2017 by B. Rozemberczki and collaborators for benchmarks of node embedding and classification methods. Nodes are pages, and an undirected edge connects two pages that like each other (mutual likes). There are two data sets:

- GEMSEC: eight networks of pages of a single category, `athletes`, `artist`, `company`, `government`, `new_sites` (news sites), `politician`, `public_figure` and `tvshow`. The pages were reindexed for anonymity, so the networks have no node attributes. The edge lists contain self-loops (from 23 in `politician` and `tvshow` to 295 in `new_sites`), which are kept.
- `musae`: a network of 22,470 pages of four categories (politicians, governmental organizations, television shows and companies), from the MUSAE study, with the names, Facebook identifiers and categories of the pages, and lists of binary features extracted from the descriptions written by the page owners (only the indices of the features are given, not their meaning). The edge list contains 179 self-loops, which are kept. SNAP no longer offers this data set for download; it was obtained from a pinned snapshot of the SNAP file in the Internet Archive (February 17, 2024).

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) None in the GEMSEC networks, besides the node indices.
- (Node) `facebook_id` (`musae`): the Facebook identifier of the page.
- (Node) `name` (`musae`): the name of the page.
- (Node) `page_type` (`musae`): its category ("politician", "government", "tvshow" or "company").
- (Node) `features` (`musae`): the indices of its binary features.
citations: B. Rozemberczki, R. Davies, R. Sarkar, and C. Sutton, "GEMSEC: Graph Embedding with Self Clustering." Proceedings of the 2019 IEEE/ACM International Conference on Advances in Social Networks Analysis and Mining (ASONAM), 65-72 (2019).
B. Rozemberczki, C. Allen, and R. Sarkar, "Multi-scale attributed node embedding." Journal of Complex Networks 9(2), cnab014 (2021).

datasets.name: facebook_slavko
datasets.description: A small network of friendships on the online social network Facebook, from the Facebook account of Slavko Žitnik, used by Blagus, Šubelj and Bajec in their study of the scaling of network density. Nodes are Facebook users (anonymized), and an undirected edge indicates that two users are friends. The data collection procedure is not documented; presumably the nodes are the friends of the account owner (who is not included), and the edges the friendships among them. The network contains 10 isolated nodes.
