- (Node) `name`: the name of the node as given by the original authors; `node_id`: the Mangal node id; `node_level`: whether the node is a `taxon`, a `population` or an `individual`; `taxon`: the name of the taxon matched in Mangal (empty if not matched); `rank`: its taxonomic rank (e.g. `species`, `genus`); `ncbi`, `tsn`, `gbif`, `eol`, `bold`: its identifiers in the NCBI Taxonomy, ITIS, GBIF, the Encyclopedia of Life and BOLD (-1 if unknown); `col`: its identifier in the Catalogue of Life.
- (Edge) `interaction_id`: the Mangal interaction id; `type`: the type of interaction; `method`: the method by which the interaction was recorded (e.g. `field observations`, `gut content`, `literature`); `direction`: `directed`, `undirected` or `unknown`; `attribute`: what the value measures (e.g. `presence/absence`, `number of visit by a pollinator`); `value`: the value of the interaction (NaN if not given); `date`: the date of the observation (as given in Mangal; often the date of the whole network).
- (Graph) `network_id`, `network_description` and `network_date`: the id, description and date of the Mangal network; `geometry`: its location, as a GeoJSON point or polygon (longitude, latitude), if known; `all_interactions`: whether absences of interactions were recorded as well; `dataset` and `dataset_description`: the Mangal data set it belongs to; `reference_doi`, `reference_bibtex`: the reference of the original publication; `data_url`: the address of the original data, if any.
citations: T. Poisot, B. Baiser, J. A. Dunne, S. Kéfi, F. Massol, N. Mouquet, T. N. Romanuk, D. B. Stouffer, S. A. Wood, D. Gravel, "mangal - making ecological network analysis simple." Ecography 39, 384-390 (2016)

datasets.name: marker_cafe
datasets.description:
Anonymized snapshot of the connections among users of TheMarker Cafe, an Israeli online social networking site (associated with the business newspaper TheMarker) that allows its members to connect and interact; most of its members are Israeli and communicate in Hebrew. Nodes are users and edges are connections between them. The data were released by M. Fire and collaborators at Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, who used them to evaluate link prediction methods, and correspond to around 2011, when their first study was published. How the data were collected is not documented.

The source file lists each connection only once, without any reciprocated pairs, and the network is treated as undirected. It contains 6 self-loops.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the anonymized user ID from the source file.
citations: M. Fire et al. "Computationally efficient link prediction in a variety of social networks." ACM Transactions on Intelligent Systems and Technology 5(1), Article 10 (2013)

datasets.name: marvel_partnerships
datasets.description:
Network of partnerships among characters of the Marvel comic book universe, compiled by Ulf Aslak in 2018 and shared as a JSON file accompanying a network visualization posted on Twitter. Nodes are heroes and villains, identified by the titles of their English Wikipedia articles, and an undirected edge connects two characters if the Wikipedia page of one lists the other as a partner. Only characters with at least one partnership are included. Further details of the extraction are not documented.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `id`: the title of the character's Wikipedia article (as in "Venom (Marvel Comics character)").
- (Node) `group`: the type of character, with 0 = hero and 1 = villain. The value 2 is used for 35 characters that have been both, such as Magneto, Rogue or Sabretooth; its meaning is not documented in the source.
- (Node) `size`: the number of partners of the character in the source data (equal to its degree).

datasets.name: marvel_universe
datasets.description:
A bipartite network of Marvel comic book characters and the comic books in which they appear, compiled by R. Alberich, J. Miro-Julia and F. Rosselló from the Marvel Chronology Project (MCP), a database created by R. Chappell that catalogs every canonical appearance of every significant Marvel character. Each edge connects a character to a comic book in which the character appears. The network contains 96,662 appearances of 6,486 characters in 12,942 comic books; the MCP database does not include comic books published between early 1993 and mid 1994. The one-mode projection onto the characters, where two characters are connected if they appear together in some comic book, is the "Marvel Universe collaboration network" studied by the authors.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the name of the character, often with its alter ego and truncated to 20 characters in the source (as in "SPIDER-MAN/PETER PAR"), or the comic book (title abbreviation and issue number, as in "ASM 300"). Some character names occur more than once.
- (Node) `is_comic`: whether the node is a comic book (otherwise it is a character).
citations: R. Alberich, J. Miro-Julia, and F. Rossello, "Marvel Universe looks almost like a real social network." arxiv:cond-mat/0202174 (2002).

datasets.name: matpower
datasets.description:
Electrical power systems distributed as test cases (`case*.m` files) with MATPOWER, the open-source MATLAB package for power flow and optimal power flow computations by Zimmerman, Murillo-Sánchez and Thomas. Nodes are buses (substations or connection points) and directed edges are branches (transmission lines, cables and transformers), directed from the "from" bus to the "to" bus of the branch (for transformers, the tap ratio and phase shift apply at the "from" side). Parallel branches are kept as multiple edges. Generators are not represented as nodes; their data are aggregated at the buses they are connected to. DC lines (present in two cases) are not included.

The test cases come from many sources, which are described in each case file. They include:

- Classic IEEE test cases and textbook examples: `case4gs`, `case5`, `case6ww`, `case9` (and variants `case9Q`, `case9target`), `case14`, `case24_ieee_rts`, `case30` (and variants `case30Q`, `case30pwl`, `case_ieee30`), `case39` (New England), `case57`, `case59` (Australian), `case60nordic`, `case118`, `case145`, `case300`.
- The Polish transmission system at several dates between 1999 and 2008: `case2383wp`, `case2736sp`, `case2737sop`, `case2746wop`, `case2746wp`, `case3012wp`, `case3120sp`, `case3375wp`.
- Parts of the European high-voltage transmission system from the PEGASE project: `case89pegase`, `case1354pegase`, `case2869pegase`, `case8387pegase`, `case9241pegase`, `case13659pegase` (Fliscounakis et al., 2013; Josz et al., 2016).
- Snapshots of the French transmission system from RTE: `case1888rte`, `case1951rte`, `case2848rte`, `case2868rte`, `case6468rte`, `case6470rte`, `case6495rte`, `case6515rte` (Josz et al., 2016).
- Synthetic grids of the ACTIVSg project, which resemble the grids of US regions without containing real infrastructure data: `case_ACTIVSg200` (Illinois), `case_ACTIVSg500` (South Carolina), `case_ACTIVSg2000` (Texas), `case_ACTIVSg10k` (western US), `case_ACTIVSg25k` (northeastern US), `case_ACTIVSg70k` (eastern US), and `case_SyntheticUSA` (combined US, 82,000 buses) (Birchfield et al., 2017).
- Radial distribution systems from the literature, e.g. `case10ba`, `case12da`, `case33bw`, `case69`, `case118zh`, `case136ma`, `case141`, `case533mt_hi`, `case533mt_lo`, `case1197`. For these cases, the unit conversions performed by the case files (branch impedances from ohms to per unit, loads from kW to MW, and, for `case141`, loads from kVA using a power factor of 0.85) have been applied.

The RTS-GMLC test case is not included, since its data use agreement requires reproducing a notice with every copy.

The networks have the following properties (in MATPOWER's units: powers in MW and MVAr, voltages in per unit of the base voltage, angles in degrees, impedances in per unit of the system base `base_mva`, a graph property):

- (Node) `bus_id`: the bus number.
- (Node) `bus_type` (1: PQ (load) bus, 2: PV (generator) bus, 3: reference (slack) bus, 4: isolated bus).
- (Node) `pd` and `qd`: the active and reactive power demand.
- (Node) `gs` and `bs`: the shunt conductance and susceptance (MW and MVAr consumed at 1 p.u. voltage).
- (Node) `area` and `zone`: area and loss zone numbers.
- (Node) `vm` and `va`: the voltage magnitude and angle.
- (Node) `base_kv`: the base voltage (kV).
- (Node) `vmax` and `vmin`: the voltage limits.
- (Node) `n_gen`: the number of in-service generators at the bus.
- (Node) `gen_p`, `gen_q`, `gen_pmax`, `gen_pmin`, `gen_qmax`, `gen_qmin`: the total active and reactive power output and limits of these generators.
- (Node) `name`: the bus name (only for some cases).
- (Edge) `r`, `x` and `b`: the branch resistance, reactance and total line charging susceptance.
- (Edge) `rate_a`, `rate_b` and `rate_c`: the long-term, short-term and emergency power ratings (MVA; 0 means unlimited).
- (Edge) `ratio`: the transformer tap ratio (0 for lines).
- (Edge) `shift`: the transformer phase shift angle.
- (Edge) `status`: 1 if in service and 0 otherwise.
- (Edge) `angmin` and `angmax`: the limits on the voltage angle difference across the branch.
citations: R. D. Zimmerman, C. E. Murillo-Sánchez, R. J. Thomas, "MATPOWER: Steady-State Operations, Planning, and Analysis Tools for Power Systems Research and Education." IEEE Transactions on Power Systems 26(1), 12-19 (2011)

S. Fliscounakis, P. Panciatici, F. Capitanescu, L. Wehenkel, "Contingency Ranking With Respect to Overloads in Very Large Power Systems Taking Into Account Uncertainty, Preventive, and Corrective Actions." IEEE Transactions on Power Systems 28(4), 4909-4917 (2013)
C. Josz, S. Fliscounakis, J. Maeght, P. Panciatici, "AC Power Flow Data in MATPOWER and QCQP Format: iTesla, RTE Snapshots, and PEGASE." arXiv:1603.01533 (2016)

A. B. Birchfield, T. Xu, K. M. Gegner, K. S. Shetye, T. J. Overbye, "Grid Structural Characteristics as Validation Criteria for Synthetic Networks." IEEE Transactions on Power Systems 32(4), 3258-3265 (2017)

datasets.name: mcgrew_preschool
datasets.description:
Competition for toys among the boys of a preschool group in Oxford (England), from the ethological observations of preschool children of W. C. McGrew. "Winners" were the children who ended up with the toy. The data were distributed by L. C. Freeman on his network data page at the University of California, Irvine (no longer online), from which this version was obtained via the Internet Archive.

A directed edge (i, j) indicates that child i won a competition for a toy against child j. The data include 19 children, two of which do not appear in any recorded competition.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the label of the child.
- (Edge) `weight`: the number of competitions won.
citations: W. C. McGrew, "An Ethological Study of Children's Behavior." Academic Press, p. 125 (1972)

datasets.name: mcm_atmospheric
datasets.description:
Networks of the chemical reactions of the Master Chemical Mechanism (MCM), a near-explicit mechanism of the gas-phase chemistry of the troposphere, which describes the degradation of 143 emitted volatile organic compounds (alkanes, alkenes, aromatics, isoprene, terpenes, oxygenated compounds, ...) and the inorganic chemistry of ozone, nitrogen oxides and sulfur, and is used in models of air quality. The reactions and their rate coefficients were derived by the MCM developers from measured kinetic data and from structure-activity relationships, following documented protocols.

The networks are directed and bipartite: nodes are chemical species and reactions, and an edge goes from each reactant to the reaction, and from the reaction to each of its products. A species that appears twice among the reactants (e.g. `HO2 + HO2`) or the products of a reaction gives parallel edges. Reactions without products (e.g. a sink of a species) only have edges from their reactants; the pseudo-species of photons (`hv`) and of unspecified products (`PROD`) of the KPP format are left out (photolysis reactions are marked as such).

There is one network for each version of the mechanism available from its website, from the files of the complete mechanism: `v3.3.1` (exported in September 2023, KPP format), `v3.2` (KPP format), `v3.1` (FACSIMILE box model, 2005), `v3.0` (FACSIMILE box model, 2003) and `v2.0` (FACSIMILE box model, 1999). The box models of the older versions contain the reactions of the mechanism (with some reactions written as several lines with partial rate coefficients, which are kept as separate reactions, and reversible reactions, which are split into their forward and backward reactions), together with the setup of the model, which is ignored.

The Common Representative Intermediates mechanism (CRI), distributed from the same site, is a reduced mechanism derived from the MCM: the degradation of the emitted compounds is described with far fewer reactions and intermediate species, which are lumped into "representative intermediates" that conserve the ozone-forming potential of each compound (counted as its number of reactive bonds, `C-C` and `C-H`), and its parameters were optimized against the MCM in box-model simulations. CRI v2 was developed with MCM v3.1 as the reference. Its two versions available from the site are included, built in the same way, from the KPP files of the complete mechanism: `cri_v2_1` (CRI v2.1, exported in June 2018: the reactions of CRI v2, with the revisions of rate coefficients of the transition from MCM v3.1 to v3.2) and `cri_v2_2` (CRI v2.2, exported in September 2023: a substantially revised chemistry of isoprene, and the revisions of rate coefficients of the transition from MCM v3.2 to v3.3.1). The reduced variants of CRI with lumped emissions (R1-R5) are not among the files of the site and are not included.

Only `v3.3.1` and `cri_v2_2` have the properties of the species (structures, formulas and masses).

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `is_reaction`: whether the node is a reaction (otherwise it is a species).
- (Node) `name`: the name of the species in the MCM (e.g. `O3`, `CH3O2`, `APINENE`), or the equation of the reaction.
- (Node) `rate`: the rate coefficient of the reaction, as an expression (in the syntax of the file: FORTRAN for KPP, FACSIMILE otherwise) of the temperature `TEMP`, of the concentrations of `M`, `O2`, `N2`, `H2O`, of named complex rate coefficients (e.g. `KMT01`, `KRO2NO`), of the sum of the peroxy radicals `RO2`, and, for photolysis, of the photolysis rates `J(...)` (empty for species).
- (Node) `is_photolysis`: whether the reaction is a photolysis.
- (Node) `smiles`, `inchi`, `inchi_key`, `formula`, `mass` (`v3.3.1`, `cri_v2_2`): the structure, formula and molar mass of the species (empty or NaN for reactions, and for the lumped species of CRI without a structure).
- (Node) `is_excited`, `is_peroxy_radical` (`v3.3.1`, `cri_v2_2`): whether the species is an excited species, or a peroxy radical.
citations: M. E. Jenkin, S. M. Saunders, M. J. Pilling, "The tropospheric degradation of volatile organic compounds: a protocol for mechanism development." Atmospheric Environment 31, 81-104 (1997)

S. M. Saunders, M. E. Jenkin, R. G. Derwent, M. J. Pilling, "Protocol for the development of the Master Chemical Mechanism, MCM v3 (Part A): tropospheric degradation of non-aromatic volatile organic compounds." Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics 3, 161-180 (2003)

M. E. Jenkin, S. M. Saunders, V. Wagner, M. J. Pilling, "Protocol for the development of the Master Chemical Mechanism, MCM v3 (Part B): tropospheric degradation of aromatic volatile organic compounds." Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics 3, 181-193 (2003)
M. E. Jenkin, J. C. Young, A. R. Rickard, "The MCM v3.3.1 degradation scheme for isoprene." Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics 15, 11433-11459 (2015)

M. E. Jenkin, L. A. Watson, S. R. Utembe, D. E. Shallcross, "A Common Representative Intermediates (CRI) mechanism for VOC degradation. Part 1: Gas phase mechanism development." Atmospheric Environment 42, 7185-7195 (2008)

L. A. Watson, D. E. Shallcross, S. R. Utembe, M. E. Jenkin, "A Common Representative Intermediates (CRI) mechanism for VOC degradation. Part 2: Gas phase mechanism reduction." Atmospheric Environment 42, 7196-7204 (2008)

M. E. Jenkin, M. A. H. Khan, D. E. Shallcross, R. Bergström, D. Simpson, K. L. C. Murphy, A. R. Rickard, "The CRI v2.2 reduced degradation scheme for isoprene." Atmospheric Environment 212, 172-182 (2019)

datasets.name: meetup_dublin
datasets.description:
A network of the public Meetup.com groups based in Dublin, Ireland, from Pakrashi et al. Meetup.com is an online platform for organizing in-person events ("meetups") of groups of people with shared interests. In September 2018, the authors used the Meetup.com API to list all the groups in Ireland, keeping the 1,482 public groups hosted in Dublin, and retrieved the members of each group. Each node is a group, and an undirected edge connects two groups that share at least one member, with a weight given by the Jaccard index of their member sets (the number of common members divided by the number of members of either group). The network is thus a weighted one-mode projection of the bipartite network of users and groups. One group shares no members with the others, and is an isolated node.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the name of the group.
- (Node) `meetup_id`: the Meetup.com identifier of the group.
- (Node) `member_count`: the number of members.
- (Node) `join_mode`: how new members join the group ("open" or "approval").
- (Node) `description`: the description of the group (as distributed, with punctuation removed).
- (Node) `created`: the date of creation of the group.
- (Node) `categories`: the list of Meetup.com categories of the group.
- (Edge) `weight`: the Jaccard index of the member sets of the two groups.
citations: A. Pakrashi, E. Alghamdi, B. Mac Namee, D. Greene, "MeetupNet Dublin: Discovering Communities in Dublin's Meetup Network." Proceedings of the 26th Irish Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Cognitive Science (AICS) (2018)

datasets.name: messal_shale
datasets.description:
Food web of the early Eocene Messel Shale (Germany), a fossil site about 48 million years old that preserves the lake and surrounding forest ecosystem of the time, compiled by J. A. Dunne, C. C. Labandeira and R. J. Williams. Nodes are taxa (plants, animals, fungi, bacteria) and non-living resources (detritus and dead animal material), and a directed edge points from a consumer to the resource it feeds on. Feeding links were inferred from several lines of evidence, such as gut contents, coprolites, damage patterns on plants, functional morphology, body size, and the diets of the closest living relatives (taxonomic uniformity), and each link was assigned a level of certainty.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the name of the taxon or resource.
- (Node) `group`: the higher-level taxonomic group of the taxon (usually its order, as in "Coleoptera").
- (Edge) `certainty`: the certainty of the feeding link, with 1 = high, 2 = intermediate, 3 = low (see the graph property `certainty_key`).
- (Edge) `evidence`: the list of types of evidence supporting the link, with codes 1 = taxonomic uniformity, 2 = functional morphology, 3 = gut contents, 4 = damage pattern, 5 = stratigraphic co-occurrence, 6 = body size, 7 = coprolites, 8 = host relationship, 9 = biochemistry and minerals, 10 = track or domicile (see the graph property `evidence_key`).
- (Edge) `references`: the list of literature references supporting the link, as indices into the graph property `reference_key`.
citations: J. A. Dunne, C. C. Labandeira, & R. J. Williams, "Highly resolved early Eocene food webs show development of modern trophic structure after the end-Cretaceous extinction." Proc. Royal Soc. B: Biological Sciences 281(1782), 20133280 (2014).

datasets.name: metal_trade
datasets.description:
The international trade in miscellaneous manufactures of metal (a class of commodities representing high technology products or heavy manufacture) among 80 countries in 1994, compiled by W. de Nooy from the United Nations' Commodity Trade Statistics. All countries with entries in the paper version of the statistics were included, but for some countries the data of 1993 (Austria, Seychelles, Bangladesh, Croatia and Barbados) or 1995 (South Africa and Ecuador) were used, since the 1994 data were not available. Non-sovereign countries were excluded (as well as most countries in central Africa, the Middle East and the former USSR, which are missing from the statistics). A directed edge points from the exporting to the importing country, and is weighted by the absolute value of the imports; imports worth less than 1% of the importing country's total imports in this class were omitted. Two pairs of countries have two edges with different values in the source. The data were distributed on the Pajek datasets page of the book *Exploratory Social Network Analysis with Pajek* (de Nooy, Mrvar and Batagelj), from which this version was obtained.[^icon]

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the name of the country.
- (Node) `continent` (1: Africa, 2: Asia, 3: Europe, 4: North America, 5: Oceania, 6: South America).
- (Node) `world_system`: the structural world system position of the country in 1994 (1: core, 2: semiperiphery, 3: periphery).
- (Node) `world_system_1980`: the world system position in 1980 according to Smith and White (1: core, 2: strong semiperiphery, 3: weak semiperiphery, 4: periphery, -1: unknown).
- (Node) `gdp_1995`: the gross domestic product per capita in 1995, in US$ (from the Statistical Yearbook of the United Nations).
- (Edge) `weight`: the value of the imports, in thousands of US$.

[^icon]: Description obtained in part from the [ICON](https://icon.colorado.edu) project.
citations: W. de Nooy, A. Mrvar, V. Batagelj, "Exploratory Social Network Analysis with Pajek." Cambridge University Press (2005)
D. A. Smith, D. R. White, "Structure and Dynamics of the Global Economy: Network Analysis of International Trade 1965-1980." Social Forces 70(4), 857-893 (1992)

datasets.name: metamath_setmm
datasets.description:
Dependencies between the theorems of set.mm, the main database of the Metamath project, a formalization of mathematics from first principles (classical first-order logic and ZFC set theory), with every step of every proof verified by machine. set.mm was started by Norman Megill in 1992, and has been developed collaboratively since then (on GitHub since 2015), with tens of thousands of theorems, from logic to real and complex analysis, algebra, topology and number theory.

The nodes are the assertions of the database: the theorems (statements with a proof, `$p`), the axioms and the definitions (`$a` statements of the form `|- ...`), and the syntax constructors (`$a` statements of the other types, which define how formulas, classes and set variables are built, e.g. `wi` for the implication). A directed edge goes from a theorem to each assertion referenced in its proof (theorems, axioms, definitions, and syntax constructors used to build the formulas of the proof), with the number of times it is referenced. The hypotheses of the theorems (`$e` and `$f` statements) are not nodes, and are left out.

The proofs are mostly stored in the compressed format of Metamath, where the steps reused within a proof are referenced once, so that the counts are of the references in the proof as stored (the number of times the statement is referenced in the compressed proof, which can be smaller than the number of times it is used in the fully expanded proof). Incomplete proofs (with unknown steps) keep the references they have.

The database is updated continuously; the networks are of the database at the last commit of each year from 2015 to 2025 (`2015` ... `2025`, from the GitHub repository), and of 31 October 2026 (`2026`).

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the label of the assertion (e.g. `ax-mp`, `df-an`, `id`), whose page is `https://us.metamath.org/mpeuni/<name>.html`.
- (Node) `kind`: `theorem`, `axiom` (`$a |-` statements other than definitions), `definition` (labels starting with `df-`) or `syntax`.
- (Node) `statement`: the statement of the assertion, as Metamath symbols (e.g. `|- ( ph -> ph )`).
- (Node) `part`, `chapter`, `section`: the headings of the part, chapter and section of the database in which the assertion appears (e.g. `CLASSICAL FIRST-ORDER LOGIC WITH EQUALITY`, `Propositional calculus`); the users' mathboxes (personal sections of the contributors, with material not yet moved to the main body) are in the part `SUPPLEMENTARY MATERIAL (USERS' MATHBOXES)`.
- (Node) `contributor`: the contributor of the assertion, as given in its comment (usually the initials of a contributor of the list in the header of the database, e.g. `NM` for Norman Megill).
- (Node) `contributed`: the date of the contribution as given in its comment, as Unix time (-1 if not given).
- (Node) `discouraged`: whether new usage of the assertion is discouraged (as stated in its comment).
- (Edge) `count`: the number of references to the assertion in the proof (as stored).
citations: N. Megill, D. A. Wheeler, "Metamath: A Computer Language for Mathematical Proofs." Lulu Press, Morrisville, North Carolina (2019)

datasets.name: metanetx_reactions
datasets.description:
Bipartite networks of metabolic reactions and metabolites from MNXref, the reconciled namespace of metabolites and biochemical reactions of MetaNetX (SIB Swiss Institute of Bioinformatics). MNXref merges the reactions and metabolites of the main metabolic databases and genome-scale models (e.g. BiGG, KEGG, MetaCyc, ModelSEED, Rhea, Reactome, SABIO-RK, ChEBI, HMDB, LipidMaps, SwissLipids), identifying the same metabolites and reactions across them, so that each reaction and each metabolite has a single MNXref identifier (`MNXR...`, `MNXM...`).

There is one network for each release of MNXref, from 1.0 (2013) to 4.5 (2025), named by its version: `1.0`, `2.0`, `3.0`, `3.1`, `3.2`, `4.0`, `4.1`, `4.2`, `4.3`, `4.4` and `4.5`. In each network, an edge goes from each metabolite of the left side of the equation of a reaction, as written by MNXref, to the reaction, and from the reaction to each metabolite of its right side, with the stoichiometric coefficient and, from version 3.0 on, the generic compartment of the metabolite (`MNXD1` and `MNXD2` for the two sides of a membrane in transport reactions, and in versions 3.x also `MNXD3` to `MNXD5`, `MNXDX` and `BOUNDARY`). The direction of the reactions is not given by MNXref (the equations are written with `=`), so the direction of the edges is only that of the written equation. A metabolite that is transported between compartments appears on both sides of a reaction. Pseudo-metabolites of MNXref are kept as nodes, e.g. `BIOMASS`, `WATER` (the solvent, distinct from the water molecule `MNXM2`) and `MNXM01` (a proton that is not balanced). Reactions without participants (e.g. `EMPTY`) are isolated nodes.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `mnx_id`: the MNXref identifier of the reaction (`MNXR...`) or of the metabolite (`MNXM...`).
- (Node) `is_reaction`: whether the node is a reaction (otherwise it is a metabolite).
- (Node) `name`: the name of the metabolite (empty for reactions, and for metabolites missing from the list of metabolites of the release).
- (Node) `reference`: the source of the identifier, i.e. the first database in which it was found (e.g. `bigg:10FTHF5GLUtl`, `chebi:15378`).
- (Node) `ec`: the EC numbers of the reaction, separated by `;`.
- (Node) `balance`: whether the reaction is balanced (in versions up to 3.2: `true`, `false`, `ambiguous`, `NA` or `redox`; from version 4.0: `B` for balanced, or empty).
- (Node) `is_transport` (versions 4.x): whether the reaction is a transport reaction.
- (Node) `formula`, `charge`, `mass`, `inchikey`: the formula, charge, mass and InChIKey of the metabolite (empty, 0 or NaN if not given; `inchikey` is not given in versions 1.0 and 2.0).
- (Edge) `coefficient`: the stoichiometric coefficient of the metabolite, as given (e.g. `1`, `2`, `0.5`, `(n)`, `(n+1)`).
- (Edge) `compartment` (versions from 3.0): the generic compartment of the metabolite in the reaction.
citations: S. Moretti, V. D. T. Tran, F. Mehl, M. Ibberson, M. Pagni, "MetaNetX/MNXref: unified namespace for metabolites and biochemical reactions in the context of metabolic models." Nucleic Acids Research 49, D570-D574 (2021)

S. Moretti, O. Martin, T. Van Du Tran, A. Bridge, A. Morgat, M. Pagni, "MetaNetX/MNXref – reconciliation of metabolites and biochemical reactions to bring together genome-scale metabolic networks." Nucleic Acids Research 44, D523-D526 (2016)

datasets.name: mexican_drug_trafficking
datasets.description:
Temporal bipartite network of the presence of drug trafficking organizations (DTOs) in the municipalities of Mexico, for each year from 1990 to 2010, from M. Coscia and V. Rios. The data were extracted automatically from web content (Google News articles and other online sources), by detecting, for each year, which DTOs were mentioned together with which municipalities a significant number of times. Nodes are the 2,457 Mexican municipalities and 10 DTOs (the nine largest organizations, plus "Otros", which groups all other DTOs), and an edge with year $t$ connects a DTO to a municipality if the organization was found to operate in the municipality in year $t$; the same pair may be connected by several edges, one for each year. Data before 2004 are less reliable than later data, according to the authors. Municipalities without any detected DTO activity are included as isolated nodes.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `is_organization`: whether the node is a DTO (otherwise it is a municipality).
- (Node) `name`: the name of the DTO, as in the source (e.g. "Sinaloa", "Zetas", "Golfo"), or the INEGI code of the municipality (as a five-digit string with leading zero, e.g. "01001").
- (Node) `state`: the INEGI code of the state of the municipality (-1 for DTOs).
- (Edge) `year`: the year of the activity.[^icon].

[^icon]: Description obtained in part from the [ICON](https://icon.colorado.edu) project.
citations: M. Coscia, V. Rios, "Knowing where and how criminal organizations operate using web content." Proceedings of the 21st ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM), 1412-1421 (2012)

datasets.name: mexican_elite
datasets.description:
The core of the Mexican political elite during most of the 20th century: Mexican presidents and their closest collaborators, from the study of J. Gil-Mendieta and S. Schmidt. Two politicians are connected if they had significant political, kinship, friendship or business ties. After the revolution, the political elite was dominated by the military, but civilians gradually assumed power. The data were distributed on the Pajek datasets page of the book *Exploratory Social Network Analysis with Pajek* (de Nooy, Mrvar and Batagelj), from which this version was obtained.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the name of the politician.
- (Node) `military`: whether the politician had a military professional background (otherwise civilian).
- (Node) `year`: the first year in which the politician occupied a significant governmental position.
citations: J. Gil-Mendieta, S. Schmidt, "The political network in Mexico." Social Networks 18(4), 355-381 (1996)
W. de Nooy, A. Mrvar, V. Batagelj, "Exploratory Social Network Analysis with Pajek." Cambridge University Press (2005)

datasets.name: mice_contacts
datasets.description:
Temporal network of contacts among the house mice (*Mus musculus domesticus*) of a free-ranging population living in a barn near Zurich, Switzerland, studied by the group of Barbara König since 2002. The adult mice carry implanted RFID transponders, and antennas at the entrances of the nest boxes of the barn record when each mouse enters and leaves a nest box. Two mice are in contact while they are in the same nest box at the same time. The data cover the period from 28 February to 1 May 2017, and were released by Bovet et al. with their study of community detection in temporal networks.

Nodes are mice, and each edge is a contact between two mice, so that two mice are connected by as many edges as the number of their contacts. The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `id`: the identifier of the mouse in the data set.
- (Node) `sex`: the sex of the mouse (`male`, `female`, or `unknown` for two mice).
- (Edge) `time` (edges): the start of the contact, in Unix time (rounded down to the second). The source gives the times in seconds from 28 February 2017 00:00:00; this is taken here as local time (CET).
- (Edge) `duration` (edges): the duration of the contact, in seconds.
citations: J. C. Evans, A. K. Lindholm, B. König, "Long-term overlap of social and genetic structure in free-ranging house mice reveals dynamic seasonal and group size effects." Current Zoology 67, 59-69 (2021)
A. Bovet, J.-C. Delvenne, R. Lambiotte, "Flow stability for dynamic community detection." Science Advances 8, eabj3063 (2022)

datasets.name: microns_mm3
datasets.description:
The synaptic connectome of the neurons in a cubic millimeter of mouse visual cortex, from the IARPA MICrONS project: a volume spanning all cortical layers of the primary visual cortex (VISp) and the higher visual areas VISrl, VISal and VISlm of an adult mouse, imaged with serial-section transmission electron microscopy, automatically segmented, with synapses detected automatically, and partially proofread. Nodes are neurons, and a directed edge $(i, j)$ indicates chemical synapses from neuron $i$ (presynaptic) to neuron $j$ (postsynaptic).

The networks are the three versions of the compilation of M. W. Reimann, which contains the synapses between the neurons with a cell body inside the larger of the two imaged subvolumes ("portion 65"), but no synapses from neurons outside it, named after the materialization (version) of the public MICrONS data, "minnie65_public", that they are based on:

- `v1412`: version 3.0.0 of the compilation (August 2025), based on materialization v1412, with 50,948 neurons. It leaves out about 20,000 neurons near the periphery of the volume, whose connectivity is strongly affected by the boundary.
- `v1181`: version 2.0.0 (September 2024), based on materialization v1181, with more proofread neurons and a newer cell type classification than v117 (71,981 neurons).
- `v117`: version 1.0.0 (September 2023), based on materialization v117 (60,048 neurons), with the coarse cell classes of the Allen Institute.

Each version has also a network with one edge per synapse (the "full" representation of the compilation), named `v1412_full`, `v1181_full` and `v117_full`, with the same nodes: two neurons are connected by as many parallel edges as there are synapses between them (11.6, 13.5 and 10.1 million edges).

The version 3.0.0 has also a "distance-dependent control" (`v1412_control`): a random network generated by the author of the compilation as a null model, in which, for each pathway (combination of the layers and synapse classes of the presynaptic and postsynaptic neurons), the connection probability is an exponentially decaying function of the distance between the neurons fitted to the data. It contains only the 45,598 excitatory neurons of `v1412` (the inhibitory neurons are left out of the control), and is unweighted (one edge per connected pair).

All versions leave out a few hundred cell bodies associated with several cell types (merges of several neurons). All connections are included, without threshold on the number of synapses (most connections in the cortex consist of one or two synapses). Note that only a small fraction of the neurons were proofread (see the properties `status_axon` and `status_dendrite`); the axons of the others are mostly incomplete, and their connections may contain errors of the automated segmentation.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `root_id`: the neuron's identifier (root ID) in the MICrONS data of that version.
- (Node) `cell_type`: the type of the neuron, predicted from features of its soma and nucleus: in `v1412` and `v1181`, the morphological type (m-type; e.g. `L2a`, `L4b`, `L5ET`, `L6tall-a` for excitatory neurons; `PTC`, `DTC`, `STC` and `ITC` for perisomatic-targeting, distal-targeting, sparsely-targeting and inhibitory-targeting inhibitory neurons); in `v117`, the coarse cell class (e.g. `23P`, `4P`, `5P_IT`, `6CT`, `BC`, `MC`).
- (Node) `classification_system` (`v1412` and `v1181`): `excitatory_neuron` or `inhibitory_neuron`.
- (Node) `synapse_class` (`v1412`): whether the neuron is excitatory (`EXC`) or inhibitory (`INH`).
- (Node) `layer` (`v1412`): the cortical layer of the neuron (`2` to `6`), derived from its type; empty for inhibitory neurons.
- (Node) `tentative_region` (`v117`): the visual area of the neuron (`visp`, `visrl`, `visal` or `vislm`), which the author of the compilation warns is only a rough estimate.
- (Node) `status_axon`, `status_dendrite`: whether the neuron's axon and dendrite were proofread (`t`) or not (`f`), for the neurons in the proofreading table of MICrONS; in `v117`, the proofreading status of the public release of the time: `non` (not proofread), `clean` (false merges removed) or `extended` (also false splits corrected); empty for the neurons that are not in that table, which were not proofread.
- (Node) `volume` (`v1412` and `v1181`): the volume of the neuron's nucleus, in µm³.
- (Node) `x`, `y`, `z`: the position of the neuron's soma, in µm ($y$ increases with the cortical depth).
- (Edge) `weight`: the number of synapses from $i$ to $j$ (not in the `_full` networks and in `v1412_control`).
- (Edge) `total_size`, `mean_size` (`v1181` and `v117`): the sum and the mean of the sizes of these synapses, as given by the synapse table of MICrONS (in voxels).
- (Edge) `synapse_id`, `size` (`_full` networks): the identifier of the synapse in the synapse table of MICrONS, and its size (in voxels).
- (Edge) `syn_x`, `syn_y`, `syn_z`, `soma_distance` (`v1181_full` and `v117_full`): the position of the synapse, in µm, and its distance from the soma of the postsynaptic neuron, in µm.

In `v1412_control`, the nodes have the properties `root_id`, `cell_type` (the m-type), `synapse_class` (`EXC`), `layer`, `volume` and `x`, `y`, `z`, as above.

The compilation's "valid" flag of the neurons, the identifiers of their cell bodies (supervoxel and nucleus IDs), and, in `v117`, their degrees (which the networks give), are left out. In the `_full` networks, the offsets of the synapses from the soma of the postsynaptic neuron (which follow from their positions) are left out. In `v1412_control`, a second set of coordinates of the neurons (`X`, `Y`, `Z`, not documented) and a few columns that are empty for almost all neurons (morphologies, spines, in-degrees) are left out.
citations: The MICrONS Consortium, "Functional connectomics spanning multiple areas of mouse visual cortex." Nature 640, 435-447 (2025)
M. W. Reimann, "Connectomics of (part of) the MICrONS mm3 dataset." Zenodo, version 3.0.0 (2025)

datasets.name: microsoft_concept
datasets.description:
Network of "IsA" relations between concepts and instances from the Microsoft Concept Graph, released by Microsoft Research in 2016. The data derive from Probase, a knowledge base that was built by automatically extracting IsA relations from a corpus of billions of web pages with syntactic patterns, and their frequencies. This is the core IsA data set of the public release, containing 33,377,320 relations between 5,376,526 concepts and 12,501,527 instances (named entities, objects, actions, attributes, etc.).

An edge connects a concept to an instance of it, with a weight equal to the number of times the relation was extracted. Nodes are identified by their (lowercase) text, so a term that appears both as a concept and as an instance is represented by a single node; therefore the network is not strictly bipartite. Edges are undirected, and the direction of the relation is not stored.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the text of the concept or instance.
- (Edge) `count`: the number of times the IsA relation was extracted from the web corpus.
citations: Z. Wang et al., "An Inference Approach to Basic Level of Categorization." Proc. ACM Internat. Conf. on Info. and Know. Management (CIKM 2015)

datasets.name: mind_news
datasets.description:
Bipartite networks of the users and news articles of the Microsoft News website, from the large version of the MIND data set (Microsoft News Dataset), compiled by Wu et al. from the anonymized behavior logs of Microsoft News. One million users who had clicked at least five news articles in the six weeks from October 12 to November 22, 2019 were sampled at random, and their ids were replaced by anonymous ones. The logs of the users consist of impressions: each impression is a list of news articles that were shown to a user at some time, with the ones that the user clicked marked. The impressions of November 9 to 14 form the training set of the data set, those of November 15 the validation set, and those of November 16 to 22 the test set, for which the clicks are not given. Each impression also comes with the click history of the user, the articles the user clicked before (in the first four weeks, from October 12 to November 8), without their times. The data set contains 4,979,946 impressions of 876,956 users and 130,379 news articles.

- `clicks`: an edge connects a user to a news article that the user clicked: once for each click in an impression of the training or validation set (3,958,501 clicks, with their times), and once for each article in the user's click history (18,131,836 pairs, without times; the histories given with the impressions of a user were merged, keeping each user-article pair once).
- `impressions`: an edge connects a user to a news article for each time the article was shown to the user in an impression (190,707,932 in all), with whether the user clicked it (unknown for the test set).

Both networks contain all the users and all the news articles of the data set. Left out are the abstracts of the articles and the entities (linked to Wikidata) recognized in their titles and abstracts, with their embeddings, as well as the smaller versions of the data set (MIND-small, a sample of 50,000 of the users, and MIND-demo), which are subsets of this one.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `is_user`: whether the node is a user (otherwise a news article).
- (Node) `name`: the anonymized id of the user, or the id of the news article in the data set.
- (Node) `category`, `subcategory` (news articles): the category and subcategory of the article on Microsoft News (empty for users).
- (Node) `title` (news articles): the title of the article (empty for users).
- (Node) `url` (news articles): the address of the article at the time of the release of the data set (empty for users).
- (Edge) `time`: the time of the impression, as Unix time (the times are given without a time zone, and taken here as UTC; -1 for the click histories).
- (Edge) `impression`: the number of the impression within its set (-1 for the click histories).
- (Edge) `split`: the set of the impression: 0 for training, 1 for validation, 2 for test (-1 for the click histories).
- (Edge) `clicked` (`impressions`): 1 if the user clicked the article, 0 if not, -1 if unknown (test set).
citations: F. Wu, Y. Qiao, J.-H. Chen, C. Wu, T. Qi, J. Lian, D. Liu, X. Xie, J. Gao, W. Wu, M. Zhou, "MIND: A Large-scale Dataset for News Recommendation." Proceedings of the 58th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL), 3597-3606 (2020)

datasets.name: mislove_osn
datasets.description:
Social graphs of four large online social networks, obtained by A. Mislove and collaborators by crawling the publicly accessible user links of each site with automated scripts. Nodes are users and a directed edge $(i,j)$ indicates that user $i$ lists user $j$ as a friend or contact. The four networks are:

- `flickr`: the photo sharing site Flickr, crawled on 9 January 2007 through its API, by following forward links from seed users. It covers an estimated 26.9% of all users; 62.0% of the links are reciprocated.
- `livejournal`: the blogging site LiveJournal, crawled on 9–11 December 2006 through its API by following both forward and reverse links, which covers the entire large weakly connected component, an estimated 95.4% of all users; 73.5% of the links are reciprocated.
- `orkut`: the social networking site Orkut run by Google, crawled between 3 October and 11 November 2006 by HTML screen-scraping. The crawl was stopped after reaching 3,072,441 users, an estimated 11.3% of all users, and links to uncrawled users are disregarded. Orkut friendships are undirected and require the consent of both users, but they are given as directed, so each friendship appears as two reciprocal edges.
- `youtube`: the video sharing site YouTube, crawled on 15 January 2007 through its API, by following forward links. The fraction of users covered is unknown; 79.1% of the links are reciprocated.

The data also include the memberships of users in user groups (special interest groups created by users; in LiveJournal they were inferred from the interests specified by users). The user IDs and group IDs were anonymized. In the four social networks above, the memberships are given as a node property, and the memberships of users absent from the social graph (e.g. 11,872 Flickr users with 33,901 memberships) are not included. They are included in the bipartite user-group membership networks of the two smaller sites:

- `flickr_groups`: memberships of Flickr users in Flickr groups.
- `youtube_groups`: memberships of YouTube users in YouTube groups.

(The membership networks of LiveJournal and Orkut, with about 112 and 327 million memberships, are only available as node properties.)

Undirected versions of the `orkut` and `youtube` networks (the largest connected component, in the case of YouTube), with communities derived from the group memberships, are the networks `orkut` and `youtube` of the entry `soc_net_comms`.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `vid`: the anonymized user ID (or, in the membership networks, the anonymized user or group ID).
- (Node) `groups` (social networks): the list of IDs of the groups of which the user is a member (empty if the user is not a member of any group).
- (Node) `is_group` (membership networks): true for groups, false for users.
citations: A. Mislove et al., "Measurement and Analysis of Online Social Networks." Proc. ACM/Usenix Internet Measurement Conference (IMC), 29-42 (2007).

datasets.name: mist
datasets.description:
The Molecular Interaction Search Tool (MIST) is a comprehensive resource of molecular interactions, assembled from several primary sources. This dataset contains the networks of the following species:

   1. Homo sapiens (Human)
   2. Drosophila melanogaster (Fly)
   3. Mus musculus (Mouse)
   4. Caenorhabditis elegans (Worm)
   5. Rattus norvegicus (Rat)
   6. Saccharomyces cerevisiae (Baker's yeast)
   7. Schizosaccharomyces pombe (Fission yeast)
   8. Danio rerio (Zebrafish)
   9. Xenopus tropicalis (Western clawed frog)

The database contains four kinds of interactions:

   1. Protein-protein interaction (PPI): “PPI” refers to physical interactions between two or more proteins.
   2. Interologs (PPI): Interactions predicted based on PPI data obtained for orthologous proteins.
   3. Genetic Interactions: Indicate that the effects of mutations in one gene can be modified by mutation of another gene.
   4. Genetic Interologs: Interactions predicted based on genetic interaction data obtained for orthologous proteins

There is one network for each species and kind of interaction, named as `<kind>_<species>` (e.g. `ppi_human` or `genetic_interolog_fly`), with the kinds `ppi`, `ppi_interolog`, `genetic` and `genetic_interolog` (there is no genetic network for the western clawed frog, and no genetic interolog network for the fission yeast). Nodes are genes (or the proteins they encode), identified by their NCBI Entrez Gene IDs, and an undirected edge connects two genes for which MIST lists an interaction of the given kind; when the same pair is listed in several records, only one of them is kept. The files of a species also contain some interactions with genes of other species (e.g. about 8% of the records of the human PPI file), which are included. The interolog files of a species contain both the interactions predicted for its genes and those predicted for the genes of other species (including Xenopus laevis) from its data, and all of them are included. The species of each gene is given by the vertex property `tax_id` (NCBI Taxonomy ID).
citations: Yanhui Hu, Arunachalam Vinayagam, Ankita Nand, Aram Comjean, Verena Chung, Tong Hao, Stephanie E Mohr, and Norbert Perrimon, “Molecular Interaction Search Tool (MIST): an integrated resource for mining gene and protein interaction data.” Nucleic Acids Res, 46, D1, Pp. D567-D574 (2017)

datasets.name: modern_math
datasets.description:
Friendship choices among school superintendents in Allegheny County (Pennsylvania, USA), from R. O. Carlson's study of the diffusion of the "modern math" teaching method in the late 1950s and early 1960s. The superintendents of school systems combining elementary and secondary programs, who had been at least two years in office, were interviewed (61 of 68), and 51 of them had adopted the method by 1963. Among other things, they were asked "Among the chief school administrators in Allegheny County, who are your three best friends?". The network contains the 38 interviewed superintendents who adopted the method and were in office at least one year before the first adoption. The friendship choices of superintendents who did not receive any choices themselves were not included by the researcher, so they appear as isolated nodes. The data were distributed on the Pajek datasets page of the book *Exploratory Social Network Analysis with Pajek* (de Nooy, Mrvar and Batagelj), from which this version was obtained.

- `directed`: the friendship choices, as directed edges from the superintendent making the choice to the chosen one.
- `symmetrized`: the symmetrized network, in which two superintendents are connected if at least one of them chose the other as a friend.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the identifier of the superintendent ("v1" is the first adopter).
- (Node) `adoption`: the year of adoption of the method by the superintendent's school system (1: 1958, 2: 1959, 3: 1960, and so on).
citations: R. O. Carlson, "Adoption of Educational Innovations." Center for the Advanced Study of Educational Administration, University of Oregon, Eugene (1965)
W. de Nooy, A. Mrvar, V. Batagelj, "Exploratory Social Network Analysis with Pajek." Cambridge University Press (2005)

datasets.name: monarch_kg
datasets.description:
The knowledge graph of the Monarch Initiative, which integrates data on genes, diseases and phenotypes across species, for the study of genetic diseases and model organisms. Nodes are biological entities of many kinds, given by their Biolink Model category, e.g. genes (of human and of model organisms such as mouse, rat, zebrafish, fruit fly, *C. elegans*, yeast), diseases (Mondo Disease Ontology), phenotypes (Human Phenotype Ontology and the phenotype ontologies of other species), genotypes, variants, anatomical entities, cell types, biological processes, molecular functions and cellular components (Gene Ontology), pathways (Reactome), chemicals and publications. A directed edge is an association between two entities with a Biolink predicate, e.g. a gene `has_phenotype` a phenotype, a gene `causes` a disease, a gene is `orthologous_to` another, a gene `interacts_with` another (STRING, BioGRID and other interaction databases), a gene `expressed_in` an anatomical entity, a term `subclass_of` a more general term of an ontology. The data are integrated from dozens of sources (e.g. the Alliance of Genome Resources, OMIM, Orphanet, ClinVar, ClinGen, HPO annotations, Gene Ontology annotations, PANTHER, Reactome, STRING, BioGRID, the PHENIO ontology), and both nodes and edges are normalized to common identifiers.

The Monarch knowledge graph is released monthly. One release per year is included, the first of each year (from the first release in the current format, of September 2023), and the latest one:

- `2023-09-28`: 830,288 nodes and 8,076,791 edges (according to its statistics),
- `2024-01-13`,
- `2025-01-15`,
- `2026-01-11`,
- `2026-10-07`: 1,670,861 nodes and 16,433,147 edges.

Left out are the qualifiers of the edges (e.g. the frequency, onset or sex of a phenotype in a disease, the species or disease context), their supporting publications and evidence codes, and the synonyms, cross-references and descriptions of the nodes.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `id`: the identifier of the entity, as a compact URI, e.g. `HGNC:11998` (the human gene TP53), `MONDO:0007254` (breast cancer), `HP:0001250` (seizure).
- (Node) `category`: the Biolink category of the entity, e.g. `biolink:Gene`, `biolink:Disease`, `biolink:PhenotypicFeature`.
- (Node) `name`: the name of the entity (empty if none).
- (Node) `symbol`: the symbol of the gene (empty for other entities and if none).
- (Node) `taxon`: the NCBI taxonomy identifier of the species of the entity, e.g. `NCBITaxon:9606` (empty if none).
- (Node) `taxon_label`: the name of the species, e.g. `Homo sapiens` (empty if none).
- (Edge) `predicate`: the Biolink predicate of the association, e.g. `biolink:has_phenotype`, `biolink:causes`, `biolink:interacts_with`.
- (Edge) `category`: the Biolink category of the association, e.g. `biolink:GeneToPhenotypicFeatureAssociation`.
- (Edge) `primary_knowledge_source`: the original source of the association, e.g. `infores:omim`, `infores:string`.
- (Edge) `knowledge_level`: e.g. `knowledge_assertion`, `predicated` or `not_provided` (empty in releases without it).
- (Edge) `agent_type`: the kind of agent that made the assertion, e.g. `manual_agent`, `automated_agent` (empty in releases without it).
- (Edge) `negated`: whether the association is negated (e.g. a gene that does *not* have a phenotype).
- (Node) `release` (graph): the date of the release.
- (Node) `dangling_nodes` (graph): the number of nodes that appear in edges but not in the list of nodes of the release (they have only an `id`).
citations: T. A. Putman et al., "The Monarch Initiative in 2024: an analytic platform integrating phenotypes, genes and diseases across species." Nucleic Acids Research 52, D938-D949 (2024)

datasets.name: montreal
datasets.description:
Network of relationships among 35 street gangs active in Montreal, Canada, studied by K. Descormiers and C. Morselli. The data were collected in 2007 through focus group interviews with 20 male youth gang members (aged 14 to 18) residing in the Centre jeunesse de Montréal–Institut universitaire, the city's main youth correctional institution, who identified the active gangs and the relations among them. Nodes are gangs and an edge indicates that a relationship between two gangs was reported. The relations studied by the authors are both alliances and conflicts, but the data, as reconstructed from the article and distributed with UCINET, are binary and do not distinguish between them; the original network is directed, but the distributed version is undirected.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the name of the gang.
- (Node) `Allegiances`: the gang coalition, with 1 = Bloods, 2 = Crips, 3 = other.
- (Node) `Ethnicity`: the main ethnicity of the gang, with 1 = Hispanic, 2 = Afro-Canadian, 3 = Caucasian, 4 = Asian, 5 = no main association or mixed.
- (Node) `Territories`: the territory of the gang, with 1 = downtown, 2 = east, 3 = west.

In all attributes, missing data are coded as 99.
citations: K. Descormiers, and C. Morselli, "Alliances, conflicts, and contradictions in Montreal’s street gang landscape." International Criminal Justice Review 21(3), 297-314 (2011)

datasets.name: moreno_sheep
datasets.description:
Dominance interactions (wins and losses) among 28 female bighorn sheep (Ovis canadensis) on the National Bison Range in western Montana (USA), observed by C. C. Hass in 1984. The data were distributed by L. C. Freeman on his network data page at the University of California, Irvine (no longer online), from which this version was obtained via the Internet Archive.

A directed edge (i, j) indicates that sheep i was observed dominating sheep j.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the identifier of the sheep.
- (Node) `age`: the age of the sheep in years (sheep with an age of 9 are at least 9 years old, and may be older).
- (Edge) `weight`: the number of occasions on which i was observed dominating j.
citations: C. C. Hass. "Social status in female bighorn sheep (Ovis canadensis): Expression, development and reproductive correlates." J. of Zoology 225(3), 509-523 (1991)

datasets.name: moreno_sociograms
datasets.description: Relationships between pupils in a classroom, from the sociograms of the "class structure" of eight school classes, from the 1st to the 8th grade, published by J. L. Moreno and H. H. Jennings in 1934, as transcribed by M. Grandjean. There is one network for each class, named `grade_1` to `grade_8`. Nodes are pupils, identified by their initials in the original sociograms (vertex property `name`; pupils with the same initials are distinguished by a "1" and a "2"), and a directed edge exists if the source wants to sit next to the target. Each child could only choose two others (in the transcription, a few pupils have one or three choices).
citations: Jacob Levy Moreno, “Who Shall Survive? A New Approach to the Problem of Human Interrelations”, Washington D.C.: Nervous and Mental Disease Publishing Co.

datasets.name: moreno_taro
datasets.description:
Gift-giving relationships (taro exchange) among 22 households in a Papuan village of the Orokaiva, studied by E. Schwimmer, who points out how these ties define the appropriate persons to mediate the act of asking for or receiving assistance among group members. P. Hage and F. Harary (1983) used the data to illustrate a Hamiltonian cycle. The data were distributed by L. C. Freeman on his network data page at the University of California, Irvine (no longer online), from which this version was obtained via the Internet Archive.

An undirected edge (i, j) indicates a gift-giving relationship between households i and j (the source matrix is symmetric).
citations: E. Schwimmer, "Exchange in the social structure of the Orokaiva." St. Martin's Press (1973)
P. Hage, F. Harary, "Structural Models in Anthropology." Cambridge University Press (1983)

datasets.name: mosquito_ppi
datasets.description:
A network of predicted protein-protein interactions of the yellow fever mosquito *Aedes aegypti*, the main vector of dengue virus, from Guo et al. The interactions were predicted with the interolog method: experimentally determined interactions in three model organisms, the yeast *S. cerevisiae* (47,783 interactions from co-immunoprecipitation and yeast two-hybrid screens), the fruit fly *D. melanogaster* (20,405 two-hybrid interactions) and the nematode *C. elegans* (4,736 literature-mined and two-hybrid interactions), were transferred to the mosquito proteins orthologous to the interacting proteins. Nodes are mosquito proteins (genes), and an undirected edge connects two proteins predicted to interact, weighted by the confidence of the prediction. The confidence scores combine the confidence of the original interaction in the model organism (estimated from statistical and topological predictors) with the InParanoid orthology score. The network has 64,449 predicted interactions among 6,263 proteins; 316 of the edges are self-loops (proteins predicted to interact with themselves).

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the VectorBase gene identifier of the protein (e.g. "AAEL010168").
- (Edge) `confidence`: the confidence score of the predicted interaction, between 0 and 1 (average 0.32).
- (Edge) `origin`: the model organism(s) from which the interaction was transferred ("yeast", "fly", "worm", or combinations such as "yeast/fly").
citations: X. Guo, Y. Xu, G. Bian, A. D. Pike, Y. Xie, Z. Xi, "Response of the mosquito protein interaction network to dengue infection." BMC Genomics 11, 380 (2010)

datasets.name: mouse_mesoscale
datasets.description:
Networks of axonal projections between regions of the mouse brain, from the Allen Mouse Brain Connectivity Atlas of Oh et al. (Allen Institute for Brain Science). In each of 469 experiments, an adeno-associated viral tracer expressing EGFP was injected into one location of the right hemisphere of a C57BL/6J mouse, and the fluorescently labeled axons were imaged brain-wide by serial two-photon tomography, registered to the Allen Reference Atlas, and segmented. The brain was divided into 295 non-overlapping regions (plus fiber tracts) in each hemisphere.

- `projections`: bipartite network between the 469 injection experiments and the 592 target regions (296 per hemisphere, including "fiber tracts"), from Supplementary Table 2. An edge connects an experiment to each target region where projections were detected, weighted by the normalized projection volume (the number of segmented signal pixels in the target region divided by that in the injection volume). Target regions are distinguished by hemisphere, ipsilateral (right) or contralateral (left) to the injection. 106 entries of the source table have the value -1, which is not documented, and are omitted.
- `model`: directed network of the 213 regions on each hemisphere (426 nodes) from Supplementary Tables 3 and 4, obtained by the authors by fitting a linear model of connectivity, in which the projection signal of each experiment is a combination of the projections of the source regions covered by its injection. Edges point from a source region (on the right hemisphere) to an ipsilateral or contralateral target region, for every non-zero fitted connection strength (32,822 edges, 16,954 of them ipsilateral). Nodes on the left (contralateral) hemisphere therefore have no outgoing edges.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `name` (regions): the region acronym (for experiment nodes, the image series identifier) in the Allen Reference Atlas.
- (Node) `full_name` (regions): the region name.
- (Node) `major_region` (regions): the major brain division (e.g. "Isocortex", "Thalamus"; acronyms such as "ISOCORTEX" or "TH" in `projections`).
- (Node) `hemisphere` (regions): "ipsilateral" (right) or "contralateral" (left).
- (Node) `voxel_count` (regions): the volume of the region in voxels of the reference atlas (100 micrometers on each side).
- (Node) `is_injection` (`projections`): whether the node is an injection experiment (otherwise it is a region).
- (Node) `image_series_id`, `specimen` (experiments, in `projections`): the identifiers of the experiment and the animal.
- (Node) `primary_structure`, `secondary_structure` (experiments, in `projections`): the regions containing the injection site.
- (Node) `injection_volume` (experiments, in `projections`): in cubic millimeters.
- (Node) `major_region` (experiments, in `projections`): the major division of the injection site.
- (Edge) `weight`: the normalized projection volume (`projections`) or the fitted normalized connection strength (`model`).
- (Edge) `pvalue`: the p-value of the fitted connection strength (NaN when it could not be computed) (`model` only).
- (Edge) `distance`: the distance between the centers of mass of the two regions, in micrometers (`model` only).
citations: S. W. Oh et al., "A mesoscale connectome of the mouse brain." Nature 508, 207-214 (2014)

datasets.name: mouse_retina
datasets.description:
Undirected network of physical contacts between neurons of the inner plexiform layer of the mouse retina, from the connectomic reconstruction of Helmstaedter et al. A block of retina (about 114 x 80 x 132 micrometres) was imaged by serial block-face electron microscopy; the neurons were reconstructed by combining skeleton tracing by about 200 (crowd-sourced) student annotators with machine-learning volume segmentation, and the contacts between the reconstructed cells were then detected automatically. Nodes are cells (950 classified neurons, plus 173 cells without annotations), and each edge is one contact between two cells, located in space and weighted by its area, so that most pairs of cells are joined by many parallel edges (577,350 contacts between 90,811 pairs of cells). Contacts are not necessarily synapses.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the cell identifier.
- (Node) `coarse`: the coarse cell class ("gc" ganglion cell, "bc" bipolar cell, "nac" narrow-field amacrine cell, "mwac" medium/wide-field amacrine cell, "other", or "NA").
- (Node) `designation`: the cell type assigned in the publication (e.g. "bc48-88", "gc10-40").
- (Node) `volgyi_type` and `macneil_type`: the corresponding ganglion cell type in the classification of Völgyi et al. and amacrine cell type in the classification of MacNeil et al.
- (Node) `certainty`: the certainty of the classification ("H" high, "M" medium, "L" low).
- (Node) `x`, `y`, `z`: the position of the cell body, in micrometres (0 for the unannotated cells).
- (Edge) `x`, `y`, `z`: the position of the contact, in micrometres.
- (Edge) `area`: the contact area, in square micrometres.

The data were obtained by OpenConnectome from the processed version of the supplementary data in E. Jonas' circuitdata repository. The data were obtained from the graph collection of the Open Connectome Project (now NeuroData), whose servers are offline, via the Internet Archive.
citations: M. Helmstaedter, K. L. Briggman, S. C. Turaga, V. Jain, H. S. Seung, W. Denk, "Connectomic reconstruction of the inner plexiform layer in the mouse retina." Nature 500, 168-174 (2013)

datasets.name: mouse_visual_cortex
datasets.description:
Directed networks of synaptic connections in the primary visual cortex of the mouse, from Bock et al. The orientation preferences of neurons were first characterized in vivo by two-photon calcium imaging; the same tissue was then imaged by large-scale serial-section transmission electron microscopy, and the axons of functionally characterized pyramidal neurons were traced to their postsynaptic targets. Edges point from a presynaptic (characterized pyramidal) neuron to its postsynaptic target, and are weighted by the number of synapses.

- `full`: all reconstructed connections: 195 nodes, including 13 characterized pyramidal neurons and their postsynaptic targets, which are mostly dendritic fragments (138) and cell bodies within the EM volume (44).
- `subset`: a smaller network of 29 nodes (11 characterized pyramidal neurons and 18 targets), labeled in the source as corresponding to Figure 5b of the publication (the targets receiving input from the characterized neurons shown there).

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `type`: the kind of node ("Characterized pyramidal neuron", "Dendritic fragment", or "Cell body in EM volume").
- (Node) `target_type`: whether the node is an inhibitory or excitatory postsynaptic target ("NA" for the characterized neurons).
- (Edge) `weight`: the number of synapses.

The data were obtained from the graph collection of the Open Connectome Project (now NeuroData), whose servers are offline, via the Internet Archive.
citations: D. D. Bock et al., "Network anatomy and in vivo physiology of visual cortical neurons." Nature 471, 177-182 (2011)

datasets.name: moviegalaxies
datasets.description:
Character networks of 773 films released between 1915 and 2012, from the Moviegalaxies website, created by J. Kaminski, M. Schober, R. Albaladejo, O. Zastupailo and C. Hidalgo. The networks were extracted automatically from the movie scripts with a script parser: nodes are characters of a film (as named in the script), and two characters are connected if they appear in the same scene, with a weight equal to the number of scenes in which they appear together. Each film is a separate network, identified by its Moviegalaxies ID.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Graph) `movie_title`, `imdb_id`, `release_date` (year), `slug`: the title of the film, its IMDb identifier, its release year, and its identifier on the Moviegalaxies website.
- (Node) `label` (nodes): the name of the character, as written in the script.
- (Node) `vid`: the node ID in the source file.
- (Node) `viz`: the visualization attributes (color, position, size) from the source GEXF file.
- (Node) `movie_id`: the Moviegalaxies ID of the film.
- (Edge) `weight`: the number of scenes in which the two characters appear together.
- (Edge) `label` (edges): the edge ID in the source file.
- (Edge) `movie_id`: the Moviegalaxies ID of the film.
citations: J. Kaminski et al., "Moviegalaxies - Social Networks in Movies." https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/T4HBA3, Harvard Dataverse, V3 (2018)

datasets.name: movielens_10m_tags
datasets.description:
A bipartite network of the tags that users of the online movie recommender service MovieLens applied to movies, from the MovieLens 10M data set released by GroupLens Research (University of Minnesota) in January 2009. MovieLens users can annotate movies with free-text tags, typically a single word or short phrase whose meaning is determined by the user. The data set contains 95,580 tag applications made between December 2005 and January 2009 by 4,009 users, who were selected at random (all selected users had rated at least 20 movies) and anonymized. Each node is a tag (a distinct tag string, case-sensitive) or a movie, and each edge is one application of the tag to the movie by some user, so that the same tag applied to the same movie by several users appears as multiple edges. Only movies that received at least one tag are included.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `is_tag`: whether the node is a tag (otherwise it is a movie).
- (Node) `name`: the tag string, or the title of the movie (including its year of release, as entered in MovieLens).
- (Node) `movie_id`: the MovieLens movie id (-1 for tags).
- (Node) `genres`: the list of genres of the movie.
- (Edge) `user`: the anonymized id of the user who applied the tag.
- (Edge) `time`: the time when the tag was applied, as Unix time.
citations: F. M. Harper, J. A. Konstan, "The MovieLens Datasets: History and Context." ACM Transactions on Interactive Intelligent Systems 5(4), 19 (2015)

datasets.name: movielens_32m
datasets.description:
Bipartite networks of the users and movies of the online movie recommender service MovieLens, from the MovieLens 32M data set released by GroupLens Research (University of Minnesota) in October 2023. The data set contains 32,000,204 ratings and 2,000,072 tag applications made between January 1995 and October 2023 by 200,948 users, who were selected at random among those who had rated at least 20 movies, and whose ids were anonymized; no demographic information about the users is given.

- `ratings`: users and movies, where each edge is the rating that a user gave to a movie, from 0.5 to 5 stars in half-star steps (a user rates a movie at most once). The network contains all 87,585 movies of the data set (those with at least one rating or tag), of which 84,432 were rated; the 3,153 movies that were only tagged have no edges.
- `tags`: tags and movies, where each edge is one application of a tag (a free-text word or short phrase, case-sensitive) to a movie by a user, so that the same tag applied to the same movie by several users (or several times) gives multiple edges. Only the movies with at least one tag are included.

The older MovieLens data sets (100K, 1M, 10M, 20M, 25M) are in the entry `movielens_ratings`; the tags of the 10M data set are in `movielens_10m_tags`.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `movie_id`: the MovieLens id of the movie (its page is `https://movielens.org/movies/<movie_id>`; -1 for the other nodes).
- (Node) `title`: the title of the movie, including its year of release.
- (Node) `genres`: the list of its genres (empty if none is listed).
- (Node) `imdb_id` and `tmdb_id`: its ids in IMDb and in The Movie Database (-1 if not given).
- (Node) `is_user` (`ratings`): whether the node is a user (otherwise a movie).
- (Node) `user_id` (`ratings`): the anonymized id of the user (-1 for movies).
- (Node) `is_tag` (`tags`): whether the node is a tag (otherwise a movie).
- (Node) `name` (`tags`): the tag string (empty for movies).
- (Edge) `rating` (`ratings`): the rating in stars.
- (Edge) `time`: the time of the rating (`ratings`), or when the tag was applied (`tags`), as Unix time.
- (Edge) `user` (`tags`): the anonymized id of the user who applied the tag (the same as `user_id` in `ratings`).
citations: F. M. Harper, J. A. Konstan, "The MovieLens Datasets: History and Context." ACM Transactions on Interactive Intelligent Systems 5(4), 19 (2015)

datasets.name: movielens_ratings
datasets.description:
Bipartite networks of the users and movies of the online movie recommender service MovieLens, from the MovieLens data sets released by GroupLens Research (University of Minnesota) between 1998 and 2019. In each data set, the users were selected at random among those who had rated at least 20 movies, and their ids were anonymized. Each edge is the rating that a user gave to a movie (a user rates a movie at most once).

- `100k`: MovieLens 100K (released in April 1998), 100,000 ratings of 1,682 movies by 943 users, on a scale from 1 to 5 stars, made between September 1997 and April 1998 (users who had less than 20 ratings or did not give complete demographic information were removed by GroupLens).
- `1m`: MovieLens 1M (released in February 2003), 1,000,209 ratings of 3,706 movies by 6,040 users who joined MovieLens in 2000, on a scale from 1 to 5 stars, made between April 2000 and February 2003.
- `10m`: MovieLens 10M (released in January 2009), 10,000,054 ratings of 10,677 movies by 69,878 users, made between January 1995 and January 2009, on a scale from 0.5 to 5 stars in half-star steps (whole stars only before February 2003).
- `20m`: MovieLens 20M (released in October 2016), 20,000,263 ratings of 26,744 movies by 138,493 users, made between January 1995 and March 2015.
- `25m`: MovieLens 25M (released in November 2019), 25,000,095 ratings of 59,047 movies by 162,541 users, made between January 1995 and November 2019.
- `20m_tags` and `25m_tags`: the tag applications of the 20M and 25M data sets (465,564 and 1,093,360), as bipartite networks of tags and movies, where each edge is one application of a tag (a free-text word or short phrase, case-sensitive) to a movie by a user, so that the same tag applied to the same movie by several users (or several times) gives multiple edges. Only the movies with at least one tag are included.

Each rating network contains all the movies listed in its data set, including those that only received tags (which have no edges). Left out are the "tag genome" relevance scores of the 20M and 25M data sets, the cross-validation splits of the 100K and 10M data sets, and the release dates and IMDb links of the 100K data set. The tags of the 10M data set are in the entry `movielens_10m_tags`, and the most recent data set (32M) is in the entry `movielens_32m`.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `movie_id`: the MovieLens id of the movie (-1 for the other nodes).
- (Node) `title`: the title of the movie, including its year of release.
- (Node) `genres`: the list of its genres (empty if none is listed).
- (Node) `imdb_id`, `tmdb_id` (`20m`, `25m`, `20m_tags` and `25m_tags`): the ids of the movie in IMDb and in The Movie Database (-1 if not given).
- (Node) `is_user` (rating networks): whether the node is a user (otherwise a movie).
- (Node) `user_id` (rating networks): the anonymized id of the user (-1 for movies).
- (Node) `gender`, `age`, `occupation`, `zip` (`100k` and `1m`): the demographic information given by the user (empty for movies); `gender` is "M" or "F". In `100k`, `age` is the age in years; in `1m`, it is the lower bound of the user's age group (1 for "under 18", 18, 25, 35, 45, 50 and 56 for "56+"). In both, -1 for movies.
- (Node) `is_tag` (`20m_tags` and `25m_tags`): whether the node is a tag (otherwise a movie).
- (Node) `name` (`20m_tags` and `25m_tags`): the tag string (empty for movies).
- (Edge) `rating` (rating networks): the rating in stars.
- (Edge) `time`: the time of the rating (rating networks), or when the tag was applied (`20m_tags` and `25m_tags`), as Unix time.
- (Edge) `user` (`20m_tags` and `25m_tags`): the anonymized id of the user who applied the tag (the same as `user_id` in the rating network of the same data set).
citations: F. M. Harper, J. A. Konstan, "The MovieLens Datasets: History and Context." ACM Transactions on Interactive Intelligent Systems 5(4), 19 (2015)

datasets.name: movies_tmdb
datasets.description:
Bipartite networks of movies and the people credited in them, and of movies and the keywords describing them, from "The Movies Dataset" assembled by R. Banik and published on Kaggle (version 7, November 2017). The dataset covers the about 45,000 movies listed in the full MovieLens dataset of GroupLens (movies released on or before July 2017); their metadata and credits were collected from the API of The Movie Database (TMDB), a community-edited online movie database. Persons are identified by their TMDB person ids, movies by their TMDB movie ids.

- `cast`: a node is either a movie or an actor, and an edge connects an actor to a movie in whose cast the actor is credited.
- `crew`: a node is either a movie or a crew member (director, writer, producer, composer, editor, etc.), and an edge connects a person to a movie in which the person has a crew credit.
- `keywords`: a node is either a movie or a keyword (a short descriptive tag assigned to movies by TMDB contributors, e.g. "based on novel", "time travel", "duringcreditsstinger"), and an edge connects a keyword to a movie tagged with it.

In `cast` and `crew`, each edge is one TMDB credit; a person credited more than once in the same movie (e.g. playing two characters, or as both director and writer) is connected to it by parallel edges. In `keywords`, each edge is one keyword assignment (there are no parallel edges). Only movies with at least one credit or keyword of the respective kind are included (2,415 of the 45,433 movies with credits have an empty cast list, and 772 an empty crew list; 14,340 of the 45,432 movies in the keyword file have no keywords). Movie metadata is given as in the source (the values of `budget`, `revenue` and `runtime` are 0 when unknown); the TMDB genres of a movie are given in `genres`.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `is_movie`: whether the node is a movie (otherwise it is a person, or a keyword in `keywords`).
- (Node) `tmdb_id`: the TMDB id of the movie, person or keyword.
