datasets.name: odlis
datasets.description:
The network of the terms of the *Online Dictionary of Library and Information Science* (ODLIS) by J. M. Reitz (Western Connecticut State University), version of December 2000, converted into Pajek format and cleaned by A. Mrvar and V. Batagelj. ODLIS is a hypertext reference resource for library and information science professionals, students and library users, which includes the vocabulary of librarianship, publishing, printing, book history, literature and computer science. A directed edge points from a term X to a term Y if Y is used to describe the meaning of X. The source contains 173 repeated edges and 5 self-loops. The data were distributed in Pajek format on the Pajek datasets page of V. Batagelj and A. Mrvar, from which this version was obtained.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the term.
citations: J. M. Reitz, "ODLIS: Online Dictionary of Library and Information Science." Libraries Unlimited (2002)

datasets.name: offshore_leaks
datasets.description:
The Offshore Leaks database of the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists (ICIJ): the offshore companies, foundations and trusts, the people and companies behind them, their intermediaries and their addresses, as revealed by the leaked documents of five investigations: the Offshore Leaks (2013), the Panama Papers (2016, from the law firm Mossack Fonseca), the Bahamas Leaks (2016), the Paradise Papers (2017, from the law firm Appleby and several corporate registries) and the Pandora Papers (2021, from several offshore service providers). The data cover offshore entities in over 200 countries and territories, over more than 80 years up to 2020. They are not complete records of the service providers, and the ICIJ notes that there are legitimate uses of offshore entities, and that the presence of a person or company in the database does not imply wrongdoing.

Each node is an entity (814,344: offshore companies, trusts and foundations), an officer (771,315: people or companies with a role in an entity, e.g. directors, shareholders and beneficiaries), an intermediary (26,768: e.g. lawyers, banks and agents that set up entities), an address (402,246), or another kind of node (2,989, e.g. companies from corporate registries). The 1,139 nodes that are listed both as officers and as intermediaries are single nodes. Each directed edge is a relationship as given in the database, e.g. from an officer to an entity of which it is a director (`officer_of`), from an intermediary to an entity (`intermediary_of`), from a node to its address (`registered_address`), or between nodes that the ICIJ found to be probably the same (e.g. `same_name_as`, `similar`, `same_as`); several relationships between the same nodes appear as multiple edges. The network contains all the 2,016,523 nodes and 3,339,267 relationships of the bulk download of the database generated on 9 September 2026.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `node_id`: the id of the node in the database.
- (Node) `node_type`: its kind (`entity`, `officer`, `intermediary`, `address` or `other`; `officer; intermediary` for the nodes listed as both).
- (Node) `name`: the name of the node.
- (Node) `original_name`, `former_name`, `address`, `company_type`, `type`, `status`, `service_provider`, `internal_id`, `note`: as given for the nodes (empty otherwise).
- (Node) `jurisdiction`, `jurisdiction_description`: where the entity was incorporated, as given (empty otherwise).
- (Node) `ibcRUC`: a registration number, as given (empty otherwise).
- (Node) `incorporation_date`, `inactivation_date`, `struck_off_date`, `dorm_date`, `closed_date`: dates as given, mostly as DD-MON-YYYY (empty otherwise).
- (Node) `countries`, `country_codes`: the countries the node is linked to, separated by semicolons (empty if not given).
- (Node) `source`: the leak and, for some, the service provider or registry (empty if not given).
- (Node) `valid_until`: how recent the data of the source are (empty if not given).
- (Edge) `rel_type`: the type of relationship (e.g. `officer_of`).
- (Edge) `link`: its description (e.g. "shareholder of", "director of").
- (Edge) `status`: the status of the relationship (e.g. "Resigned").
- (Edge) `start_date` and `end_date`: as given (in several formats).
- (Edge) `start_time` and `end_time`: the same as Unix time for the dates given as DD-MON-YYYY or YYYY-MM-DD (NaN otherwise).
- (Edge) `source`: the leak (empty for 518,982 relationships).
citations: International Consortium of Investigative Journalists (ICIJ), "Offshore Leaks Database." (2026)

datasets.name: offsides_twosides
datasets.description:
Networks of drug side effects and of side effects of drug combinations, from OFFSIDES and TWOSIDES of the Tatonetti lab (nSIDES project), mined from the reports of adverse events of the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS). For each drug (or pair of drugs) and each adverse event, the proportional reporting ratio (PRR) compares the frequency of the event among the reports of the drug with its frequency among the reports of control drugs, which are matched by a propensity score model to correct for confounding (e.g. by indication or co-medication). OFFSIDES focuses on effects that are not listed on the drug label ("off-label" side effects). The files repeat their header line every 200,000 rows; these lines are skipped. The data are those of the files published in March 2024 (from the release of November 2019), which their authors describe as out of date.

- `offsides`: bipartite network of drugs and adverse events (side effects), where an edge is a signal of the drug causing the event.
- `twosides`: network of drugs, where an edge joins two drugs whose combination is associated with an adverse event, labeled by the event; two drugs are joined by one edge per event (so that the network is a multigraph).

The drugs are RxNorm ingredients, and the adverse events are MedDRA terms (preferred terms).

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `rxnorm_id`: the RxNorm identifier of the drug (-1 for adverse events).
- (Node) `meddra_id` (`offsides`): the MedDRA identifier of the adverse event (-1 for drugs).
- (Node) `name`: the name of the drug or of the adverse event.
- (Node) `is_drug` (`offsides`): whether the node is a drug (otherwise it is an adverse event).
- (Edge) `condition_meddra_id`, `condition_name` (`twosides`): the MedDRA identifier and name of the adverse event.
- (Edge) `a`: the number of reports for the drug (or pair of drugs) that report the event; `b`: the number of its reports that do not report it; `c`: the number of reports of the matched control drugs that report the event; `d`: the number of reports of the control drugs that do not.
- (Edge) `prr`: the proportional reporting ratio, $(a/(a+b))/(c/(c+d))$, and `prr_error` its error estimate (NaN if not given; the counts are -1 if not given).
- (Edge) `mean_reporting_frequency`: the fraction of the reports of the drug (or pair) that report the event, $a/(a+b)$.
citations: N. P. Tatonetti, P. P. Ye, R. Daneshjou, R. B. Altman, "Data-Driven Prediction of Drug Effects and Interactions." Science Translational Medicine 4, 125ra31 (2012)

datasets.name: ogbl_biokg
datasets.description:
A heterogeneous biomedical knowledge graph, from the `ogbl-biokg` dataset of the Open Graph Benchmark (OGB), a benchmark for link prediction (version 1, of 2020), built from BioKG, which integrates data of biomedical databases (e.g. UniProt, Reactome, KEGG, DrugBank, SIDER, the Gene Ontology, CTD, ...). The nodes are entities of five types: diseases (10,687), proteins (17,499), drugs (10,533), side effects (9,969) and protein functions (45,085), and each directed edge is a triple (head, relation, tail) with one of 51 relations, e.g. drug-protein interactions, protein-protein interactions of several kinds (activation, binding, catalysis, expression, inhibition, post-translational modification, reaction), drug-side effect associations, drug-drug interactions labeled by the class of diseases on which the interaction has an effect (e.g. `drug-drug_cancer`), and the hierarchy of protein functions. Two entities can be joined by several edges with different relations.

The triples are split at random into the training (4,762,678), validation (162,886) and test (162,870) sets of the benchmark; the network contains all 5,088,434 triples, with their set as edge property `split`. The training triples are read from the plain files of the relations, the validation and test triples from the PyTorch files of the split (`split/random/valid.pt`, `test.pt`, of a legacy format, read without PyTorch). The negative samples of the validation and test triples (500 random heads and 500 random tails of the same type for each triple, against which the true triple is ranked in the benchmark: about 163 million non-edges) are left out.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `kind`: the type of the entity: `disease`, `protein`, `drug`, `sideeffect` or `function`.
- (Node) `entity_id`: the identifier of the entity: a UMLS concept identifier for diseases and side effects, an NCBI Gene (Entrez) identifier for proteins, a STITCH compound identifier for drugs, a Gene Ontology identifier for functions.
- (Edge) `relation`: the relation of the triple, e.g. `drug-protein`, `protein-protein_binding`.
- (Edge) `split`: the set of the triple in the benchmark: `train`, `valid` or `test`.
citations: W. Hu, M. Fey, M. Zitnik, Y. Dong, H. Ren, B. Liu, M. Catasta, J. Leskovec, "Open Graph Benchmark: Datasets for Machine Learning on Graphs." Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 33, 22118-22133 (2020)

B. Walsh, S. K. Mohamed, V. Nováček, "BioKG: A Knowledge Graph for Relational Learning On Biological Data." Proceedings of the 29th ACM International Conference on Information & Knowledge Management (CIKM), 3173-3180 (2020)

datasets.name: ogbl_citation2
datasets.description:
A directed citation network of papers of the Microsoft Academic Graph (MAG), from the `ogbl-citation2` dataset of the Open Graph Benchmark (OGB), a benchmark for link prediction (version 1, of December 2020). The papers are a subset of MAG, and an edge from paper A to paper B means that A cites B.

For the benchmark, two references of each of the most recent papers (published in 2019) are held out, one for validation and one for testing (86,596 references each); these held-out citations are included here, so that the network contains all the 30,561,187 citations of the dataset, and they are marked by an edge property.

Each paper also has the node features of the benchmark: a 128-dimensional vector obtained by averaging the word2vec embeddings of the words in its title and abstract (the embeddings were trained by the OGB authors on the MAG corpus). The negative samples of the benchmark (references that do not exist) are also left out. The data do not include the titles of the papers.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `mag_id`: the identifier of the paper in the Microsoft Academic Graph.
- (Node) `year`: the publication year of the paper.
- (Node) `features`: the 128-dimensional feature vector of the paper (the average of the word2vec embeddings of the words of its title and abstract).
- (Edge) `split`: the part of the benchmark the citation belongs to: `train`, `valid` or `test`.
citations: W. Hu, M. Fey, M. Zitnik, Y. Dong, H. Ren, B. Liu, M. Catasta, J. Leskovec, "Open Graph Benchmark: Datasets for Machine Learning on Graphs." Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 33, 22118-22133 (2020)
K. Wang, Z. Shen, C. Huang, C.-H. Wu, Y. Dong, A. Kanakia, "Microsoft Academic Graph: When experts are not enough." Quantitative Science Studies 1(1), 396-413 (2020)

datasets.name: ogbl_ppa
datasets.description:
An undirected network of functional associations between the proteins of 58 species, from the `ogbl-ppa` dataset of the Open Graph Benchmark (OGB), a benchmark for link prediction (version 1, of May 2020). The proteins and associations are a subset of the STRING database (version 11): an edge means that two proteins are associated in a biologically meaningful way, e.g. by a physical interaction, co-expression, homology or genomic neighborhood (the kinds of evidence are not given). The species span the tree of life (e.g. human, mouse, yeast, *Arabidopsis thaliana*, *Plasmodium falciparum*, bacteria). The networks of all the species of STRING are in the entry `string_all`.

For the benchmark, the edges were split by "throughput": the associations found with high-throughput techniques (e.g. automated screens, or predictions) are used for training, and those found with low-throughput, resource-intensive experiments (e.g. experimentally determined interactions of single protein pairs) for validation and testing. All the 30,326,273 edges of the dataset are included here, with their part of the split as an edge property; the negative samples of the benchmark (pairs of proteins that are not associated) are left out. In the benchmark, each node has as features a one-hot vector of its species, which is given here as the species' taxonomy identifier.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `protein_id`: the identifier of the protein in STRING, e.g. `9606.ENSP00000000233` (the NCBI taxonomy identifier of the species, followed by the identifier of the protein in its source database).
- (Node) `species`: the NCBI taxonomy identifier of the species of the protein, e.g. 9606 (human).
- (Edge) `split`: the part of the benchmark the edge belongs to: `train`, `valid` or `test`.
citations: W. Hu, M. Fey, M. Zitnik, Y. Dong, H. Ren, B. Liu, M. Catasta, J. Leskovec, "Open Graph Benchmark: Datasets for Machine Learning on Graphs." Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 33, 22118-22133 (2020)

D. Szklarczyk et al., "STRING v11: protein-protein association networks with increased coverage, supporting functional discovery in genome-wide experimental datasets." Nucleic Acids Research 47, D607-D613 (2019)

datasets.name: ogbl_wikikg2
datasets.description:
A knowledge graph extracted from Wikidata, from the `ogbl-wikikg2` dataset of the Open Graph Benchmark (OGB), a benchmark for link prediction (version 1, of December 2020). Each node is an entity of Wikidata (e.g. a person, a place, a work or a concept), and a directed edge from entity A to entity B is a statement (A, relation, B) of Wikidata with one of 535 relations (Wikidata properties, e.g. `P31`, "instance of", or `P27`, "country of citizenship"). Pairs of entities may be connected by several edges with different relations. Rare entities were filtered out by the OGB authors.

The triples come from three snapshots of Wikidata of 2015: those of May 2015 form the training set of the benchmark, and those added in the snapshots of August and November 2015 form the validation and test sets (429,456 and 598,543 triples); all of them are included, and the set is given as an edge property. The negative samples of the benchmark are left out. The data do not include the labels of the entities and relations, which can be looked up in Wikidata (some entities and relations may have been removed from Wikidata since 2015).

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `wikidata_id`: the Wikidata identifier of the entity, e.g. `Q92894`.
- (Edge) `relation`: the Wikidata property of the relation, e.g. `P31`.
- (Edge) `split`: the set of the benchmark the triple belongs to: `train` (May 2015), `valid` (August 2015) or `test` (November 2015).
citations: W. Hu, M. Fey, M. Zitnik, Y. Dong, H. Ren, B. Liu, M. Catasta, J. Leskovec, "Open Graph Benchmark: Datasets for Machine Learning on Graphs." Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 33, 22118-22133 (2020)
D. Vrandečić, M. Krötzsch, "Wikidata: a free collaborative knowledgebase." Communications of the ACM 57(10), 78-85 (2014)

datasets.name: ogbn_arxiv
datasets.description:
A directed citation network of the computer science papers of the arXiv preprint server, as indexed by the Microsoft Academic Graph (MAG), from the `ogbn-arxiv` dataset of the Open Graph Benchmark (OGB), a benchmark for node classification (version 1, of May 2020). Each paper is labeled with its primary arXiv subject area (one of the 40 computer science categories, chosen by the authors and the arXiv moderators), and the publication years range from 1971 to 2020.

An edge from paper A to paper B means that A cites B. There are no self-loops, and 8,444 pairs of papers cite each other.

Each paper also has the node features of the benchmark: a 128-dimensional vector obtained by averaging the word2vec embeddings of the words in its title and abstract (the embeddings were trained by the OGB authors on the MAG corpus). The titles of the papers come from a separate file of the OGB authors, which also has their abstracts (left out). The titles are as normalized by MAG (in lower case, without punctuation).

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `mag_id`: the identifier of the paper in the Microsoft Academic Graph.
- (Node) `title`: the title of the paper, normalized.
- (Node) `year`: the publication year of the paper.
- (Node) `subject`: the primary arXiv subject area of the paper, e.g. `cs.LG` or `cs.AI`.
- (Node) `features`: the 128-dimensional feature vector of the paper (the average of the word2vec embeddings of the words of its title and abstract).
citations: W. Hu, M. Fey, M. Zitnik, Y. Dong, H. Ren, B. Liu, M. Catasta, J. Leskovec, "Open Graph Benchmark: Datasets for Machine Learning on Graphs." Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 33, 22118-22133 (2020)
K. Wang, Z. Shen, C. Huang, C.-H. Wu, Y. Dong, A. Kanakia, "Microsoft Academic Graph: When experts are not enough." Quantitative Science Studies 1(1), 396-413 (2020)

datasets.name: ogbn_mag
datasets.description:
A heterogeneous network of papers, their authors, the institutions of the authors, and the fields of study of the papers, a subset of the Microsoft Academic Graph (MAG), from the `ogbn-mag` dataset of the Open Graph Benchmark (OGB), a benchmark for node classification (version 2, of June 2020, from which duplicate edges were removed). The benchmark task is to predict the venue (conference or journal) of each paper, one of 349 venues, which the papers are labeled with.

The network has nodes of four kinds: 736,389 papers, 1,134,649 authors, 8,740 institutions and 59,965 fields of study, and directed edges of four kinds: an author *writes* a paper (7,145,660 edges), a paper *cites* another paper (5,416,271), a paper *has_topic* a field of study (7,505,078), and an author is *affiliated_with* an institution (1,043,998). The nodes are identified by their MAG identifiers only (the data do not include titles, names, or the names of the fields of study and venues).

The papers also have the node features of the benchmark: a 128-dimensional vector obtained by averaging the word2vec embeddings of the words in the title and abstract of the paper (the embeddings were trained by the OGB authors on the MAG corpus); the other nodes have no features. The splits of the benchmark (by year) are also left out.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `kind`: the kind of the node (`paper`, `author`, `institution` or `field_of_study`).
- (Node) `mag_id`: the identifier of the node (paper, author, institution or field of study) in the Microsoft Academic Graph.
- (Node) `year`: the publication year of a paper (-1 for other nodes).
- (Node) `venue`: the MAG identifier of the venue (conference or journal) of a paper (-1 for other nodes).
- (Node) `features`: the 128-dimensional feature vector of a paper (the average of the word2vec embeddings of the words of its title and abstract; empty for other nodes).
- (Edge) `kind`: the relation (`writes`, `cites`, `has_topic` or `affiliated_with`).
citations: W. Hu, M. Fey, M. Zitnik, Y. Dong, H. Ren, B. Liu, M. Catasta, J. Leskovec, "Open Graph Benchmark: Datasets for Machine Learning on Graphs." Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 33, 22118-22133 (2020)
K. Wang, Z. Shen, C. Huang, C.-H. Wu, Y. Dong, A. Kanakia, "Microsoft Academic Graph: When experts are not enough." Quantitative Science Studies 1(1), 396-413 (2020)

datasets.name: ogbn_products
datasets.description:
An undirected network of products sold on Amazon, two products being connected if they were bought together, from the `ogbn-products` dataset of the Open Graph Benchmark (OGB), a benchmark for node classification (version 1, of May 2020). The network was built by W.-L. Chiang and colleagues for the evaluation of Cluster-GCN (where it is called "Amazon2M"), from the Amazon product data of the Extreme Classification Repository (originally collected by J. McAuley and colleagues from the Amazon website), and processed further by the OGB authors.

Each product is labeled with one of 47 top-level categories of Amazon (the target of the classification task), and has the node features of the benchmark: a 100-dimensional vector obtained from the bag-of-words of its description, reduced by principal component analysis. The products are identified by their Amazon ASIN; their names and descriptions are not included. The benchmark split of the products into training, validation and test sets follows their sales rank (the top 8% are for training, the next 2% for validation and the rest for testing) and is kept as the property `split`.

As noted by OGB, a few self-loops appear more than once; they are kept as given.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `asin`: the Amazon Standard Identification Number of the product.
- (Node) `category`: the top-level category of the product, e.g. `Books` or `Electronics` (as named in the mapping file of OGB, where one category has an empty name and another one is named `#508510`).
- (Node) `split`: the set of the product in the benchmark's split by sales rank: `train` (the 8% best-selling products), `valid` (the next 2%), or `test` (the rest).
- (Node) `features`: the 100-dimensional feature vector of the product (the reduced bag-of-words of its description).
citations: W. Hu, M. Fey, M. Zitnik, Y. Dong, H. Ren, B. Liu, M. Catasta, J. Leskovec, "Open Graph Benchmark: Datasets for Machine Learning on Graphs." Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 33, 22118-22133 (2020)

W.-L. Chiang, X. Liu, S. Si, Y. Li, S. Bengio, C.-J. Hsieh, "Cluster-GCN: An Efficient Algorithm for Training Deep and Large Graph Convolutional Networks." Proceedings of the 25th ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery & Data Mining, 257-266 (2019)

datasets.name: ogbn_proteins
datasets.description:
An undirected network of functional associations between the proteins of eight species, from the `ogbn-proteins` dataset of the Open Graph Benchmark (OGB), a benchmark for node classification (version 1, of May 2020). The proteins and associations come from the STRING database (version 11): an edge means that two proteins are functionally associated, and has as features the scores of eight kinds of evidence for the association. The species are *Escherichia coli* (taxonomy identifier 511145), *Arabidopsis thaliana* (3702), *Saccharomyces cerevisiae* (4932), *Caenorhabditis elegans* (6239), *Drosophila melanogaster* (7227), *Danio rerio* (7955), *Homo sapiens* (9606) and *Mus musculus* (10090); the networks of all the species of STRING are in the entry `string_all`.

The task of the benchmark is to predict the presence of 112 protein functions (terms of the Gene Ontology), given as binary labels of the nodes. The nodes are split by species: the proteins of one species are used for validation, those of another for testing, and the rest for training.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `protein_id`: the identifier of the protein in STRING, e.g. `9606.ENSP00000000233` (the NCBI taxonomy identifier of the species, followed by the identifier of the protein).
- (Node) `species`: the NCBI taxonomy identifier of the species of the protein.
- (Node) `labels`: the 112 binary labels of the protein (1 if the protein has the function, 0 otherwise), in the order of the graph property `label_go_terms`.
- (Node) `split`: the part of the benchmark the protein belongs to: `train`, `valid` or `test`.
- (Edge) `homology`, `neighborhood`, `fusion`, `cooccurence`, `coexpression`, `experimental`, `database`, `textmining`: the scores of the eight kinds of evidence for the association (between 0 and 1; 0 if there is no evidence of that kind), as in STRING: homology, conserved genomic neighborhood, gene fusions, phylogenetic co-occurrence, co-expression, experiments, curated databases and text mining (as named by STRING, with its spelling of `cooccurence`).
- (Node) `label_go_terms` (graph): the Gene Ontology term of each label, e.g. `GO:0003674`.
citations: W. Hu, M. Fey, M. Zitnik, Y. Dong, H. Ren, B. Liu, M. Catasta, J. Leskovec, "Open Graph Benchmark: Datasets for Machine Learning on Graphs." Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 33, 22118-22133 (2020)

D. Szklarczyk et al., "STRING v11: protein-protein association networks with increased coverage, supporting functional discovery in genome-wide experimental datasets." Nucleic Acids Research 47, D607-D613 (2019)

datasets.name: omnipath
datasets.description:
Directed and signed networks of molecular interactions from OmniPath, a database that integrates more than 100 resources of literature-curated and predicted molecular interactions (mostly of human proteins): signaling pathways (post-translational interactions, e.g. SIGNOR, SignaLink, Reactome, KEGG, PhosphoSite), enzyme-substrate (kinase-substrate) relations, ligand-receptor interactions between cells, transcriptional regulation of genes by transcription factors (DoRothEA, CollecTRI), regulation by miRNAs and lncRNAs, and interactions of small molecules with proteins. Each edge is an interaction, from the source to the target of the interaction (e.g. from a kinase to its substrate), with its direction and sign (stimulation or inhibition) when they are known; the interactions whose direction is unknown are also listed from a source to a target, with `is_directed` false.

The networks are all the archived contents of the OmniPath web service (the `interactions` query, with all its datasets and organisms, i.e. human, and the interactions translated by homology to mouse and rat), each named by the date from which it was served, until the next one: `2018-06-14`, `2018-11-14`, `2019-04-25`, `2019-06-26`, `2019-08-26`, `2019-10-18`, `2019-11-27`, `2020-02-17`, `2020-05-19`, `2020-08-03`, `2020-09-09`, `2020-09-21`, `2021-01-21`, `2021-03-29`, `2021-06-16`, `2021-06-21`, `2021-11-13`, `2022-01-14`, `2023-03-30`, `2023-05-18`, `2023-05-24`, `2023-07-28` (until 2025-08-13), `2025-08-13` (the last content of the legacy web service, until 2026-06-24) and `2026-06-25` (with the new CollecTRI 2 dataset as a separate dataset). No two of them have identical content (`2023-05-24` and `2023-07-28` have the same interactions, resources and datasets, but differ in some gene symbols, directions, signs and further attributes). The current content of the web service (`omnipath_webservice_interactions__latest`, replaced in place at every update) is left out. Nodes are proteins (UniProt accessions), protein complexes (`COMPLEX:` followed by the accessions of their members), miRNAs, lncRNAs and small molecules.

The networks have the following properties (the columns of the web service; the later contents have more of them):

- (Node) `name`: the identifier of the node in OmniPath (e.g. the UniProt accession `P0DP23`).
- (Node) `genesymbol`: the gene symbol of the node (e.g. `CALM1`).
- (Node) `ncbi_tax_id`: the NCBI taxonomy identifier of the organism of the node (e.g. 9606 for human; -1 if not given).
- (Node) `entity_type` (from `2020-05-19`): the kind of node, e.g. `protein`, `complex`, `mirna`, `lncrna`, `small_molecule`.
- (Edge) `is_directed`, `is_stimulation`, `is_inhibition`: whether the interaction is directed, stimulatory and inhibitory, according to at least one resource.
- (Edge) `consensus_direction`, `consensus_stimulation`, `consensus_inhibition` (from `2019-06-26`): the same, according to the majority of the resources.
- (Edge) `sources`: the resources of the interaction, separated by `;`.
- (Edge) `references`: the PubMed identifiers of the references of the interaction (prefixed by the resource in the later contents), separated by `;`.
- (Edge) `type`: the kind of interaction, e.g. `post_translational`, `transcriptional`, `post_transcriptional`, `mirna_transcriptional`, `small_molecule_protein` (`PPI`, `TF` and `MTI` until `2020-02-17`).
- (Edge) Dataset flags, e.g. `omnipath` (the core literature-curated signaling network), `kinaseextra`, `ligrecextra`, `pathwayextra`, `mirnatarget`, `dorothea`, `collectri`, `collectri2`, `tf_target`, `lncrna_mrna`, `tf_mirna`, `small_molecule` (`tfregulons` until `2020-02-17`; `ligrecextra` and `pathwayextra` from `2019-06-26`, `tf_target`, `lncrna_mrna` and `tf_mirna` from `2020-05-19`, `small_molecule` from `2022-01-14`, `collectri` from `2023-03-30`, `collectri2` in `2026-06-25`): whether the interaction belongs to the dataset.
- (Edge) `dorothea_curated`, `dorothea_chipseq`, `dorothea_tfbs`, `dorothea_coexp`, `dorothea_level` (`tfregulons_...` until `2020-02-17`): the kinds of evidence and the confidence level (`A` to `E`) of the transcriptional regulation in DoRothEA.
- (Edge) `curation_effort` (from `2020-02-17`): the number of unique resource-reference pairs of the interaction.
- (Edge) `extra_attrs` (from `2021-11-13`): further attributes given by the resources, in JSON.
- (Edge) `evidences` (from `2023-05-18`): the provenance of the interaction by resource and dataset, with the references and the direction and sign given by each, in JSON.
- (Edge) `dip_url` (until `2021-06-21`): the URL of the interaction in DIP.
citations: D. Türei, T. Korcsmáros, J. Saez-Rodriguez, "OmniPath: guidelines and gateway for literature-curated signaling pathway resources." Nature Methods 13, 966-967 (2016)

D. Türei, A. Valdeolivas, L. Gul, N. Palacio-Escat, M. Klein, O. Ivanova, M. Ölbei, A. Gábor, F. Theis, D. Módos, T. Korcsmáros, J. Saez-Rodriguez, "Integrated intra- and intercellular signaling knowledge for multicellular omics analysis." Molecular Systems Biology 17, e9923 (2021)

datasets.name: open_payments
datasets.description:
Payments and other transfers of value from manufacturers of drugs, medical devices and medical supplies, and from group purchasing organizations, to physicians, other health care practitioners (physician assistants, nurse practitioners, ...) and teaching hospitals in the United States, as reported by the companies to the Open Payments program of the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), which publishes them under the Physician Payments Sunshine Act. The networks contain the "general payments" (payments not made in connection with a research agreement: food and beverage, consulting fees, travel, speaker fees, royalties, education, gifts, ...), with one network per program year (the calendar year of the payments), from 2019 to 2025, named after the year (e.g. `2024`).

Each network is a bipartite multigraph of the paying companies and the recipients, with a directed edge from a company to a recipient for each payment record, with its date, amount, form, nature and associated product. A record may aggregate several payments of small value (with the number of payments given). The companies are identified by their Open Payments identifier, the physicians and practitioners by their Open Payments profile identifier, and the teaching hospitals by their Open Payments identifier; only the companies and recipients with some payment in the year are included. The records are those of the publication of June 2026 (the data are refreshed by CMS at least once a year, with corrections and disputes resolved by the recipients, so that the data of a year change between publications). The years 2013 to 2018, which are no longer part of the current publication of CMS, are not included, and neither are the research payments, the ownership and investment interests, the addresses of the recipients and companies, the payments to third parties (only their flag), and the products other than the first one listed with each payment.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `is_company`: whether the node is a paying company (otherwise it is a recipient).
- (Node) `id`: the Open Payments identifier of the company, the profile identifier of the physician or practitioner, or the identifier of the teaching hospital.
- (Node) `name`: the name of the company or of the teaching hospital, or the name of the physician or practitioner (first, middle and last names, and suffix).
- (Node) `kind`: `Company`, `Physician`, `Non-Physician Practitioner` or `Teaching Hospital`.
- (Node) `npi` (physicians and practitioners): the National Provider Identifier of the recipient (0 if not given, and for the other nodes).
- (Node) `ccn` (teaching hospitals): the CMS Certification Number of the hospital (empty for the other nodes).
- (Node) `city` (recipients), `state`, `country`: the location of the recipient (its primary business address), or the state and country of the company.
- (Node) `primary_type` (physicians and practitioners): the first primary type of the recipient (e.g. `Medical Doctor`, `Nurse Practitioner`).
- (Node) `specialty` (physicians and practitioners): the first specialty of the recipient, as a path of the provider taxonomy (e.g. `Allopathic & Osteopathic Physicians|Family Medicine`).
- (Edge) `time`: the date of the payment (of the first payment if several are aggregated), as the Unix time of its beginning (midnight UTC).
- (Edge) `amount`: the total amount of the payment, in US dollars.
- (Edge) `payments`: the number of payments included in the record.
- (Edge) `form`: the form of payment (e.g. `Cash or cash equivalent`, `In-kind items and services`, `Stock`).
- (Edge) `nature`: the nature of the payment (e.g. `Food and Beverage`, `Consulting Fee`, `Travel and Lodging`, `Royalty or License`).
- (Edge) `product`: the name of the (first) drug, device or supply associated with the payment (empty if none).
- (Edge) `product_type`: the type of that product (`Drug`, `Biological`, `Device`, `Medical Supply`, or empty).
- (Edge) `third_party`: the indicator of payments to a third party at the request of the recipient (e.g. `No Third Party Payment`, `Entity`, `Individual`).
- (Edge) `record_id`: the identifier of the record in Open Payments.
citations: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, "Open Payments: General Payment Data." Publication of June 30, 2026 (program years 2019-2025)

datasets.name: open_targets_associations
datasets.description:
Bipartite networks of genes (drug targets) and diseases or phenotypes, from the Open Targets Platform, which integrates the evidence that a gene is involved in a disease from many sources (genetic associations, somatic mutations, known drugs, affected pathways, gene expression, animal models, and text mining of the literature) into association scores between 0 and 1, to help the selection of drug targets.

Nodes are targets (Ensembl genes) and diseases (terms of the Experimental Factor Ontology, EFO, and of the ontologies it imports, such as MONDO, HP, Orphanet and GO), and an edge connects a target and a disease that have an association, with its overall score, and its scores by type of evidence (data type).

- `2021` ... `2026`: the direct associations (from evidence for the disease itself) of the releases of September of each year (21.09 to 26.09).
- `indirect_2026`: the indirect associations of release 26.09, where the evidence for a disease is also propagated to all its ancestors in the ontology (only the overall score).

The scores by data source (finer than the data types), the yearly scores of release 26.09 (except the first year with a positive score), and the indirect associations of the earlier releases are left out.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `is_target`: whether the node is a target (otherwise it is a disease).
- (Node) `ot_id`: the identifier of the target (Ensembl gene, e.g. `ENSG00000141510`) or disease (e.g. `EFO_0000311`, `MONDO_0007254`).
- (Node) `name`: the approved symbol of the gene, or the name of the disease.
- (Node) `full_name` (targets): the approved name of the gene.
- (Node) `biotype`, `chromosome` (targets): the biotype of the gene (e.g. `protein_coding`) and its chromosome.
- (Node) `therapeutic_areas` (diseases): the therapeutic areas of the disease (their identifiers).
- (Edge) `score`: the overall association score.
- (Edge) `evidence_count`: the number of pieces of evidence of the association.
- (Edge) `score_<datatype>` (direct associations): the association score from the evidence of each data type (`genetic_association`, `somatic_mutation`, `known_drug`, `affected_pathway`, `rna_expression`, `animal_model`, `literature`, and the types of the release; NaN if there is no evidence of the type).
- (Edge) `novelty`, `first_year` (`2026`, `indirect_2026`): the current novelty of the association (a measure of how recent its evidence is), and the first year in which its score was positive (`-1` if unknown, e.g. for evidence without a date).
citations: A. Buniello, D. Suveges, C. Cruz-Castillo, M. B. Llinares, H. Cornu, I. Lopez, K. Tsukanov, J. M. Roldán-Romero, C. Mehta, L. Fumis, et al., "Open Targets Platform: facilitating therapeutic hypotheses building in drug discovery." Nucleic Acids Research 53, D1467-D1475 (2025)

datasets.name: openalex_cocitations
datasets.description:
Bipartite networks of highly cited papers and the sets of them that are cited together, in five fields of research, built by Nakajima et al. from the OpenAlex snapshot of 27 September 2024, as distributed by XGI-data:

- `biochem`: Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology;
- `cs`: Computer Science;
- `math`: Mathematics;
- `neuro`: Neuroscience;
- `physics`: Physics and Astronomy.

In each field, the papers of each subfield were ranked by their numbers of citations, and the top papers that account for 10% of the cumulative citations of the subfield were selected (at least 100 papers per subfield). For each other paper of OpenAlex, the set of selected papers it cites was determined; each set of at least two papers that is cited by at least 3 papers is a co-citation set, connected to its papers. The sets cited by fewer papers, and the numbers of papers citing each set, are not included in the data.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `is_cocitation`: whether the node is a co-citation set (otherwise a paper).
- (Node) `openalex_id` (papers): the OpenAlex identifier of the paper (e.g. `W2010634640`, see `https://openalex.org/<id>`).
- (Node) `title` (papers): the title of the paper (in lower case).
- (Node) `date` (papers): the publication date (YYYY-MM-DD).
- (Node) `year` (papers): the publication year.
- (Node) `topic`, `subfield`, `field`, `domain` (papers): the primary topic of the paper in OpenAlex and its subfield, field and domain.
- (Node) `cited_by_count` (papers): the number of citations of the paper in OpenAlex.
citations: K. Nakajima, Y. Sasaki, T. Uno, M. Aida, "Learning Multi-Order Block Structure in Higher-Order Networks." arXiv:2511.21350 (2025)
J. Priem, H. Piwowar, R. Orr, "OpenAlex: A fully-open index of scholarly works, authors, venues, institutions, and concepts." arXiv:2205.01833 (2022)

datasets.name: openflights
datasets.description:
Network of airline routes among airports worldwide, from the OpenFlights route database (originally based on the Airline Route Mapper data). Nodes are airports and a directed edge $(i,j)$ indicates that an airline operates a regular route from airport $i$ to airport $j$. Each route is listed separately for each airline that operates it (including codeshares), so pairs of airports can be connected by multiple edges. The route database was last updated in June 2014 and is not a complete record of all flights; routes whose airports are not identified in the airport database were discarded, as well as airports without any routes.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `id`: the OpenFlights ID of the airport.
- (Node) `name`, `city`, `country`: the name of the airport, and the city and country where it is located.
- (Node) `IATA/FAA`, `ICAO`: the three-letter IATA (or FAA) code and the four-letter ICAO code of the airport, if available.
- (Node) `latitude`, `longitude`: the coordinates of the airport, in degrees.
- (Node) `altitude`: the altitude of the airport, in feet.
- (Node) `timezone`: the offset from UTC, in hours (99 if unknown).
- (Node) `DST`: the daylight saving time convention, with E = Europe, A = US/Canada, S = South America, O = Australia, Z = New Zealand, N = none, U = unknown (`\N` if missing).
- (Edge) `airline`: the two-letter IATA or three-letter ICAO code of the airline.
- (Edge) `airline_code`: the OpenFlights ID of the airline.
- (Edge) `codeshare`: whether the route is a codeshare, i.e. operated by another carrier.
- (Edge) `stops`: the number of stops (0 for direct flights).
- (Edge) `equipment`: the three-letter codes of the aircraft types typically used on the route, separated by spaces.
- (Edge) `distance`: the great-circle distance between the two airports, in kilometers.

datasets.name: openlegaldata_citations
datasets.description:
Directed networks of the citations in German court decisions, to other decisions and to the sections of laws, extracted by Open Legal Data (the Open Legal Data Platform, de.openlegaldata.io), a project that collects German court decisions and laws from the websites of the courts and of the federal and state governments, and extracts their references automatically (from the citations in the text of the decisions, such as file numbers of decisions and "§ 433 BGB" for laws).

Each node is a court decision (a case) or a section of a law, and a directed edge from A to B means that A cites B: a decision cites another decision or a law section, or a law section refers to another section of the same law. The edges are weighted by the number of times the citation was extracted (a decision citing the same law section in several places of its text gives as many rows in the data). There are two networks:

- `2019`: the citation graph of the first dataset of court decisions of Open Legal Data (published in 2019, with about 100,000 decisions), with decisions and laws identified by the numeric ids of the database of Open Legal Data (decisions and laws numbered separately); it contains only citations from decisions (442,236 rows).
- `2026`: the dump of 20 May 2026 (7,438,459 rows), with decisions identified by their slug in Open Legal Data (e.g. `bgh-2018-09-05-2-str-45417`, the page `https://de.openlegaldata.io/case/<slug>/`) and law sections by the slug of their law book and their own (e.g. `bgb/433`); it also contains the references between the sections of the same law (from the law texts).

The decisions are described by their court and the attributes of the decision when they cite something (those cited without citing anything only have the attributes of their court in `2026`, and none in `2019`); the law sections by their law book, section number and title (when they are cited). The extraction is automatic, and the references to decisions cover only those that could be matched to a decision in the database.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `is_law`: whether the node is a law section (otherwise it is a court decision).
- (Node) `oldp_id` (`2019`): the id of the decision or the law section in Open Legal Data.
- (Node) `slug` (`2026`): the slug of the decision, or `<book slug>/<section slug>` for a law section.
- (Node) `court`, `chamber`, `city`, `state`, `jurisdiction`, `level_of_appeal` (decisions): the court (e.g. `Bundesgerichtshof`), its chamber or senate (e.g. `2. Strafsenat`), its city, its state (or `Bundesrepublik Deutschland` for federal courts), its branch of jurisdiction (e.g. `Ordentliche Gerichtsbarkeit`, `Arbeitsgerichtsbarkeit`) and its level of appeal (e.g. `Bundesgericht`, `Landgericht`).
- (Node) `court_id` (`2019`, decisions): the id of the court in Open Legal Data (-1 if unknown).
- (Node) `date`, `file_number`, `decision_type` (decisions): the date of the decision (`YYYY-MM-DD`), its file number (`Aktenzeichen`, e.g. `2 StR 454/17`) and its type (e.g. `Urteil`, `Beschluss`).
- (Node) `review_status` (`2026`, decisions): the review status of the decision in Open Legal Data (e.g. `accepted`).
- (Node) `source`, `private` (`2019`, decisions): the source from which the decision was collected, and whether it was marked as private (1, 0 or -1 if unknown).
- (Node) `book_code`, `section`, `law_title` (law sections): the abbreviation of the law (e.g. `BGB`, `ZPO`), the section (e.g. `§ 433`) and its title.
- (Node) `book_slug` (`2026`, law sections): the slug of the law book (e.g. `bgb`).
- (Edge) `count`: the number of times the citation was extracted.
citations: M. Ostendorff, T. Blume, S. Ostendorff, "Towards an Open Platform for Legal Information." Proceedings of the ACM/IEEE Joint Conference on Digital Libraries in 2020 (JCDL '20), 385-388 (2020)

datasets.name: opensanctions
datasets.description:
The network of the persons, companies, organizations and other entities of interest for sanctions screening and investigations of OpenSanctions, an open database that consolidates the sanctions lists of governments and international organizations, the lists of politically exposed persons (PEPs, politicians and their family members and close associates), lists of wanted criminals, debarred companies, and related corporate registry and ownership data, from more than 300 sources, with de-duplicated entities. The network is built from the `default` collection, the broadest one ("any entity that should receive enhanced public scrutiny"), in the version of 31 October 2026, in the FollowTheMoney (FtM) data model.

Each node is an FtM "thing": a person, a company, an organization, a legal entity of unknown kind, a public body, a political or public position, an address, a security, a vessel, an airplane, a crypto wallet, an asset, or an article, all of them included. Each directed edge is a relationship between two of them: either an FtM relationship entity, from its source to its target (`Occupancy`: holder → position; `Ownership`: owner → asset; `Directorship`: director → organization; `Employment`: employee → employer; `Membership`: member → organization; `Family`: person → relative; `Associate`: person → associate; `Representation`: agent → client; `Succession`: predecessor → successor; `UnknownLink`: subject → object; `Documentation`: entity → document; and the other relationship schemata, if any), or a reference from one thing to another (`addressEntity`: thing → its address; `holder`: holder → crypto wallet; `issuer`: issuer → security; `organization`: organization → position; `parent`: parent → organization; `operator` and `owner` of assets). The network is a multigraph. The relationships whose ends are not both in the collection (e.g. relatives that are not themselves of interest) are not included, and neither are the sanction records (`Sanction`, which link an entity to a sanctioning authority given as text; whether an entity is sanctioned is given by its topics), nor the identification documents, passports and other records that do not join two things.

The entities are compiled from many sources of different precision: the same person or company can still appear as several nodes when the sources could not be matched, and many PEP records lack exact dates of birth or full names. The data change daily; the version used is pinned (`20261031125407-kkl`).

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `entity_id`: the id of the entity in OpenSanctions (its page is `https://www.opensanctions.org/entities/<entity_id>/`).
- (Node) `schema`: its FtM schema (e.g. `Person`, `Company`, `Position`, `Vessel`).
- (Node) `name`: its caption (display name).
- (Node) `topics`: its topics (e.g. `sanction`, `role.pep`, `role.rca` for relatives and close associates, `crime`, `debarment`, `poi` for persons of interest).
- (Node) `countries`: its countries (two-letter codes, from the `country`, `jurisdiction`, `nationality` and `citizenship` properties).
- (Node) `birth_date` (persons): the first date of birth given (`YYYY`, `YYYY-MM` or `YYYY-MM-DD`; empty if none).
- (Node) `datasets`: the source datasets of OpenSanctions in which it appears.
- (Node) `is_target`: whether it is a "target" of screening (sanctioned, PEP, wanted, etc.), as opposed to a related entity.
- (Node) `first_seen`, `last_seen`, `last_change`: the times of its first and last appearance in the sources and of its last change (ISO 8601).
- (Node) `properties`: all its FtM properties, as a JSON object of lists of values.
- (Edge) `schema`: the FtM schema of the relationship (e.g. `Ownership`, `Family`), or the name of the referencing property (e.g. `addressEntity`).
- (Edge) `relation_id`: the id of the relationship entity (empty for references).
- (Edge) `role`: the role or kind of the relationship (`role` or `relationship` property, e.g. `father`, `subsidiary of`; empty if none).
- (Edge) `start_date`, `end_date`: the first start and end dates given (empty if none).
- (Edge) `datasets`: the source datasets of the relationship.
- (Edge) `properties`: all the FtM properties of the relationship entity, as a JSON object (empty for references).

datasets.name: opensky_flights
datasets.description:
Monthly networks of flights between airports worldwide, from January 2019 to December 2021, derived from the crowdsourced air traffic data of the OpenSky Network, a network of more than 2500 receivers of the ADS-B and Mode S messages broadcast by aircraft. The data were compiled by Strohmeier, Olive, Lübbe, Schäfer and Lenders to illustrate the development of air traffic during the COVID-19 pandemic (the version of the data set with anonymized aircraft information and a CC BY license, release v21.12, the last one of that version, which contains all the files of the earlier ones). The other version of the data set, with non-anonymized aircraft information, a non-commercial license, and later corrections, which extends to December 2022, is in the entry `opensky_flights_full`. It lists every flight seen by the network, with its origin and destination airports, which were inferred from the trajectory of the aircraft on takeoff and approach, without cross-checking with other sources.

Each network covers one month, and is named by it (e.g. `2020-04`); the month of a flight is the (UTC) day of the last message received from it. Nodes are airports, identified by their four-letter (ICAO) codes, and a directed edge from one airport to another is weighted by the number of flights from the first to the second in that month. The individual flights are aggregated into these weighted edges (about 49 million flights over the three years, of those whose origin and destination are known). Flights whose origin or destination airport could not be determined (which are many, e.g. flights that left the coverage of the network) are left out. Flights that took off and landed at the same airport (e.g. training or test flights) are kept as self-loops. Only airports with at least one flight in the month are included.

The names, positions and types of the airports come from the OurAirports database (public domain; a snapshot of January 2022), matched by their ICAO code or, failing that, by their GPS code; for airport codes that are not found there, these properties are empty (`NaN` for the coordinates).

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `code`: the four-letter code of the airport (as given by OpenSky).
- (Node) `name`: the name of the airport.
- (Node) `lat` and `lon`: its latitude and longitude.
- (Node) `type`: the type of airport in OurAirports (e.g. `large_airport`, `small_airport`, `heliport`).
- (Node) `country`: the ISO 3166-1 code of its country.
- (Edge) `weight`: the number of flights from the origin to the destination airport in the month.
citations: M. Strohmeier, X. Olive, J. Lübbe, M. Schäfer, V. Lenders, "Crowdsourced air traffic data from the OpenSky Network 2019–2020." Earth System Science Data 13(2), 357-366 (2021)

datasets.description:

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the name of the airport.
- (Node) `lat` and `lon`: its latitude and longitude.
- (Node) `type`: the type of airport in OurAirports (e.g. `large_airport`, `small_airport`, `heliport`).

datasets.name: openstreetmap
datasets.description:
Street networks of every city and town, county, urbanized area and census tract in the United States, constructed by G. Boeing from OpenStreetMap (OSM) data with the OSMnx software (version 0.8.1). For each area, all public drivable streets inside its boundary were downloaded from OSM, keeping all connected components; the boundaries are those of the 2017 TIGER/Line shapefiles of the U.S. Census Bureau. The data were released in 2018. The networks are topologically simplified: nodes are street intersections and dead ends (OSM nodes where streets merely bend are removed), and edges are the street segments between them, with their full shapes stored as geometries.

Each network corresponds to one area, named after the source archive and file, as in `01-AL-cities-street_networks:0100124_Abbeville` (state FIPS code, state abbreviation, spatial scale, and the area's census GEOID and name). There are 18,430 cities and towns, 2,952 counties, 450 urbanized areas and 69,208 census tracts (the Zillow neighborhoods of the upstream data are not included). The networks are directed multigraphs: a two-way street is represented by edges in both directions, a one-way street by an edge in its direction of travel, and parallel edges may connect the same pair of nodes.

The networks have the following properties (attributes that are missing in OSM are empty, and not every property is present in every network):

- (Node) `osmid`: the OSM ID of the node.
- (Node) `x`, `y`: the longitude and latitude of the node, in degrees.
- (Node) `highway`: the OSM highway tag of the node, e.g. "traffic_signals", "stop", "turning_circle".
- (Node) `ref`: the OSM reference tag of the node (e.g. a highway exit number).
- (Edge) `osmid`: the OSM ID of the way (or list of ways) that the edge belongs to.
- (Edge) `name`: the name of the street.
- (Edge) `highway`: the OSM highway type of the street, e.g. "motorway", "primary", "residential".
- (Edge) `oneway`: whether the street is one-way.
- (Edge) `length`: the length of the street segment, in meters.
- (Edge) `geometry`: the shape of the street segment as a WKT line string of longitude–latitude coordinates (empty for straight segments).
- (Edge) `lanes`, `maxspeed`, `ref`, `bridge`, `tunnel`, `junction`, `access`, `width`, `service`, `landuse`, etc.: the corresponding OSM tags of the street.
- (Node) `streets_per_node`: the number of streets that meet at the node (given as a graph-level attribute in the upstream GraphML files).
- (Graph) `area`: the identifier of the area, as in "01_AL_0100124_Abbeville".
- (Graph) `crs`, `simplified`: the coordinate reference system, and whether the graph was simplified.
citations: G. Boeing, "Street Network Models and Measures for Every U.S. City, County, Urbanized Area, Census Tract, and Zillow-Defined Neighborhood." Urban Science 3(1), 28 (2019)

datasets.name: oregon_as
datasets.description:
Weekly snapshots of the Internet at the level of Autonomous Systems (ASs), between March 31 and May 26 2001, as distributed by SNAP and used by Leskovec, Kleinberg and Faloutsos in their study of the evolution of networks over time. Nodes are ASs, and an undirected edge indicates that two ASs exchange traffic (peering relationship), as inferred from routing data.

- `oregon1_<date>`: 9 graphs inferred from the Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) tables collected by the University of Oregon Route Views project.
- `oregon2_<date>`: 9 graphs inferred from the Route Views BGP data combined with Looking Glass data and the Internet Routing Registry, which reveal many more peering links.

The dates are given as YYMMDD (from 010331 to 010526). Each AS is identified by its AS number, which is consistent across all graphs. As distributed, each graph contains one edge listed twice.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `as_number`: the AS number.
citations: J. Leskovec, J. Kleinberg, C. Faloutsos, "Graphs over time: densification laws, shrinking diameters and possible explanations." Proceedings of the 11th ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery in Data Mining (KDD), 177-187 (2005)
University of Oregon Route Views Project

datasets.name: packet_delays
datasets.description:
Measurements of the difference in delay experienced by packet probes sent over the Internet, from an experiment conducted by M. Coates and collaborators during a short period in 2001, from a desktop computer in the ECE department at Rice University to similar machines at ten university locations. The data were collected to test a method for inferring the topology of the Internet routing tree from end-to-end measurements, and are distributed with the book "Statistical Analysis of Network Data" by E. D. Kolaczyk.

Each probe consisted of two small packets, separated by one large packet: both small packets were sent to the same destination, while the large packet was sent to a different (or the same) destination. The difference in delay between the two small packets, caused by the large packet queueing in front of the second small packet, indicates how much of the path the two destinations share.

Nodes are the ten destination hosts: 1 = Instituto Superior Técnico (Portugal), 2 = Instituto de Telecomunicações (Portugal), 3 = University of California, Berkeley, 4 and 5 = Michigan State University (hosts 1 and 2), 6 = University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign, 7 and 8 = University of Wisconsin, Madison (hosts 1 and 2), 9 and 10 = Rice University (hosts 1 and 2). Each probe is a directed edge from the destination of the small packets to the destination of the large packet, so the network is a multigraph with self-loops, where each ordered pair of destinations is connected by between 57 and 125 edges.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the destination number, from 1 to 10.
- (Edge) `delay`: the difference in delay of the two small packets of the probe, in milliseconds (as stated in the source documentation).
citations: M. Coates et al., "Maximum likelihood network topology identification from edge-based unicast measurements." ACM SIGMETRICS Performance Evaluation Review 30(1), 11-20 (2002)

datasets.name: paris_transportation
datasets.description:
Multilayer transportation network of the Île-de-France region (Paris and its suburbs), constructed by F. Asgari and collaborators at Télécom SudParis to map sparse cellular phone trajectories onto transportation routes. It combines the road network, from the French National Geographic Institute (IGN), with the RER commuter rail, metro and tramway networks, from OpenStreetMap. Each node is a road intersection, a train station, a metro station or a tram station, and edges connect consecutive nodes along a road or line. Cross-layer edges connect nodes of different layers where a transition between transport modes is possible (e.g. between a station and a nearby road intersection). Edges marked as two-way in the source are represented by two directed edges, one in each direction, and one-way edges by a single edge from the first to the second endpoint listed in the source (the source does not distinguish one-way streets digitized against their direction of travel, so the direction of some one-way edges may be reversed). A few pairs of nodes are connected by more than one edge, and there are 3 self-loops.

The network was parsed from the upstream node and edge lists. (The upstream GraphML file is broken: there each edge connects a node to an additional node without attributes, whose identifier is the ID of the edge, because the columns of the edge list are mislabelled; the endpoints of each edge are in its first two columns, and the column labeled as the target contains the edge ID.)

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the node ID in the source data.
- (Node) `type`: the layer of the node, one of "road", "train", "metro" or "tram".
- (Node) `lat`, `lon`: the latitude and longitude of the node, in degrees (the corresponding columns are swapped in the source).
- (Edge) `type`: the layer of the edge, one of "road", "train", "metro", "tram" or "crosslayer".
- (Edge) `name`: the name of the road (e.g. "D1", "A86") or of the transit line (e.g. "RER A", "M7"), or "None".
citations: F. Asgari  et al., "CT-Mapper: Mapping sparse multimodal cellular trajectories using a multilayer transportation network." Computer Communications 95, 69-81 (2016)

datasets.name: parker_asher_classrooms
datasets.description:
Friendships among the children of three elementary school classes, from the study of J. G. Parker and S. R. Asher, who collected network data from 881 children in 36 classrooms of the third, fourth and fifth grades in five public elementary schools in the US Midwest. Each child was given a roster of the children in the class, and was asked to choose his or her "very best friend", three "best friends", and an unlimited number of "friends". C. J. Anderson, S. Wasserman and B. Crouch (1999) selected three of the classrooms, one of each grade, and ignored the distinctions between the types of friendship. The data were distributed by L. C. Freeman on his network data page at the University of California, Irvine (no longer online), from which this version was obtained via the Internet Archive.

- `third`, `fourth`, `fifth`: the classrooms of the third, fourth and fifth grades.

A directed edge (i, j) indicates that child i named child j as a very best friend, best friend or friend.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `boy`: whether the child is a boy.
citations: J. G. Parker, S. R. Asher, "Friendship and friendship quality in middle childhood: Links with peer group acceptance and feelings of loneliness and social dissatisfaction." Developmental Psychology 29(4), 611-621 (1993)
C. J. Anderson, S. Wasserman, B. Crouch, "A p* primer: logit models for social networks." Social Networks 21(1), 37-66 (1999)

datasets.name: parlnet
datasets.description:
Networks of legislative cosponsorship among the members of 27 parliamentary chambers of 19 European countries and Israel, from the parlnet project of F. Briatte, one network per chamber and legislature (150 networks, covering legislatures that started between 1983 and 2015). The bills (mostly private bills, and in some chambers also government bills, motions or resolutions) and their sponsors were scraped from the websites and open data portals of the parliaments. Only bills with at least two sponsors are used. Nodes are members of parliament (MPs) who sponsored at least one such bill, and a directed edge $(i,j)$ means that MP $i$ cosponsored at least one bill whose first author was MP $j$ (the first author of each bill is connected to every other sponsor of the bill, and not the cosponsors among themselves). In the Austrian Nationalrat, only the MPs who filed the bills are known, not the further supporters. Party affiliations that changed during a legislature are recorded as the longest one, and some parties are recoded as parliamentary groups (see the appendix of the paper). MPs with the same name are distinguished by a suffix (e.g. "-1").

The networks are named after the country (ISO code), the chamber when the country has two (e.g. `fr_an` for the French Assemblée nationale, `fr_se` for the French Sénat, `it_ca` and `it_se`, `cz_po` and `cz_se`, `ch_cn` and `ch_cs`, `be_ch` and `be_se`, `ie_da` and `ie_se`, `ro_ca` and `ro_se`), and the first year of the legislature, e.g. `at1995`, `fr_an2012`, `se2014`.

The data come from the file `parlnet.rda` of the project's repository (commit `7c2cf94`, April 2017), which also contains, for 123 of the networks, "committee co-membership" networks (objects `conet_*`): these contain exactly the same ties as the corresponding cosponsorship networks (each directed tie as an undirected edge), with the number of committees shared by the two MPs as their only attribute, which is included here as the edge property `committee` of the cosponsorship networks, so they are not included separately. The local paths of the MPs' photographs, and two bookkeeping vertex attributes of the Finnish networks (`party_length`, `constituency_length`), are also left out.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Graph) `country`: the country.
- (Graph) `chamber`: the chamber's name as a Wikipedia page title, in the language `lang`.
- (Graph) `chamber_type`: `Lower`, `Upper` or `Unicameral`.
- (Graph) `legislature`: its number or name.
- (Graph) `years`: the period of the legislature.
- (Graph) `lang`: the language of the Wikipedia titles of the chamber and constituencies.
- (Graph) `ipu`: the identifier of the chamber in the IPU PARLINE database.
- (Graph) `seats`: the statutory number of seats.
- (Graph) `n_cosponsored`: the number of cosponsored bills.
- (Node) `name`: the name of the MP.
- (Node) `sex`: `F` or `M`.
- (Node) `born`: the year of birth (-1 if unknown).
- (Node) `party`: the abbreviation of the MP's party.
- (Node) `partyname`: the name of the party.
- (Node) `lr`: the Left/Right score of the party, from 0 (left) to 10 (right), from the ParlGov database (NaN if not available).
- (Node) `constituency`: the MP's constituency, generally as a Wikipedia page title (empty if not available, e.g. in the Belgian Senate).
- (Node) `nyears`: the seniority of the MP, in years in the same chamber before the legislature (-1 if unknown).
- (Node) `url`: the address of the MP's profile on the website of the parliament.
- (Node) `n_au`, `n_co`, `n_bills`: the numbers of cosponsored bills on which the MP is the first author, a cosponsor, and either.
- (Edge) `weight`: the number of bills first-authored by $j$ and cosponsored by $i$.
- (Edge) `nfw`: the "Newman-Fowler" weight, $\sum_k Y_{ij}(k)/c_j(k)$, where $c_j(k)$ is the number of cosponsors of the $k$-th bill of $j$, and $Y_{ij}(k)=1$ if $i$ is one of them.
- (Edge) `gsw`: the "Gross-Shalizi" weight, the Newman-Fowler weight divided by its maximum, $\sum_k 1/c_j(k)$ (between 0 and 1).
- (Edge) `committee`: the number of parliamentary committees of which both MPs are members (only in the 123 networks where committee memberships are available).
citations: F. Briatte, "Network patterns of legislative collaboration in twenty parliaments." Network Science 4(2), 266-271 (2016)

datasets.name: patentsview
datasets.description:
The utility, design, plant and reissue patents granted by the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) since 1976, their citations, inventors, assignees and technology classes, from the bulk data of PatentsView (the patent data platform of the USPTO), in a third-party copy: the tables were downloaded from PatentsView, processed and redistributed on Hugging Face by DataForge (data.zalize.com), as of August 2026. (PatentsView's own downloads now require an API key of the USPTO Open Data Portal.) The entry `us_patents` has the earlier citation network of 1975-1999 of the NBER.

- `citations`: the citation network: a directed edge goes from a patent to each patent it cites (U.S. patents only; the citations of foreign patents and of the scientific literature are not included). Cited patents that are not in the table of patents (e.g. granted before 1976) are nodes without metadata.
- `inventors`: the undirected bipartite network of the patents and their inventors, as disambiguated by PatentsView.
- `assignees`: the undirected bipartite network of the patents and their assignees (the owners of the patents: companies, universities, government agencies, individuals), as disambiguated by PatentsView.
- `cpc`: the undirected bipartite network of the patents and the groups of the Cooperative Patent Classification (CPC) to which they belong.
- `company_citations`: the citations between companies, aggregated by DataForge: a directed edge goes from a company group (the assignees harmonized and grouped by company by DataForge) to a company group whose patents its patents cite, weighted by the number of citations (only the pairs with at least a minimum number of citations given by DataForge).

The texts of the patents (abstracts) and the derived statistics of DataForge (citation metrics, trends per class) are left out.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `is_patent` (bipartite networks): whether the node is a patent (otherwise an inventor, assignee or CPC group).
- (Node) `name`: the patent number (e.g. `10000000`, `D1006496` for design patents, `RE49999` for reissues), the PatentsView identifier of the inventor or of the assignee, the CPC group (e.g. `H04L63/0428`), or the name of the company group.
- (Node) `title` (patents, `citations`): the title of the patent.
- (Node) `patent_type` (patents, `citations`): `utility`, `design`, `plant`, `reissue`, ...
- (Node) `wipo_kind` (patents, `citations`): the kind code, e.g. `B2`.
- (Node) `grant_date`, `filing_date` (patents, `citations`): the dates of grant and filing (Unix time, -1 if unknown).
- (Node) `num_claims` (patents, `citations`): the number of claims (-1 if unknown).
- (Node) `withdrawn` (patents, `citations`): whether the patent was withdrawn.
- (Node) `cpc_subclass` (patents, `citations`): the primary CPC subclass.
- (Node) `wipo_field` (patents, `citations`): the WIPO technology field.
- (Node) `assignee` (patents, `citations`): the harmonized name of the first assignee.
- (Node) `assignee_country` (patents, `citations`): the country of the first assignee.
- (Node) `inventor_country` (patents, `citations`): the country of the first inventor.
- (Node) In the bipartite networks, patents have only their `name`.
- (Edge) `date` (`citations`): the date of the cited patent given in the citation (Unix time, -1 if unknown).
- (Edge) `category` (`citations`): who gave the citation: `cited by applicant`, `cited by examiner`, `cited by other`, `cited by third party`, `imported from a related application`, or empty if unknown.
- (Node) `first_name`, `last_name`, `country` (inventors): the name and the country of the inventor (of their first record).
- (Edge) `sequence` (bipartite networks): the position of the inventor, assignee or CPC group in the list of the patent.
- (Node) `assignee_name`, `name_harmonized` (assignees): the name of the assignee, as given and harmonized.
- (Node) `group` (assignees): the company group of DataForge.
- (Node) `is_individual` (assignees): whether the assignee is an individual.
- (Node) `assignee_type` (assignees): the USPTO assignee type code, e.g. 2 for a U.S. company, 3 for a foreign company, 6 for the U.S. government.
- (Node) `country`, `state`, `city` (assignees): the location of the assignee.
- (Node) `section`, `class`, `subclass` (CPC groups): the CPC section, class and subclass of the group.
- (Edge) `cpc_type` (`cpc`): `inventional` or `additional`.
- (Node) `n_patents`, `first_grant_year`, `last_grant_year`, `country`, `top_cpc_subclasses` (company groups, `company_citations`): the number of patents, the years of the first and last grants, the country and the top CPC subclasses of the group, from the company profiles of DataForge (empty, or -1, if missing).
- (Edge) `weight`, `first_year`, `last_year` (`company_citations`): the number of citations, and the first and last year of the citations.
citations: PatentsView (U.S. Patent and Trademark Office); packaged by DataForge, "US Patents, Citations & Assignee Graph (USPTO / PatentsView)." Zenodo (2026)

datasets.name: paul_revere
datasets.description:
Memberships of 254 persons in colonial Boston in seven organisations at the time of the American Revolution (the St Andrews Lodge of freemasons, the Loyal Nine, the North Caucus, the Long Room Club, the Tea Party participants, the Boston Committee of Correspondence and the London Enemies list), from Appendix D of David Hackett Fischer's book "Paul Revere's Ride" (1994). The membership matrix was transcribed by Kieran Healy in 2013 for his analysis of how metadata can be used to identify Paul Revere as a central figure, and distributed with that analysis and in the UCINET datasets collection (University of Manchester). Healy's transcription contains errors in the memberships of several persons; a corrected matrix, transcribed again from Fischer's appendix by C. Brunson, replaced it in Healy's repository in 2015 (with 319 instead of 334 memberships; e.g. 16 persons are common to the London Enemies list and the North Caucus, not 20).

- `membership`: bipartite network of persons and the organizations they belonged to, from the original (2013, uncorrected) transcription, as distributed by UCINET.
- `co_membership`: one-mode projection of `membership`, connecting persons who belonged to the same organizations, as distributed by UCINET.
- `membership_corrected`: bipartite network of persons and organizations, from the corrected (2015) transcription.
- `whigs`: the subnetwork of `membership_corrected` used by Brunson (2015), which excludes the Tea Party participants and the London Enemies list (treated as non-group affiliations in the data preparation of Brunson's `bitriad` R package), and the persons not belonging to any of the remaining five organizations (136 persons, 160 memberships).

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the name of the person, as "Surname.Firstname", or of the organization.
- (Node) `is_organization` (bipartite networks): true for the organizations.
- (Edge) `weight` (`co_membership` only): the number of organizations shared by the two persons.[^ucinet].

[^ucinet]: Description obtained in part from the [UCINET datasets page](https://sites.google.com/site/ucinetsoftware/datasets/covert-networks/paul-revere).
citations: D. H. Fischer, "Paul Revere's Ride." Oxford University Press (1994)
K. Healy, "Using Metadata to Find Paul Revere." (2013)
C. Brunson, "Triadic analysis of affiliation networks." Network Science 3(4), 480-508 (2015)

datasets.name: pchic_blood_cells
datasets.description:
Networks of chromatin contacts between promoters and other regions of the human genome, measured with Promoter Capture Hi-C (PCHi-C) in 17 types of primary blood cells (and their progenitors) by Javierre et al., to link enhancers and non-coding disease variants to the genes they regulate. In Hi-C, the DNA of the cells is cross-linked, cut with the restriction enzyme HindIII, and ligated, so that pairs of fragments that are close in the three-dimensional nucleus are sequenced together; in Capture Hi-C, the ligation products are enriched for the fragments that contain a promoter (the "baits", fragments that contain annotated promoters). Significant interactions were called with CHiCAGO, whose score (a soft-thresholded $-\log$ $p$-value) is given per cell type.

Nodes are HindIII restriction fragments of the genome (GRCh37 assembly), and a directed edge goes from a bait to a fragment it interacts with (the "other end"), with the CHiCAGO scores of the interaction in the cell types. Interactions between two baits are detected from the point of view of each bait, so that they can appear in both directions.

- `cutoff5`: the interactions with a score of at least 5 (the threshold of the study) in at least one cell type.
- `cutoff0`: all the interactions with a positive score in at least one cell type (the unthresholded data).
- `reciprocal_cutoff0`: the interactions of the reciprocal capture experiment, in which fragments that interact with promoters (mostly enhancers) were captured as baits, in four cell types (megakaryocytes, erythroblasts, activated and non-activated CD4+ T cells), with a positive score in at least one of them.
- `pchic_vs_rchic`: the interactions between the baits of PCHi-C and the baits of the reciprocal capture, with their scores in both experiments, from the point of view of PCHi-C (edges go from the PCHi-C bait to the reciprocal bait), for the four cell types of the reciprocal capture.

The cell types (abbreviations of the score properties) are: `Mon` (monocytes), `Mac0`, `Mac1`, `Mac2` (macrophages M0, M1 and M2), `Neu` (neutrophils), `MK` (megakaryocytes), `EP` (endothelial precursors), `Ery` (erythroblasts), `FoeT` (fetal thymus), `nCD4`, `tCD4`, `aCD4`, `naCD4` (naive, total, activated and non-activated CD4+ T cells), `nCD8`, `tCD8` (naive and total CD8+ T cells), `nB`, `tB` (naive and total B cells).

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `fragment_id`: the identifier of the restriction fragment (from the restriction map of the capture design).
- (Node) `chr`, `start`, `end`: the chromosome and the coordinates of the fragment (GRCh37).
- (Node) `genes`: the genes whose promoters are in the fragment, separated by `;` (Ensembl release 75; empty for fragments without annotated promoters).
- (Node) `is_bait`: whether the fragment is a bait of the experiment (in `pchic_vs_rchic`: a PCHi-C bait).
- (Edge) `dist`: the distance between the bait and the other end (positive if the bait is upstream of the other end; NaN for interactions between chromosomes).
- (Edge) `Mon`, `Mac0`, ..., `tB`: the CHiCAGO scores of the interaction in each cell type (in `pchic_vs_rchic`: `PCHiC_MK`, ..., `rCHiC_MK`, ... for the two experiments).
- (Edge) `cluster_id`, `cluster_post_prob` (`cutoff5`): the cluster of the interaction in the clustering of the interactions by their scores across cell types (with AutoClass, Figure 2B of the paper), and the posterior probability of the assignment.
- (Edge) `is_b2b` (`reciprocal_cutoff0`): whether the interaction is between two baits.
citations: B. M. Javierre, O. S. Burren, S. P. Wilder, R. Kreuzhuber, S. M. Hill, S. Sewitz, J. Cairns, S. W. Wingett, C. Várnai, M. J. Thiecke, et al., "Lineage-Specific Genome Architecture Links Enhancers and Non-coding Disease Variants to Target Gene Promoters." Cell 167, 1369-1384.e19 (2016)

datasets.name: peeringdb
datasets.description:
Networks of the interconnection facilities of the Internet from PeeringDB, the database maintained by network operators in which they register their networks (autonomous systems), the Internet exchange points (IXPs) where they exchange traffic, and the colocation facilities (data centers) where they are present, from the daily snapshots archived by CAIDA since July 2010. There is one network per month, from the first snapshot of the month in the archive (from 29 July 2010 to 1 October 2026, 195 snapshots), and the latest snapshot (30 October 2026). The networks are named after the date of their snapshot (e.g. `2020_01_01`). As the archive's README explains, the snapshots from 22 January to 9 August 2017 are not fully up to date, and those from October 2017 to March 2018 repeat the data of 9 October 2017 (they are kept, as they are in the archive); there are no snapshots in April 2016.

Nodes are networks (as registered, each with its AS number), IXPs, facilities and, from 2017 on, organizations (the companies that operate them; the older format of the database, used until March 2016, has no organizations).
