The data were compiled by M. Cantor and collaborators for a study of nestedness across levels of biological organization, and are distributed in the repository of that study (file `pop_hyena.txt`). Individuals were identified by photo-identification of natural markings (unique spot patterns), and two individuals were considered associated when observed in the same group. Nodes are individuals, and an undirected edge connects two individuals that were observed together at least once, weighted by their association index, the twice-weight index (TWI), an estimate of the proportion of time the two individuals spend together (from 0, never seen together, to 1, always together). To avoid spurious associations, only individuals observed more than five times, all from a single well-sampled clan, are included. The individuals are identified only by anonymous numeric labels. The source data list 585 pairs of individuals with nonzero association, among 36 individuals (the accompanying documentation states 35).

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the numeric label of the individual in the source data.
- (Edge) `weight`: the twice-weight association index.
citations: K. E. Holekamp, J. E. Smith, C. C. Strelioff, R. C. Van Horn, H. E. Watts, "Society, demography and genetic structure in the spotted hyena." Molecular Ecology 21, 613-632 (2012)
K. E. Holekamp, J. E. Smith, C. C. Strelioff, R. C. Van Horn, H. E. Watts, "Data from: Society, demography and genetic structure in the spotted hyena." Dryad Digital Repository (2011)

M. Cantor, M. M. Pires, F. M. D. Marquitti, R. L. G. Raimundo, E. Sebastián-González, P. P. Coltri, S. I. Perez, D. R. Barneche, D. Y. C. Brandt, K. Nunes, F. G. Daura-Jorge, S. R. Floeter, P. R. Guimarães Jr., "Nestedness across biological scales." PLoS ONE 12(2), e0171691 (2017)

datasets.name: stackexchange_answers
datasets.description:
Bipartite networks of users of question-and-answer sites of the Stack Exchange network and the questions they answered, assembled by A. R. Benson and collaborators from Stack Exchange data. Users and questions are anonymized and given only as integer indices.

- `mathoverflow`: users of MathOverflow (mathoverflow.net, a site for research-level mathematics), each connected to every question they answered. Questions carry the tags assigned to them on the site.
- `stackoverflow`: the same construction for Stack Overflow (stackoverflow.com, a site for programming questions).
- `algebra`, `geometry`: users of MathOverflow who answered questions whose tags match the patterns "\*algebra\*" (e.g. `lie-algebras`, `ac.commutative-algebra`) or "\*geometry\*" (e.g. `ag.algebraic-geometry`, `complex-geometry`), respectively, obtained from the MathOverflow data dumps. The answers were split into calendar months, and for each month and each matching tag there is a group node connected to all users who answered a question with that tag during that month. The same tag can therefore give rise to many groups (one per month in which it received answers), and identical sets of users can appear in several groups. The answers span the years 2009 to 2019, but the month of each group is not given in the source data. Users who belong to no group were removed.

The source pages do not state when the `mathoverflow` and `stackoverflow` data were collected; the data were released in 2020.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `is_question` (`mathoverflow`, `stackoverflow`): whether the node is a question (otherwise a user).
- (Node) `tags` (`mathoverflow`, `stackoverflow`): the list of tags of each question (empty for users).
- (Node) `is_group` (`algebra`, `geometry`): whether the node is a group of users who answered questions with a given tag in a given month (otherwise a user).
- (Node) `tag` (`algebra`, `geometry`): the question tag of the group (empty for users).
citations: N. Veldt, A. R. Benson, J. Kleinberg, "Minimizing Localized Ratio Cut Objectives in Hypergraphs." Proceedings of the 26th ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery & Data Mining, 1708-1718 (2020)
I. Amburg, N. Veldt, A. R. Benson, "Diverse and Experienced Group Discovery via Hypergraph Clustering." Proceedings of the 2022 SIAM International Conference on Data Mining (SDM), 145-153 (2022)

datasets.name: stackexchange_tags
datasets.description:
Bipartite networks of questions and the tags attached to them on three question-and-answer sites of the Stack Exchange network, assembled by A. R. Benson and collaborators from the Stack Exchange data dump (archive.org), covering the complete history of each site up to August 2017. Each question carries between one and five tags indicating its topics, and is connected to its tags, and is timestamped with its creation time.

- `ask_ubuntu`: Ask Ubuntu (askubuntu.com), a site for questions about the Ubuntu operating system. Questions span January 2009 to August 2017 (only five questions, migrated from other sites, predate the launch of the site in July 2010).
- `math_sx`: Mathematics Stack Exchange (math.stackexchange.com). Questions span March 2010 to August 2017 (only one question, migrated from another site, predates the launch of the site in July 2010).
- `stack_overflow`: Stack Overflow (stackoverflow.com), a site for programming questions. Questions span July 2008 to August 2017.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `is_question`: whether the node is a question (otherwise a tag).
- (Node) `name` (tags): the name of the tag.
- (Node) `post_id` (questions): the post id of the question on its site (so that, e.g., question 1 of `ask_ubuntu` is https://askubuntu.com/questions/1).
- (Node) `time` (questions): the creation time of the question, in Unix time (seconds since 1970-01-01 UTC). The source data give the times in milliseconds relative to the earliest question; they were converted to absolute times by matching the creation times of a sample of the questions, obtained from the Stack Exchange API (the conversion is accurate to within one second).
citations: A. R. Benson, R. Abebe, M. T. Schaub, A. Jadbabaie, J. Kleinberg, "Simplicial closure and higher-order link prediction." Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 115(48), E11221-E11230 (2018)

datasets.name: stackexchange_threads
datasets.description:
Bipartite networks of users and the question threads they took part in, on three question-and-answer sites of the Stack Exchange network, assembled by A. R. Benson and collaborators from the Stack Exchange data dump (archive.org), covering the history of each site up to August 2017. Only the threads in which the question and all its answers were posted within 24 hours are included; each such thread is connected to the user who asked the question and to the users who answered it, and is timestamped with the time of the question.

- `ask_ubuntu`: Ask Ubuntu (askubuntu.com), a site for questions about the Ubuntu operating system. Threads span December 2009 to August 2017.
- `math_sx`: Mathematics Stack Exchange (math.stackexchange.com). Threads span July 2010 to August 2017.
- `stack_overflow`: Stack Overflow (stackoverflow.com), a site for programming questions. Threads span August 2008 to August 2017.
- `stack_overflow_25`: the version of `stack_overflow` distributed by the source restricted to the threads with at most 25 users, which leaves out 13 threads (with 26 to 67 users), and the users who took part only in those. Its file of question ids is empty; the question ids were taken from the full version, whose other threads are the same, in the same order.

The users are anonymous (they are identified only by an index of the source data). A user who both asked and answered a question is connected to its thread once.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `is_thread`: whether the node is a thread (otherwise a user).
- (Node) `question_id` (threads): the post id of the question on its site (so that, e.g., question 1 of `ask_ubuntu` is https://askubuntu.com/questions/1).
- (Node) `time` (threads): the time of the question, in Unix time (seconds since 1970-01-01 UTC). The source data give the times in milliseconds relative to the earliest question; they were converted to absolute times by matching the creation times of a sample of the questions, obtained from the Stack Exchange API (the conversion is accurate to about one second, but for a few questions, e.g. migrated from other sites, the times of the data differ from the creation times of the API by up to a few hours).
citations: A. R. Benson, R. Abebe, M. T. Schaub, A. Jadbabaie, J. Kleinberg, "Simplicial closure and higher-order link prediction." Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 115(48), E11221-E11230 (2018)

datasets.name: stackoverflow
datasets.description:
A bipartite network of users and the questions they marked as favorites on Stack Overflow, the question-and-answer website on computer programming of the Stack Exchange network. Users of Stack Overflow could mark a question as a "favorite" (a feature later renamed "bookmarks") to follow it and find it again later. The data are from the Stack Exchange data dump of December 2011, which contains the public content of the site from its start in July 2008 to early December 2011, published by Stack Exchange under the CC BY-SA 3.0 license. Nodes are users and questions, and an undirected edge connects a user to a question that the user had marked as favorite at the time of the dump, timestamped with the day it was marked. Favorites that were later removed are not in the data.

Only the users with at least one favorite and the questions that are a favorite of at least one user are included. The favorites of 17,359 questions that are not in the dump (presumably deleted after being marked, while the votes were kept) are included, but these questions have no metadata.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `is_user`: whether the node is a user (otherwise it is a question).
- (Node) `so_id`: the Stack Overflow id of the user or question (users have pages at `https://stackoverflow.com/users/<so_id>`, and questions at `https://stackoverflow.com/questions/<so_id>`).
- (Node) `created`: the creation time of the user account or the question (Unix time; -1 if unknown).
- (Node) `name` (users): the display name of the user.
- (Node) `reputation` (users): the reputation score of the user (-1 if unknown).
- (Node) `title`, `tags` (questions): the title and the tags of the question (as written on the site, e.g. `<c#><winforms>`).
- (Node) `score` (questions): the score (up votes minus down votes) of the question.
- (Node) `views` (questions): the number of times it was viewed.
- (Node) `missing` (questions): whether the question is absent from the dump (then `title` and `tags` are empty, `created` and `views` are -1, and `score` is 0).
- (Edge) `time`: the day at which the user marked the question as favorite (Unix time of midnight UTC).
citations: Stack Exchange, Inc., "Stack Exchange Data Dump - Dec 2011."

datasets.name: stanford_web
datasets.description: The web graph of Stanford University (stanford.edu), as collected in 2002. Nodes represent pages and a directed edge from page A to page B represents a hyperlink in A pointing to B.
citations: J. Leskovec, K. Lang, A. Dasgupta, M. Mahoney. Community Structure in Large Networks: Natural Cluster Sizes and the Absence of Large Well-Defined Clusters. Internet Mathematics 6(1) 29--123, 2009

datasets.name: star_wars
datasets.description:
Networks of the characters of the first seven Star Wars films (Episodes I to VII, released from 1977 to 2015), extracted by Evelina Gabasova from the film screenplays available in the Internet Movie Script Database (IMSDb). The screenplays (drafts that sometimes differ from the final films) were split into scenes at their "INT." and "EXT." scene headers, and the names of the characters were identified in each scene, using a manually compiled list of aliases to merge different names of the same character (e.g. Palpatine, Darth Sidious and the Emperor are a single node, as are Amidala and Padmé; Anakin and Darth Vader are, however, kept as separate nodes). Nodes are characters, and an edge connects two characters that occur together in at least one scene, weighted by the number of such scenes. The networks are undirected.

There are four kinds of networks, for each episode (`episode1` to `episode7`) and for all the episodes together (`full`):

- `*_interactions`: two characters are connected if they both speak in the same scene.
- `*_interactions_all`: as `interactions`, with R2-D2 and Chewbacca (who do not have spoken lines in the screenplays) added using the data of the `mentions` network.
- `*_mentions`: two characters are connected if they are both mentioned (by name) in the same scene.
- `full_interactions_all_merged`: as `full_interactions_all`, with Anakin and Darth Vader merged into a single node ("DARTH VADER").

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the name of the character.
- (Node) `scenes`: the number of scenes in which the character appears (speaks or is mentioned, according to the network type).
- (Node) `colour`: the color of the node in the author's visualizations (main characters have distinct colors, all others are gray).
- (Edge) `weight`: the number of scenes in which both characters appear.
citations: E. Gabasova, "Star Wars social network." Zenodo, version 1.0.1 (2016)

datasets.name: statsbomb
steam
datasets.description:
Networks of the users of Steam, the video game distribution platform of Valve, and the games (and other products, such as soundtracks and add-ons) they reviewed or own, collected by J. McAuley and colleagues (University of California, San Diego) from the public pages of the Steam store and community.

There are four networks:

- `reviews`: the reviews of games on Steam (version 2 of the data, collected for Kang and McAuley 2018), 7.8 million reviews by 2.6 million users of 15 thousand games, from 2010 to January 2018. A directed edge from a user to a game is a review. Users are identified by their Steam user id where it is given with the review (for about 40% of the reviews), otherwise by their user name; since user names need not be unique, and a user may appear with and without id, user nodes do not correspond exactly to users.
- `ownership`: the games owned by 88,310 users of Australia (version 1 of the data, collected for Wan and McAuley 2018 and Pathak et al. 2017), with the time played. A directed edge from a user to a game means that the user owns the game. the 673 users listed twice are included once (with their first listing), which leaves 5.09 of the 5.15 million ownership records.
- `australian_reviews`: the reviews written by 25,799 of these Australian users (59,305 reviews), with their recommendation and the ratings by other users.
- `bundles`: the 615 bundles of games sold together on Steam (as listed by SteamDB), and the 3,525 items in them. A directed edge from a bundle to a game means that the game is part of the bundle.

All networks are bipartite. The games have the metadata of the Steam store (as collected in early 2018) where available; the texts of the reviews are not included.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `is_user` (`reviews`, `ownership`, `australian_reviews`): whether the node is a user (otherwise it is a game).
- (Node) `is_bundle` (`bundles`): whether the node is a bundle (otherwise it is a game).
- (Node) `id`: the Steam user id or user name of a user, the Steam application id of a game, or the id of a bundle.
- (Node) `name` (games and bundles): the name of the game or bundle.
- (Node) `products` (users of `reviews`): the number of products of the user, as shown with the review (the largest value over the user's reviews).
- (Node) `genres`, `tags`, `specs` (games): the genres, user-defined tags and features of the game in the store, comma-separated.
- (Node) `developer`, `publisher`, `release_date`, `sentiment` (games): as given in the store (e.g. `Mostly Positive`).
- (Node) `price` (games): the price of the game in US dollars (NaN if not given or not a number, e.g. free to play).
- (Node) `metascore` (games): the Metacritic score of the game (-1 if not given).
- (Node) `early_access` (games): whether the game was in early access.
- (Node) `bundle_price`, `bundle_final_price` (bundles): the price of the bundle without and with its discount, in US dollars.
- (Node) `genre` (games of `bundles`): the genres of the game, as given with the bundle.
- (Edge) `time` (`reviews`): the date of the review, as Unix time.
- (Edge) `hours` (`reviews`): the hours played by the user at the time of the review (NaN if not given).
- (Edge) `recommended` (`reviews`): whether the user recommends the game.
- (Edge) `early_access` (`reviews`): whether the review was written while the game was in early access.
- (Edge) `found_funny` (`reviews`): the number of users who found the review funny (0 if not given).
- (Edge) `compensation` (`reviews`): the compensation of the reviewer, e.g. `Product received for free` (empty if none).
- (Edge) `playtime_forever`, `playtime_2weeks` (`ownership`): the time played by the user, in total and in the last two weeks, in minutes.
- (Edge) `posted`, `last_edited` (`australian_reviews`): the dates of the review, as shown on Steam (e.g. `Posted November 5, 2011.`; without the year for reviews of the year of collection).
- (Edge) `recommend` (`australian_reviews`): whether the user recommends the game.
- (Edge) `funny`, `helpful` (`australian_reviews`): the ratings of the review by other users, as shown on Steam (e.g. `15 of 20 people (75%) found this review helpful`).
- (Edge) `discounted_price` (`bundles`): the price of the game in the bundle, in US dollars.
citations: W.-C. Kang, J. McAuley, "Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation." 2018 IEEE International Conference on Data Mining (ICDM), 197-206 (2018)
M. Wan, J. McAuley, "Item recommendation on monotonic behavior chains." Proceedings of the 12th ACM Conference on Recommender Systems (RecSys), 86-94 (2018)

A. Pathak, K. Gupta, J. McAuley, "Generating and Personalizing Bundle Recommendations on Steam." Proceedings of the 40th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval, 1073-1076 (2017)

datasets.name: stem_forma_mentis
datasets.description:
Forma mentis networks (semantic networks of free associations annotated with the emotional valence of each concept) of 159 Italian high-school students (in their final year, aged 18 to 19) and 59 early-career international STEM researchers (doctoral students and post-docs working with quantitative methods on complex systems), from Stella et al. Each participant took part in a continuous free association task, in which they gave three associated words for each of 50 cue words: 10 cues common to all participants (mathematics, complex, physics, chemistry, system, biology, life, art, school and university), and 40 drawn at random from 390 frequent words of the Wikipedia pages on complex systems, physics, mathematics, biology, chemistry and psychology. The students answered in Italian, and the researchers in English. Each node is a word (converted to lowercase, spell-checked, and normalized to singular forms), and an undirected edge connects a cue to an associated response. Afterwards, the participants rated the valence of the cues and responses on a scale from 1 (very negative) to 5 (very positive). The following networks are included:

- `students`: all associations given by the students.
- `students_filtered`: only the associations given by at least two different students.
- `researchers`: all associations given by the researchers.
- `researchers_filtered`: the filtered network of the researchers, as distributed with the data (the paper analyzes only the unfiltered network of researchers, due to the smaller sample size).

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the word.
- (Node) `valence`: the valence category of the word ("Positive", "Neutral" or "Negative"). A word was labeled as positive (negative) if its median valence score was higher (lower) than that of the remaining words, according to a Kruskal-Wallis test at significance level 0.1, and neutral otherwise. The labels come from the valence files of the complete networks, and are empty for the few words that are missing from them (1 word in each complete network, and 13 in each filtered network, which contain a few words in different forms).
citations: M. Stella, S. De Nigris, A. Aloric, C. S. Q. Siew, "Forma mentis networks quantify crucial differences in STEM perception between students and experts." PLOS ONE 14(10), e0222870 (2019)

datasets.name: stitch_chemicals
datasets.description:
Networks of known and predicted associations between chemicals, and between chemicals and proteins, from STITCH ("search tool for interactions of chemicals"), version 5.0, the companion database of STRING (see the entries `string_all` and `string_ppi`). The chemicals are those of PubChem; STITCH merges the salt forms of a compound, and distinguishes the stereo-specific compounds (identifiers `CIDs...`) from the "flat" compounds whose stereoisomers are merged (`CIDm...`); the suffix is the PubChem compound identifier (CID). The proteins are those of STRING 10.

STITCH combines evidence from several channels, each of which gives a confidence score, into a combined confidence score: experiments (e.g. binding affinities from ChEMBL, PDSP Ki, PDB), curated databases (e.g. DrugBank, KEGG, GLIDA, Matador, CTD), co-mention in the scientific literature (text mining), and, for protein-chemical links, predictions (e.g. from co-occurrence in pathways), and, for chemical-chemical links, the structural similarity of the chemicals. Scores are multiplied by 1000 (the lowest combined score in the files is 150).

- `chemical_chemical`: an undirected network of chemicals, with an edge between two associated chemicals (both orientations of each pair are listed upstream; each pair is an edge once). A few chemicals (34) are associated with themselves, as self-loops.
- `protein_chemical_<taxid>`: a bipartite network of the chemicals and the proteins of an organism, with an edge between a chemical and a protein associated with it. STITCH has such networks for 2,031 organisms (31 GB of files); only those of the seven model organisms of the entry `string_ppi` are included, named after their NCBI taxonomy identifiers: `9606` (human), `10090` (mouse), `4932` (yeast *Saccharomyces cerevisiae*), `511145` (*Escherichia coli* K-12 MG1655), `7227` (fruit fly *Drosophila melanogaster*), `6239` (*Caenorhabditis elegans*) and `3702` (*Arabidopsis thaliana*).

The scores of the channels of the protein-chemical associations include evidence transferred from other organisms by orthology (e.g. an experiment on a mouse protein also supports the association with its human ortholog); a separate file of STITCH splits each of them into its direct and its transferred part, which are included as edge properties. The modes of action of the protein-chemical associations (e.g. binding, activation, inhibition), which STITCH gives for a subset of them (e.g. for 1.4 million of the 3.5 million associations of yeast), are included as edge properties, as lists with one entry per mode of action. STITCH lists each mode of action in both orientations of the pair, with a flag that tells whether the first item is the acting one (e.g. the chemical inhibits the protein, or the protein catalyzes a reaction of the chemical); these are merged into one entry, with the acting side (`chemical`, `protein`, or empty if neither is acting). The modes of action of pairs that are not among the associations of the network (with a combined score below 150) are left out.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `stitch_id`: the identifier of the node in STITCH: `CIDm<CID>` or `CIDs<CID>` (with the CID padded with zeros to 8 digits) for chemicals, `<taxid>.<protein id>` (e.g. `9606.ENSP00000257254`) for proteins.
- (Node) `name`: the name of the chemical (empty for proteins).
- (Node) `molecular_weight`: the molecular weight of the chemical (NaN for proteins).
- (Node) `smiles`: the structure of the chemical, as a SMILES string (empty for proteins).
- (Node) `is_chemical` (`protein_chemical_<taxid>` networks): whether the node is a chemical (otherwise it is a protein).
- (Edge) `combined_score`: the combined confidence score of the association (from 150 to 999).
- (Edge) `experimental`, `database`, `textmining`: the scores of the corresponding channels (0 if there is no evidence of that kind).
- (Edge) `similarity` (`chemical_chemical`): the score of the structural similarity of the chemicals.
- (Edge) `prediction` (`protein_chemical_<taxid>`): the score of the predictions.
- (Edge) `experimental_direct`, `experimental_transferred`, `prediction_direct`, `prediction_transferred`, `database_direct`, `database_transferred`, `textmining_direct`, `textmining_transferred` (`protein_chemical_<taxid>`): the scores of the channels from evidence on the organism itself and from evidence transferred from other organisms by orthology.
- (Edge) `action_mode`, `action_effect`, `action_actor`, `action_score` (`protein_chemical_<taxid>`): the modes of action of the association, as lists with one entry per mode (empty if none): the mode (`activation`, `binding`, `catalysis`, `expression`, `inhibition`, `pred_bind` (predicted binding), `phenotype`, `reaction`), its effect as given by STITCH (`activation`, `inhibition`, or empty), the acting side (`chemical`, `protein`, or empty), and the score of the mode of action.
- (Node) `taxon_id`, `organism` (graph, `protein_chemical_<taxid>`): the NCBI taxonomy identifier and the name of the organism.
citations: D. Szklarczyk, A. Santos, C. von Mering, L. J. Jensen, P. Bork, M. Kuhn, "STITCH 5: augmenting protein-chemical interaction networks with tissue and affinity data." Nucleic Acids Research 44, D380-D384 (2016)

datasets.name: strayer_preschool
datasets.description:
Agonistic interactions among preschool children in two groups in Waterloo (Ontario, Canada), from the ethological study of social agonism and dominance relations of F. F. Strayer and J. Strayer (1976). The data were distributed by L. C. Freeman on his network data page at the University of California, Irvine (no longer online), from which this version was obtained via the Internet Archive.

- `group1`: 17 children.
- `group2`: 19 children.

A directed edge (i, j) indicates agonistic interactions between children i and j that resulted in the submission of one of them. The direction of the edges is not documented (in such data, the row child is usually the winner of the encounter).

The networks have the following properties:

- (Edge) `weight`: the number of interactions.
citations: F. F. Strayer, J. Strayer, "An ethological analysis of social agonism and dominance relations among preschool children." Child Development 47(4), 980-989 (1976)

F. F. Strayer, J. Strayer, T. R. Chapeskie, "The perception of social power among preschool children." In D. R. Omark, F. F. Strayer, D. G. Freedman (eds.), Dominance Relations: An Ethological View of Human Conflict and Social Interaction, Garland STPM Press (1980)

datasets.name: strayer_rhesus_macaques
datasets.description:
Dominance among the 30 adult members (5 males and 25 females) of a colony of rhesus macaques (Macaca mulatta) housed at the Wisconsin Regional Primate Center in Madison, from F. F. Strayer and M. S. Cummins (1980). The monkeys were deprived of water, and observations were made of which monkey got access to a drinking fountain, during six month-long experimental periods. The data were converted into an index of consistency in linear dominance rankings over the periods, which is not clearly presented. The data were distributed by L. C. Freeman on his network data page at the University of California, Irvine (no longer online), from which this version was obtained via the Internet Archive.

A directed edge (i, j) indicates dominance of monkey i over monkey j.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the label of the monkey (numbers are males, letters are females).
- (Node) `male`: whether the monkey is male.
- (Edge) `weight`: the dominance index (integer from 1 to 6).
citations: F. F. Strayer, M. S. Cummins, "Aggressive and competitive social structures in captive monkey groups." In D. R. Omark, F. F. Strayer, D. G. Freedman (eds.), Dominance Relations: An Ethological View of Human Conflict and Social Interaction, 85-96, Garland STPM Press (1980)

datasets.name: string_ppi
datasets.description:
Networks of functional associations between the proteins of seven model organisms, from the STRING database, version 12.5. Nodes are proteins, and an undirected edge indicates a functional association between two proteins, i.e. that they contribute jointly to a biological function, which does not necessarily mean that they physically bind each other. STRING combines evidence from several channels: physical interactions from experiments, curated pathway and complex databases, co-expression, conserved genomic neighborhood, gene fusions, phylogenetic co-occurrence, and co-mention in the scientific literature (text mining), including evidence transferred from other organisms by orthology. Each channel gives a confidence score, and the channels are combined into an overall confidence score.

The organisms are human (*Homo sapiens*, `human`), mouse (*Mus musculus*, `mouse`), baker's yeast (*Saccharomyces cerevisiae*, `yeast`), the bacterium *Escherichia coli* K-12 MG1655 (`ecoli`), the fruit fly (*Drosophila melanogaster*, `fly`), the nematode *Caenorhabditis elegans* (`worm`) and the thale cress (*Arabidopsis thaliana*, `arabidopsis`). For each organism there are two networks:

- `<organism>_all`: all the associations in STRING, of any score (the lowest score in STRING is 0.15).
- `<organism>_min400`: only the associations with a combined score of at least 0.4, STRING's default threshold ("medium confidence").

All networks of an organism have the same nodes, all the proteins of the organism in STRING (proteins without associations are isolated nodes). STRING is available for over 12,000 organisms; only these seven are included here.

The entry also contains the networks of the same organisms in the earlier versions 11.0 (2019), 11.5 (2021) and 12.0 (2023) of STRING, named `<organism>_v<version>_all` and `<organism>_v<version>_min400` (e.g. `human_v11.0_all`), built in the same way; the networks without a version in their names are those of version 12.5. The sets of proteins and the scores differ between versions. Versions before 11.0 are not included.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `string_id`: the STRING identifier of the protein (the NCBI taxonomy identifier of the organism followed by the protein's identifier, e.g. `9606.ENSP00000000233`).
- (Node) `name`: the preferred name of the protein (e.g. `ARF5`).
- (Node) `size`: the length of the protein, in amino acids.
- (Node) `annotation`: a description of the protein.
- (Edge) `combined_score`: the combined confidence score of the association, multiplied by 1000 (from 150 to 999).
- (Edge) `neighborhood`, `fusion`, `cooccurence`, `coexpression`, `experimental`, `database`, `textmining`: the scores of the individual channels, multiplied by 1000 (0 if there is no evidence of that kind).
citations: D. Szklarczyk et al., "The STRING database in 2025: protein networks with directionality of regulation." Nucleic Acids Research 53, D730-D737 (2025)

D. Szklarczyk et al., "The STRING database in 2023: protein-protein association networks and functional enrichment analyses for any sequenced genome of interest." Nucleic Acids Research 51, D638-D646 (2023)

D. Szklarczyk et al., "The STRING database in 2021: customizable protein-protein networks, and functional characterization of user-uploaded gene/measurement sets." Nucleic Acids Research 49, D605-D612 (2021)

D. Szklarczyk et al., "STRING v11: protein-protein association networks with increased coverage, supporting functional discovery in genome-wide experimental datasets." Nucleic Acids Research 47, D607-D613 (2019)

datasets.name: student_cooperation
datasets.description:
Network of cooperation among 185 students of the mandatory "Computer and Network Security" course at Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, Israel, in 2012, from two different departments. Nodes are students and edges denote implicit or explicit cooperation between two students while doing their homework assignments, as inferred by M. Fire et al. from the data collected during the course. There are three types of links, and a pair of students can be connected by several edges of different types.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the anonymous identifier of the student.
- (Edge) `type`: the type of link: `Partners` (explicit cooperation: the students submitted an assignment together), `Computer` (the students submitted assignments from the same computer), or `Time` (implicit cooperation inferred from the timing of the students' activity; see Fire et al. for the precise definitions).
citations: M. Fire et al., "Predicting student exam's scores by analyzing social network data." International Conference on Active Media Technology, 584-595 (AMT 2012)

datasets.name: student_government
datasets.description:
Communication relations among the members and advisors of the Student Government of the University of Ljubljana (Slovenia), collected by V. Hlebec in May 1992 in an experiment comparing two methods of collecting network data: recall, in which respondents named the members of their egocentric networks from memory, and recognition, in which they were given a list of all members and selected those they communicate with (most often). The number of listed persons was not limited in either method. Communication flow was identified by three questions, referring to the matters of the Student Government during the six months since its formation: "Who of the members and advisors of the Student Government do you (most often) informally discuss with?", "Which members and advisors do you (most often) ask for an opinion?", and "Which members and advisors (most often) ask you for an opinion?". One of the twelve members refused to cooperate, so the networks have 11 actors. The data reflect the actors' cognition of the communication, rather than observed interactions. The data were distributed in Pajek format on the Pajek datasets page of V. Batagelj and A. Mrvar, from which this version was obtained.

- `discussion_recall`, `discussion_recognition`: informal discussion, from the respondent to the person named.
- `ask_recall`, `ask_recognition`: asking for an opinion, from the respondent to the person named.
- `asked_recall`, `asked_recognition`: being asked for an opinion; the matrices were transposed in the source, so that an edge points from the person who asks for an opinion to the respondent who reported it.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the position of the actor (prime minister, ministers 1 to 7, and advisers 1 to 3).
citations: V. Hlebec, "Recall versus recognition: Comparison of the two alternative procedures for collecting social network data." In A. Ferligoj, A. Kramberger (eds.), Developments in Statistics and Methodology, Metodološki zvezki 9, FDV, Ljubljana (1993), pp. 121-129

datasets.name: suffragettes
datasets.description:
Networks of the militant suffragette movement in the United Kingdom (1906-1914), collected by Gemma Edwards and Nick Crossley at the University of Manchester. The relational data were constructed from historical archives, including letters and speeches of suffragettes, and from secondary sources such as autobiographies and newspaper accounts (in particular, letters give dated information on who was writing to whom). Data distributed by the UCINET datasets collection (University of Manchester). Nodes are persons, named in the vertex property `name` (a few names occur more than once, for different persons). The networks are:

- `visits_1908` to `visits_1913`: co-location of 85 persons through visits in each year, with the edge property `weight` giving the number of co-occurrences.
- `blathwayt_covisitation`: co-visitation network of the same 85 persons (visits to the Blathwayt family home, Eagle House, near Bath), with `weight` the number of co-visits.
- `pankhurst_inner_circle`: pre-existing ties among 112 persons in the circle of Emmeline Pankhurst (where the two directions in the source matrix differ, the tie is included).
- `bristol_bath_militant_acts`: bipartite network of 13 suffragettes and 18 militant acts in Bristol and Bath in which they took part (the vertex property `is_act` marks the acts, which are named by their date and a description).
- `bristol_bath_militant_acts_projection`: one-mode projection of the above, with `weight` the number of shared acts.
- `bristol_bath_events`: co-attendance of 49 persons at events in Bristol and Bath.
- `arrests`: bipartite network of 1216 persons and the 398 dates and places at which they were arrested (the vertex property `is_arrest` marks the arrest events, named by their date and an abbreviated location).
- `co_arrests`: one-mode network of the same 1216 persons connected by co-arrests, with `weight` as given by the source. This matrix is not exactly the projection of `arrests` (its values, up to 563, are not documented).

The diagonal entries of the one-mode matrices (e.g. the number of visits of each person) are not included.[^ucinet]

[^ucinet]: Description obtained in part from the [UCINET datasets page](https://sites.google.com/site/ucinetsoftware/datasets/covert-networks/suffragettes).
citations: N. Crossley, G. Edwards, E. Harries, and R. Stevenson, "Covert social movement networks and the secrecy-efficiency trade off: The case of the UK suffragettes (1906-1914)." Social Networks 34(4), 634-644 (2012)
G. Edwards and N. Crossley, "Measures and meanings: Exploring the ego-net of Helen Kirkpatrick Watts, militant suffragette." Methodological Innovations Online 4(1), 37-61 (2009)
G. Edwards, "Infectious innovations? The diffusion of tactical innovation in social movement networks, the case of suffragette militancy." Social Movement Studies 13(1), 48-69 (2014)

datasets.name: swedish_criticism
datasets.description:
Co-mentions of 15 authors in Swedish literary criticism during the stylistic revolution in Swedish literature of 1881-1883, from the study of K. E. Rosengren. Rosengren recorded the sets of authors (other than the author being reviewed) that were mentioned together in the reviews published in the Swedish press during those years. Pairs mentioned together less than five times were dropped, and only those pairs whose proportion of co-mentions was more than three standard errors above its expectation were included. The data were analyzed by L. C. Freeman (1986). The data were distributed by L. C. Freeman on his network data page at the University of California, Irvine (no longer online), from which this version was obtained via the Internet Archive.

An undirected edge connects two authors that were significantly co-mentioned.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the name of the author.
citations: K. E. Rosengren, "Sociological Aspects of the Literary System." Natur och Kultur (1968)
L. C. Freeman, "Boxicity and the social context of Swedish literary criticism, 1881-1883." Journal of Social and Biological Structures 9(2), 141-149 (1986)

datasets.name: swingers
datasets.description:
Bipartite (two-mode) sexual affiliation network of swinger couples and the swinger parties they attended, from the study of A.-M. Niekamp et al. on the spread of sexually transmitted infections among swingers (heterosexuals who engage in sexual activity with partners outside their relationship). Each couple ("swing unit") is represented by a single node, and an edge connects a couple to a party it attended. There are 57 couples and 39 parties. The data were distributed as a two-mode matrix by the UCINET project. Edges are directed from couples to parties, although the direction carries no additional information.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the label of the node in the upstream matrix (numbers for couples, letters for parties).
- (Node) `is_party`: whether the node is a party (true) or a couple (false).
citations: A.-M. Niekamp et al., "A sexual affiliation network of swingers, heterosexuals practicing risk behaviours that potentiate the spread of sexually transmitted infections: A two-mode approach." Social Networks 35(2), 223-236 (2013)

datasets.name: swissrailnet
datasets.description:
Network representations of the Swiss railway network, built by M. Sterchi, E. Raubach and L. Hilfiker from the open data of Swiss public transport (opentransportdata.swiss): the timetable of all scheduled stops on Wednesday, March 5, 2025 ("Actual Data"), the list of service points valid on that day, and the numbers of passengers boarding and alighting at each station. The authors define four representations; in all of them, the nodes are the same 1,626 train stations (including a few stations in Italy and Germany operated by Swiss companies), and they differ in the definition of the edges:

- `space_of_changes`: a directed edge from station $i$ to station $j$ if some train serves $j$ after $i$ on the same trip, so that one can travel from $i$ to $j$ without changing trains. The edges are weighted by the number of such connections on that day and their average duration.
- `space_of_stops`: a directed edge from station $i$ to station $j$ if some train stops at $j$ immediately after $i$ (a non-stop connection), with the same weights.
- `space_of_stations`: an undirected edge between geographically adjacent stations, i.e. stations next to each other along the railway tracks. It was derived from the non-stop connections and validated manually: 11 edges, e.g. of long tunnels and high-speed lines served without stop, were added, and 11 edges between stations that are not adjacent were removed.
- `space_of_stations_raw`: the same as `space_of_stations`, but also including the 11 edges that were removed manually, which the authors published in a separate file, marked by an edge property.
- `temporal`: every individual connection of the day, as in `space_of_changes` but without aggregation: a directed edge from $i$ to $j$ for each train trip that serves $j$ after $i$, with the time of departure from $i$ and the duration of the journey. There are many parallel edges.

The `temporal` network also has 83 self-loops, the connections of trips that return to their station (at two stations, presumably on loop lines), which do not appear in the aggregated networks. Times are rounded to the minute; connections taking less than a minute have a duration of 0. The dataset has two versions on figshare (July and October 2025), which contain the same nodes and edges; the second adds the node property `traffic_valid`, and its files are used here.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the name of the station.
- (Node) `bpuic`: its official number (Swiss/European station code).
- (Node) `canton` and `municipality`: where it is located (empty for the stations abroad).
- (Node) `company`: the company responsible for it.
- (Node) `latitude`, `longitude` and `elevation` (m): its position.
- (Node) `avg_daily_traffic`, `avg_daily_traffic_weekdays` and `avg_daily_traffic_weekends`: the average daily numbers of railway passengers boarding and alighting at the station (over all days, Monday to Friday, and weekends and public holidays; NaN where not available; the value 49 indicates an unreliable measurement).
- (Node) `traffic_valid`: whether these numbers are available and reliable.
- (Edge) `num_connections` (`space_of_changes` and `space_of_stops`): the number of trains per day connecting the two stations.
- (Edge) `avg_duration` (`space_of_changes` and `space_of_stops`): the average duration of the connection (minutes).
- (Edge) `distance_geodesic` (`space_of_stations` and `space_of_stations_raw`): the geodesic distance between the two stations (km).
- (Edge) `distance_exact` (`space_of_stations` and `space_of_stations_raw`): the distance along the tracks (km), available only for the lines of the Swiss Federal Railways (NaN otherwise).
- (Edge) `manually_added` (`space_of_stations` and `space_of_stations_raw`): whether the edge was added manually.
- (Edge) `manually_removed` (`space_of_stations_raw`): whether the edge was removed manually (and is therefore absent from `space_of_stations`).
- (Edge) `time` (`temporal`): the departure time (Unix time; the times run from midnight of March 5, 2025, Central European Time, into the morning of March 6).
- (Edge) `start` (`temporal`): the departure time in minutes after midnight of March 5, as given in the data.
- (Edge) `duration` (`temporal`): the duration of the connection (minutes).

Only the `space_of_stations` and `space_of_stations_raw` networks are laid out as spatial networks (without the partition of the stochastic block model).
citations: M. Sterchi, E. Raubach, L. Hilfiker, "SwissRailNet: Four representations of a spatially embedded railway network dataset." Data in Brief 63, 112266 (2025)
M. Sterchi, E. Raubach, L. Hilfiker, "Four representations of the Swiss railway network." figshare, dataset, version 2 (2025)

datasets.name: teenage_friends
datasets.description:
Friendship networks among the pupils of the older cohort of a secondary school in Glasgow (Scotland), from the Teenage Friends and Lifestyle Study, which aimed to identify how attitudes towards smoking and smoking behaviour change over early to mid adolescence. The study was carried out by L. Michell and P. West of the MRC Medical Sociology Unit, University of Glasgow. The pupils were followed over their second, third and fourth year at the school, from February 1995 (when they were aged 13) to January 1997, at three measurement points (`t1` to `t3`). A total of 160 pupils were part of the cohort, of which 129 were present at all three time points. Pupils could name up to six friends; at the first time point, a second questionnaire allowed up to six more nominations, which were censored in this release for consistency over time. The school was representative of others in the region in terms of social class composition. The data were distributed by T. Snijders with the SIENA software (release of July 2026). The frequently used "s50" excerpt of 50 girls is a subset of an earlier release of these data.

A directed edge (i, j) indicates that pupil i named pupil j as a friend.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the pupil identifier.
- (Node) `present`: whether the pupil was part of the cohort at this time point.
- (Node) `sex` (1: boy, 2: girl).
- (Node) `age`: the age in years on 1 January 1995.
- (Node) `alcohol`: alcohol consumption (1: non, 2: once or twice a year, 3: once a month, 4: once a week, 5: more than once a week).
- (Node) `tobacco`: tobacco use (1: non, 2: occasional, 3: regular, i.e. more than once per week).
- (Node) `cannabis`: cannabis use (1: non, 2: tried once, 3: occasional, 4: regular).
- (Node) `money`: pocket money per month in British pounds.
- (Node) `romantic`: whether the pupil had a romantic relation (1: no, 2: yes).
- (Node) `smoking_at_home`, `parent_smoking` and `sibling_smoking`: smoking at home, by at least one parent and by at least one sibling (1: no, 2: yes; first non-missing value over the three time points).
- (Node) `dist_school`: the distance between the pupil's home and the school in kilometers.
- (Node) `selection129`: whether the pupil is one of the 129 present at all time points.
- (Node) `selection50`: whether the pupil is one of the 50 girls of the "s50" excerpt. The variables `alcohol`, `tobacco`, `cannabis`, `money`, `romantic` and `dist_school` refer to the time point of the network. Missing values are -1 (or NaN for `money`, `age` and `dist_school`).
- (Edge) `relation`: the type of friendship (1: best friend, 2: just a friend).
citations: L. Michell, A. Amos, "Girls, pecking order and smoking." Social Science & Medicine 44(12), 1861-1869 (1997)
M. Pearson, L. Michell, "Smoke Rings: social network analysis of friendship groups, smoking and drug-taking." Drugs: Education, Prevention and Policy 7(1), 21-37 (2000)
C. Steglich, T. A. B. Snijders, M. Pearson, "Dynamic networks and behavior: Separating selection from influence." Sociological Methodology 40(1), 329-393 (2010)

datasets.name: telegram_channels_graph
datasets.description:
Networks of public Telegram channels, from the dataset of Shapovalova and Sofiienko, who collected 264,777 channels and their publications through the Telegram API. Each node is a channel, and there are two networks:

- `forwards`: a directed edge from channel u to channel v means that publications of u were forwarded to v (v republished posts of u), with the number of forwarded publications as weight (2,207,614 edges, including 21,140 self-loops).
- `mentions`: a directed edge from channel u to channel v means that publications of u mention v through a URL (a link to the channel or to one of its posts), with the number of mentions as weight (8,046,017 edges). The file contains repeated pairs of channels (933,000 of the edges duplicate a pair, with their own counts), which are kept as multiple edges, as they are.

The direction follows the columns `FromId` and `ToId` of the files (in `forwards`, e.g., the news agency RIA Novosti is the source of 133,600 forwarded publications, and the target of 45).

Both networks contain all channels of the dataset. For about half of them (133,603), the authors also give the 90th percentile of the views and of the forwards of their publications, and their main language (determined with fastText), at the time of a snapshot. A few channels (947) appear twice in the file of channels, with two main languages (ties), which are both kept. The mentions are made by 13,013 channels that are not in the file of channels; they are included as nodes without attributes (`has_record` false). The time range of the data is not stated; the channels were created from September 2015 to October 2024, and the snapshots were taken from 2015 to October 2024.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `channel_id`: the id of the channel on Telegram.
- (Node) `has_record`: whether the channel is in the file of channels.
- (Node) `name`: its username (its address is `https://t.me/<name>`; empty for some).
- (Node) `title`.
- (Node) `created`: the time of creation of the channel (Unix time).
- (Node) `snapshot`: the time of the snapshot of the statistics (Unix time; -1 if there are none).
- (Node) `top_lang`: the ISO code of the main language of its publications (two codes separated by a comma for ties; empty if unknown).
- (Node) `p90_views` and `p90_forwards`: the 90th percentiles of the numbers of views and forwards of its publications at the time of the snapshot (NaN if unknown).
- (Edge) `count`: the number of forwarded publications (`forwards`) or of mentions (`mentions`).
citations: S. Shapovalova, A. Sofiienko, "Telegram channels graph dataset." Zenodo (2025)

datasets.name: telegram_forwards
datasets.description:
Networks of Telegram channels and groups from the Pushshift Telegram dataset of Baumgartner, Zannettou, Squire and Blackburn, who collected all messages (317 million, from 2015 to 2019) of 27,801 public channels and groups (supergroups), which they found by a snowball crawl starting from about 250 channels on politics, cryptocurrencies and other topics, through the channels referenced in their messages (mostly right-wing and cryptocurrency channels). The data are as returned by the Telegram API (Telethon). The entry contains two networks:

- `forwards`: a directed edge from channel u to channel v means that messages of u were forwarded to v (v republished messages first posted in u), weighted by the number of forwarded messages. Besides the crawled channels, the nodes include all channels whose messages were forwarded to them. Forwards of messages of individual users (and of hidden ones, given only by name) are left out.
- `posts`: a bipartite network of users and channels, where an edge connects a user to a channel (or group) in which they posted messages, weighted by the number of messages. Messages posted by the channels themselves (in broadcast channels, without user) are left out, and so are service messages (e.g. users joining). All crawled channels are included, also those without messages of users.

In `posts`, the users have the information of their profiles (names, usernames, phone numbers and flags) from the file of the 2.2 million accounts of the dataset, retrieved in 2019; Telegram users have no biographies in these data, and most phone numbers are hidden (about 13,000 accounts show one). Left out are the profile photos and the online status of the users, and the contents of the messages, replies and mentions.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `channel_id` (channels): the id of the channel on Telegram.
- (Node) `crawled` (channels): whether the channel is one of the crawled ones (otherwise only a source of forwarded messages).
- (Node) `title`, `username`, `created` (channels): its title, its username (its address is `https://t.me/<username>`) and its time of creation (Unix time), known for the crawled channels and for the channels linked to them (empty or -1 otherwise).
- (Node) `broadcast` (channels): whether it is a broadcast channel (1), a group (0) or unknown (-1).
- (Node) `participants_count` (channels): the number of members when it was crawled (-1 if unknown).
- (Node) `about` (channels): its description (crawled channels only).
- (Node) `retrieved` (channels): the time when its information was retrieved (Unix time; -1 for channels not crawled).
- (Node) `is_user` (`posts`): whether the node is a user (otherwise a channel).
- (Node) `user_id` (`posts`): the id of the user on Telegram (-1 for channels).
- (Node) `has_profile` (`posts`): whether the user is in the file of accounts.
- (Node) `first_name`, `last_name` (`posts`): the display name of the user.
- (Node) `phone` (`posts`): the phone number of the user, if visible (international format without "+").
- (Node) `bot`, `deleted`, `verified`, `scam`, `restricted` (`posts`): the flags of the account (false for channels).
- (Node) `username`, `retrieved` (users, in `posts`): the username of the account (its address is `https://t.me/<username>`) and the time when the profile was retrieved (Unix time). The other channel properties are empty or -1 for users.
- (Edge) `count`: the number of forwarded messages (`forwards`) or of posted messages (`posts`).
- (Edge) `first_time` and `last_time`: the times of the first and of the last of these messages (Unix time; in `forwards`, the times when they were forwarded).
citations: J. Baumgartner, S. Zannettou, M. Squire, J. Blackburn, "The Pushshift Telegram Dataset." Proceedings of the International AAAI Conference on Web and Social Media 14, 840-847 (2020)

datasets.name: tennis_atp
datasets.description:
Networks of the men's singles tennis matches of the Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP), built by U. Michieli from the match records compiled by J. Sackmann (https://github.com/JeffSackmann/tennis_atp). Nodes are players.

- `wins`: matches of the main ATP tour from 1968 to the end of August 2017. A directed edge $i\to j$ goes from a losing player $i$ to a winning player $j$, with `weight` equal to the number of times $j$ won against $i$ (the weights add up to 151,734 matches).
- `points`: the same matches and players as `wins`, with ATP ranking points as weights. A directed edge is present in both directions between any two players that met, and, according to the source documentation, the weights are "the respective ATP points awarded" to the two players (the loser of a match also receives points); the weight of $i\to j$ is thus presumably the total of points earned by $j$ in their matches against $i$.
- `extended`: an undirected and unweighted network, where an edge connects two players who played at least one match against each other between 1968 and the end of March 2018, including also the Davis Cup, and the Challenger and Futures tournaments from 1991 onwards (which are not included in the other two networks).

An undirected and unweighted version of `wins` (where an edge connects two players who met) is also distributed upstream; it is not included here, as it is equivalent to `wins` with the edge directions and weights ignored.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the player's name, as "Surname I." (`wins`, `points`) or "Firstname Surname" (`extended`).
- (Edge) `weight`: the number of wins (`wins`) or the ATP points (`points`).
citations: U. Michieli, "Complex network analysis of men single ATP tennis matches." arXiv:1804.08138 (2018)

datasets.name: terrorist_attacks
datasets.description:
Networks of terrorist attacks from the Profiles in Terror (PIT) knowledge base of the MIND Lab at the University of Maryland, as distributed by the LINQS group (Zhao, Sen and Getoor) as a benchmark for relational (collective) classification. PIT was a semantic knowledge base of terrorism intelligence (attacks, terrorists and terrorist organizations) extracted from sources such as news media reports. The dataset contains 1293 terrorist attacks, each classified into one of six types.

Nodes are attacks, and there are two networks:

- `colocation`: an edge connects two attacks that occurred in the same geographical location.
- `colocation_same_org`: an edge connects two attacks that occurred in the same location and were carried out by the same organization (a subset of the edges of `colocation`).

The networks have the following vertex properties: `name`, the identifier of the attack in PIT (for most attacks, the name of the organization responsible, or "Unknown", followed by the date in the format YYYYMMDD; the remaining identifiers are URLs of PIT documents); `attack_type`, the class of the attack (arson, bombing, kidnapping, NBCR attack, i.e. nuclear, biological, chemical or radiological, weapon attack, or other attack); and `features`, a vector of 106 binary attributes of the attack (according to the source, including information such as the year of the attack and keywords from its description; their meanings are not given in the data). The same two networks, restricted to the attacks with at least one edge, are also distributed by the UCINET datasets collection as "Linux Terrorists".
citations: B. Zhao, P. Sen, and L. Getoor, "Event classification and relationship labeling in affiliation networks." Proceedings of the Workshop on Statistical Network Analysis (SNA) at the 23rd International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML) (2006)

datasets.name: terrorists_911
datasets.description:
Network of the 19 hijackers of the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks in the United States and of other individuals associated with them, compiled by V. Krebs from public information released in newspapers after the attacks. Nodes are individuals and an undirected edge indicates a known association between two individuals (e.g. having lived or trained together, or having met or communicated). The network has 62 nodes. This version of the data was distributed by A. Clauset.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `id`: the numerical identifier of the individual in the upstream data.
- (Node) `name`: the name of the individual.
- (Node) `group`: the flight the individual was aboard on September 11, 2001, for the hijackers (one value from 0 to 3 for each of the four hijacked flights), or 4 for individuals who were not aboard any of the flights. The correspondence between the values 0 to 3 and the flights is not documented in the upstream data.
citations: V. Krebs, "Mapping networks of terrorist cells." Connections 24, 43-52 (2002).

datasets.name: tflink
datasets.description:
Directed networks of the regulation of genes by transcription factors (TFs) in seven model organisms, from TFLink, which integrates the TF-target gene interactions of about 10 databases (e.g. ORegAnno, TRRUST, ReMap, GTRD, ChIP-Atlas, HTRIdb, PAZAR, TFe, Yeastract, modERN, REDfly, ...), from small-scale experiments (e.g. reporter assays, electrophoretic mobility shift assays, curated from the literature) and large-scale experiments (mostly ChIP-seq). An edge goes from a TF to a target gene whose expression it regulates, or to whose regulatory region it binds. The data are those of version 1.0 (April 2022) of TFLink.

There is one network per organism, with all its interactions (small and large scale): `human` (*Homo sapiens*), `mouse` (*Mus musculus*), `rat` (*Rattus norvegicus*), `zebrafish` (*Danio rerio*), `fly` (*Drosophila melanogaster*), `worm` (*Caenorhabditis elegans*) and `yeast` (*Saccharomyces cerevisiae*). The small-scale and large-scale subsets that TFLink also provides are those of the edges with `small_scale` true or false. The binding sites of the TFs are not included.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `uniprot`: the UniProt accession of the TF or target gene product.
- (Node) `gene_id`: the NCBI Gene identifier of the gene (-1 if not given).
- (Node) `name`: the name of the gene.
- (Node) `tflink_orthologs`: the UniProt accessions of the orthologs of the node in the other organisms of TFLink, prefixed by the organism (e.g. `Hs:Q15049`), separated by `;` (empty if none).
- (Node) `other_orthologs`: the same, for the orthologs that are not in TFLink.
- (Edge) `detection_method`: the methods of detection of the interaction, separated by `;`.
- (Edge) `pubmed_ids`: the PubMed identifiers of the publications of the interaction, separated by `;`.
- (Edge) `source_databases`: the databases from which the interaction comes, separated by `;`.
- (Edge) `small_scale`: whether the interaction is supported by small-scale experiments.
citations: O. Liska, B. Bohár, A. Hidas, T. Korcsmáros, B. Papp, D. Fazekas, E. Ari, "TFLink: an integrated gateway to access transcription factor-target gene interactions for multiple species." Database 2022, baac083 (2022)

datasets.name: tgbl_comment
datasets.description:
A temporal network of replies between the users of Reddit from 2005 to 2010, from the `tgbl-comment` dataset of the Temporal Graph Benchmark (TGB), extracted from the Reddit data of Nadiri and Takes (2022), based on the Pushshift collection of Reddit comments. Each node is a user, and each timestamped directed edge is a comment of a user in reply to a post or comment of another user (or of the same user: there are self-loops). The users are identified only by indices (the anonymized author identifiers of the source data), and the subreddits only by indices in the order of their first appearance (their names are not given).

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `user_id`: the identifier of the user in the source data.
- (Edge) `time`: the time of the comment, in Unix time.
- (Edge) `subreddit`: the index of the subreddit of the comment.
- (Edge) `num_words`: the number of words of the comment.
- (Edge) `score`: the score of the comment (upvotes minus downvotes).
citations: S. Huang, F. Poursafaei, J. Danovitch, M. Fey, W. Hu, E. Rossi, J. Leskovec, M. Bronstein, G. Rabusseau, R. Rabbany, "Temporal Graph Benchmark for Machine Learning on Temporal Graphs." Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36 (Datasets and Benchmarks Track) (2023)
A. Nadiri, F. W. Takes, "A large-scale temporal analysis of user lifespan durability on the Reddit social media platform." Companion Proceedings of the Web Conference 2022, 677-685 (2022)

datasets.name: tgbn_genre
datasets.description:
A temporal bipartite network of 992 users of the music website Last.fm and the music genres of the songs they listened to, from February 2005 to June 2009, from the `tgbn-genre` dataset of the Temporal Graph Benchmark (TGB). TGB built it by matching the songs of the Last.fm listening histories of about 1,000 users (the "Last.fm 1K" data collected by Ò. Celma) with the genre tags of the songs in the Million Song Dataset. Each listen of a song gives a timestamped edge from the user to each genre of the song, weighted by the weight of the genre for the song; TGB kept only the genres with a weight of at least 10% for a song, and that occur at least a thousand times, and cleaned the genre names of typos. A listen may thus give several edges, and repeated edges.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `is_genre`: whether the node is a genre (otherwise a user).
- (Node) `name`: the identifier of the user (e.g. `user_000871`) or the name of the genre (e.g. `80s`).
- (Edge) `time`: the time of the listen, in Unix time.
- (Edge) `weight`: the weight of the genre for the song listened to (between 0 and 1).
citations: S. Huang, F. Poursafaei, J. Danovitch, M. Fey, W. Hu, E. Rossi, J. Leskovec, M. Bronstein, G. Rabusseau, R. Rabbany, "Temporal Graph Benchmark for Machine Learning on Temporal Graphs." Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36 (Datasets and Benchmarks Track) (2023)
Ò. Celma, "Music Recommendation and Discovery in the Long Tail." Springer (2010)
T. Bertin-Mahieux, D. P. W. Ellis, B. Whitman, P. Lamere, "The Million Song Dataset." Proceedings of the 12th International Society for Music Information Retrieval Conference (ISMIR), 591-596 (2011)

datasets.name: tgbn_reddit
datasets.description:
A temporal bipartite network of the users of Reddit and the subreddits they posted in, from January 2008 to December 2010, from the `tgbn-reddit` dataset of the Temporal Graph Benchmark (TGB), extracted from the Reddit data of Nadiri and Takes (2022), based on the Pushshift collection of Reddit posts and comments (the TGB paper states that the data span 2005 to 2019, but the times of the data span 2008 to 2010). Each timestamped edge from a user to a subreddit is a post (or comment) of the user in the subreddit, with its number of words and its score. The users are identified only by indices (the anonymized author identifiers of the source data).

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `is_subreddit`: whether the node is a subreddit (otherwise a user).
- (Node) `name`: the name of the subreddit (empty for users).
- (Node) `user_id`: the identifier of the user in the source data (-1 for subreddits).
- (Edge) `time`: the time of the post, in Unix time.
- (Edge) `num_words`: the number of words of the post.
- (Edge) `score`: the score of the post (upvotes minus downvotes).
citations: S. Huang, F. Poursafaei, J. Danovitch, M. Fey, W. Hu, E. Rossi, J. Leskovec, M. Bronstein, G. Rabusseau, R. Rabbany, "Temporal Graph Benchmark for Machine Learning on Temporal Graphs." Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36 (Datasets and Benchmarks Track) (2023)
A. Nadiri, F. W. Takes, "A large-scale temporal analysis of user lifespan durability on the Reddit social media platform." Companion Proceedings of the Web Conference 2022, 677-685 (2022)

datasets.name: tgbn_token
datasets.description:
A temporal bipartite network of Ethereum addresses ("users") and the ERC20 tokens they sent or received, from April 2016 to June 2018, from the `tgbn-token` dataset of the Temporal Graph Benchmark (TGB), extracted from the token transaction data of Shamsi et al. (Chartalist). For a selection of users, each transfer of a token from or to one of them gives a timestamped edge from the user to the token, with the amount transferred, and whether the user sent or received it (a transfer between two selected users gives two edges). Transfers of a zero amount were removed by TGB. The tokens are identified by the addresses of their contracts.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `is_token`: whether the node is a token (otherwise a user).
- (Node) `address`: the Ethereum address of the user, or of the contract of the token.
- (Edge) `time`: the time of the transfer, in Unix time.
- (Edge) `value`: the amount of the token transferred, as given by the data (in the smallest units of the token).
- (Edge) `sender`: whether the user sent the amount (otherwise received it).
citations: S. Huang, F. Poursafaei, J. Danovitch, M. Fey, W. Hu, E. Rossi, J. Leskovec, M. Bronstein, G. Rabusseau, R. Rabbany, "Temporal Graph Benchmark for Machine Learning on Temporal Graphs." Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36 (Datasets and Benchmarks Track) (2023)

K. Shamsi, F. Victor, M. Kantarcioglu, Y. R. Gel, C. G. Akcora, "Chartalist: Labeled Graph Datasets for UTXO and Account-based Blockchains." Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 35 (Datasets and Benchmarks Track) (2022)

datasets.name: tgbn_trade
datasets.description:
Yearly directed networks of the international trade in agricultural products between the nations of the United Nations from 1986 to 2016, from the `tgbn-trade` dataset of the Temporal Graph Benchmark (TGB), based on the data of MacDonald et al. (2015), compiled from FAOSTAT. Each node is a nation, and an edge from nation A to nation B in a year means that A traded agricultural products with B in that year (the edges of all years form a single network, with the year as an edge property). The weight of an edge is the share of the trade of A that goes to B in that year, i.e. the trade values (the sum over all agricultural products) normalized by TGB so that the weights of the edges from each nation in each year sum to one; the trade values themselves are not included in the data.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the name of the nation.
- (Edge) `year`: the year of the trade.
- (Edge) `share`: the share of the trade of the source nation with the target nation in that year.
citations: S. Huang, F. Poursafaei, J. Danovitch, M. Fey, W. Hu, E. Rossi, J. Leskovec, M. Bronstein, G. Rabusseau, R. Rabbany, "Temporal Graph Benchmark for Machine Learning on Temporal Graphs." Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36 (Datasets and Benchmarks Track) (2023)

G. K. MacDonald, K. A. Brauman, S. Sun, K. M. Carlson, E. S. Cassidy, J. S. Gerber, P. C. West, "Rethinking Agricultural Trade Relationships in an Era of Globalization." BioScience 65(3), 275-289 (2015)

datasets.name: thgl_forum
datasets.description:
A temporal heterogeneous network of the comments posted on Reddit in January 2014, from the `thgl-forum` dataset of the Temporal Graph Benchmark (TGB 2.0), extracted from the Reddit data of Nadiri and Takes (2022), based on the Pushshift collection of Reddit comments. The nodes are users and subreddits, and each comment gives two timestamped directed edges: one from its author to the user it replies to (`reply`), and one from its author to the subreddit it is posted in (`post`), both with the number of words and the score of the comment. Only the users and subreddits with at least 100 edges were kept by TGB. The users and subreddits are anonymized (they are identified only by indices).

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `is_subreddit`: whether the node is a subreddit (otherwise a user).
- (Edge) `relation`: `reply` (from a user to the user replied to) or `post` (from a user to a subreddit).
- (Edge) `time`: the time of the comment, in Unix time.
- (Edge) `num_words`: the number of words of the comment.
- (Edge) `score`: the score of the comment (upvotes minus downvotes).
citations: J. Gastinger, S. Huang, M. Galkin, E. Loghmani, A. Parviz, F. Poursafaei, J. Danovitch, E. Rossi, I. Koutis, H. Stuckenschmidt, R. Rabbany, G. Rabusseau, "TGB 2.0: A Benchmark for Learning on Temporal Knowledge Graphs and Heterogeneous Graphs." Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37 (Datasets and Benchmarks Track) (2024)
A. Nadiri, F. W. Takes, "A large-scale temporal analysis of user lifespan durability on the Reddit social media platform." Companion Proceedings of the Web Conference 2022, 677-685 (2022)

datasets.name: thgl_github
datasets.description:
Temporal heterogeneous networks of the activity on GitHub, from the `thgl-github` and `thgl-software` datasets of the Temporal Graph Benchmark (TGB 2.0), built from the public event stream of GitHub collected by GH Archive. The nodes are users, repositories, issues and pull requests, anonymized by TGB (they are identified only by indices). Each timestamped directed edge is an event of one of 14 kinds: a user opens, closes or reopens an issue or a pull request (with a corresponding edge from the issue or pull request to its repository), a user is added as a member of a repository, or a repository is forked from another one (the edge goes from the new fork to the forked repository). The comments on issues and pull requests, which TGB extracted as well, were removed by TGB since they rarely interact more than once. The networks are:

- `march_2024` (`thgl-github`): the activity of March 2024, keeping only the nodes with more than two edges;
- `january_2024` (`thgl-software`): the activity of January 2024, keeping only the nodes with at least 10 edges.

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `kind`: the kind of the node: `user`, `repository`, `issue` or `pull_request`.
- (Edge) `relation`: the kind of event: `user_opened_issue`, `user_closed_issue`, `user_reopened_issue`, `issue_opened_in_repository`, `issue_closed_in_repository`, `issue_reopened_in_repository`, `user_opened_pull_request`, `user_closed_pull_request`, `user_reopened_pull_request`, `pull_request_opened_in_repository`, `pull_request_closed_in_repository`, `pull_request_reopened_in_repository`, `user_added_as_member` or `forked_from`.
- (Edge) `time`: the time of the event, in Unix time, as given by TGB. The times appear to be shifted by the offset of the US Eastern time zone (4 or 5 hours later than the actual times of the events, which GH Archive gives in UTC): those of `march_2024` span from 2024-03-01 05:00 to 2024-04-01 03:59 UTC, and those of `january_2024` from 2024-01-01 05:01 to 2024-02-01 04:59 UTC.
citations: J. Gastinger, S. Huang, M. Galkin, E. Loghmani, A. Parviz, F. Poursafaei, J. Danovitch, E. Rossi, I. Koutis, H. Stuckenschmidt, R. Rabbany, G. Rabusseau, "TGB 2.0: A Benchmark for Learning on Temporal Knowledge Graphs and Heterogeneous Graphs." Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37 (Datasets and Benchmarks Track) (2024)

datasets.name: thgl_myket
datasets.description:
A temporal bipartite network of the users of the Myket Android app market (an Iranian app store) and the apps they installed or updated, from June 2020 to January 2021, from the `thgl-myket` dataset of the Temporal Graph Benchmark (TGB 2.0), provided by the Myket Corporation. Each timestamped directed edge from a user to an app is an installation of the app (for the first time) or an update of it. The users and apps are anonymized (they are identified only by indices). A smaller, downsampled version of the data was published earlier by Loghmani and Fazli (2023); this one has all the data.

The network has the following properties:

- (Node) `is_app`: whether the node is an app (otherwise a user).
- (Edge) `update`: whether the event is an update of the app (otherwise a first installation).
- (Edge) `time`: the time of the event, in Unix time, as given by TGB (the times span from 2020-06-18 03:55 to 2021-01-01 04:59 UTC, so that they may be shifted by the offset of a time zone).
citations: J. Gastinger, S. Huang, M. Galkin, E. Loghmani, A. Parviz, F. Poursafaei, J. Danovitch, E. Rossi, I. Koutis, H. Stuckenschmidt, R. Rabbany, G. Rabusseau, "TGB 2.0: A Benchmark for Learning on Temporal Knowledge Graphs and Heterogeneous Graphs." Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37 (Datasets and Benchmarks Track) (2024)
E. Loghmani, M. Fazli, "Effect of Choosing Loss Function when Using T-batching for Representation Learning on Dynamic Networks." arXiv:2308.06862 (2023)

datasets.name: thurman_office
datasets.description:
Relations among 15 employees of the overseas office of a large international corporation, observed by B. Thurman during 16 months, in which two major disputes erupted in this subgroup. Thurman analyzed the outcome of the disputes in terms of the network of formal and informal associations among those involved. The data were distributed in UCINET format (from the UCINET data collection of S. P. Borgatti, M. G. Everett and L. C. Freeman) on the Pajek datasets page of V. Batagelj and A. Mrvar, from which this version was obtained.

- `formal`: the formal organizational chart (THURA), as directed edges between employees (from the row to the column of the source matrix). The direction is not documented, but the edges appear to go from a superior to a subordinate (e.g. the president has an edge to every other employee).
- `multiplex`: the employees linked by multiplex (informal) ties (THURM).

The networks have the following properties:

- (Node) `name`: the (pseudonymous) name or position of the employee.
citations: B. Thurman, "In the office: Networks and coalitions." Social Networks 2(1), 47-63 (1979)
S. P. Borgatti, M. G. Everett, L. C. Freeman, "UCINET for Windows: Software for Social Network Analysis." Analytic Technologies, Harvard, MA (2002)

datasets.name: tkgl_icews
datasets.description:
A temporal network of political events between socio-political actors (e.g. governments, politicians, organizations, or citizens of a country) worldwide, from January 1995 to December 2022, from the `tkgl-icews` dataset of the Temporal Graph Benchmark (TGB 2.0), based on the Integrated Crisis Early Warning System (ICEWS) coded event data. ICEWS codes events automatically from news stories with the CAMEO taxonomy of event types. Each node is an actor, and each directed edge from actor A to actor B is an event of one of the CAMEO types (e.g. A makes a statement to, consults, accuses, or attacks B), with its date. The events whose source or target is missing were removed by TGB. The actors are anonymized in the data (they are identified only by indices).

The network has the following properties:

- (Edge) `relation`: the CAMEO code of the type of the event (e.g. `051`, "praise or endorse", or `173`, "arrest, detain, or charge with legal action"), see the CAMEO codebook.
- (Edge) `time`: the date of the event, in Unix time (of midnight in the US Eastern time zone, as given).
citations: J. Gastinger, S. Huang, M. Galkin, E. Loghmani, A. Parviz, F. Poursafaei, J. Danovitch, E. Rossi, I. Koutis, H. Stuckenschmidt, R. Rabbany, G. Rabusseau, "TGB 2.0: A Benchmark for Learning on Temporal Knowledge Graphs and Heterogeneous Graphs." Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37 (Datasets and Benchmarks Track) (2024)
E. Boschee, J. Lautenschlager, S. O'Brien, S. Shellman, J. Starz, M. Ward, "ICEWS Coded Event Data." Harvard Dataverse (2015)

datasets.name: tkgl_smallpedia
datasets.description:
A temporal knowledge graph extracted from Wikidata, from the `tkgl-smallpedia` dataset of the Temporal Graph Benchmark (TGB 2.0): the statements between the Wikidata entities with identifiers below one million (i.e. Q1 to Q999999) that are paired with Wikipedia pages. Each node is an entity of Wikidata, and a directed edge from entity A to entity B is a statement (A, relation, B), with a Wikidata property as relation (e.g. `P166`, "award received", or `P54`, "member of sports team"). Pairs of entities may be connected by several edges.
